title: 8020: faith
content: A constant outlook of trust towards God, whereby human beings abandon all reliance on their own efforts and put their full confidence in him, his word and his promises.

resource.label: 8028: faith, as a body of beliefs

title: 8021: faith, nature of
content:
Confidence in and commitment to God and Jesus Christ. These attitudes remain sure even though the objects of faith are unseen. True faith is seen in obedient action, love and continuing good works.

The object of faith

God as the object of faith

HEB 11:6 See also PSA 25:1–25:2, PSA 26:1; PRO 29:25; 1PE 1:21

Jesus Christ as the object of faith

JHN 14:1 See also JHN 3:16, JHN 3:18, JHN 3:36, JHN 6:68–6:69

False objects of faith

Human resources: PSA 20:7; ; HOS 10:13; PSA 118:9 other people; ; PRO 28:26 self; ; ISA 42:17 idols

Faith is personal trust in God

2SA 22:31 See also PSA 18:2–18:6, PSA 27:13–27:14; 1PE 2:23

True faith cannot be second-hand

2TI 1:5 See also JHN 4:42

title: 8022: faith, as basis of salvation
content:
Both in the OT and in the NT faith is the only basis of salvation. Faith is the means by which God's grace in Christ, and with him the blessings of salvation, is received. Paul's doctrine of justification by faith emphasises the centrality of faith in the Christian life.

Salvation by faith in the OT

HAB 2:4

The faith of Abraham and other individuals

GEN 15:6 See also ROM 4:9–4:16 Abraham, the father of those righteous by faith; HEB 11:4 Abel; HEB 11:5 Enoch; HEB 11:7 Noah

Salvation by faith in the NT

ROM 1:16–1:17 See also 1CO 1:21; PHP 3:8–3:9

Salvation through faith alone

EPH 2:8–2:9 See also ROM 3:27–3:28, ROM 4:1–4:8; PSA 32:1–32:2; ROM 9:30–9:32; GAL 3:10–3:14; DEU 27:26

Salvation is by faith in Jesus Christ

JHN 3:14–3:16 Being “lifted up” is a reference to Jesus Christ's death on the cross; ROM 10:9–10:10 The necessity of outward confession, as evidence of personal faith in Jesus Christ. See also JHN 8:24; ACT 8:37, ACT 13:38–13:39; ROM 3:21–3:26, ROM 4:24; 2CO 4:13–4:14; GAL 3:22

Salvation is for all who believe

ROM 10:4 Jesus Christ is the “end of the law”, in the sense that he brings it to its goal and fulfilment, and accomplishes its intentions. See also ACT 15:7–15:9; ROM 3:29–3:30

title: 8023: faith, necessity of
content:
A fundamental duty for all people and the necessary response to God's self-revelation. The only channel through which God's blessings may be received, and the only means by which life may be made meaningful, in relationship with God.

In the NT

content:

title: 8025: faith, origins of
content:
Faith is a gift from God himself and is not to be seen as the result of human striving or achievement. Faith is inspired by the word and works of God.

title: 8028: faith, as a body of beliefs
content:

title: 8030: trust
content: Reliance on and confidence in a person. Scripture affirms the total trustworthiness of God, especially in relation to his promises to his people. Christian faith is, essentially, trust in the person and character of God. While Scripture insists that believers should be able to trust one another, it also provides examples of false or misplaced trust.

title: 8031: trust, importance of
content:

title: 8102: abiding in Christ
content:
The NT stresses the need for believers to remain in Christ. The reality of this close personal relationship with Jesus Christ is expressed in obedience to his word and is essential to effective discipleship.

Jesus Christ tells his disciples to abide in him

JHN 15:4–15:9 See also MAT 24:10–24:13; LUK 9:62; JHN 6:67

NT writers exhort believers to abide in Christ

COL 2:6 See also GAL 4:9, GAL 5:5–5:6; COL 3:1–3:3; HEB 12:1–12:3

Abiding in Christ depends upon holding on to his teaching

1JN 2:24 See also JHN 8:31; 2TH 2:15; 2TI 3:14; 2JN 1:9; 3JN 1:3–1:4

It depends on obedience to him

JHN 15:10 See also MAT 7:24–7:25; JHN 14:23; JAS 1:25; 1JN 3:24

It requires living like Jesus Christ

1JN 2:6

Aids to abiding in Christ

Eating his flesh and drinking his blood

JHN 6:56 Jn 6:35–40 gives the primary explanation of this verse as being a metaphor of the believer coming in faith to Jesus Christ, “the bread of life”. But the verse also reflects the language of the Lord's Supper.

The Spirit's anointing

1JN 2:27 See also JHN 14:17, JHN 14:23; ROM 8:9; 1JN 3:24

Jesus Christ abides in believers

JHN 15:4 It is clear that the believer's “abiding in Christ” and Jesus Christ's “abiding in him” are closely connected, although the verse does not make their exact relationship clear. Because of Jesus Christ's indwelling by his Spirit, believers are able to continue to live as his disciples; as they do so, the reality of his indwelling presence is deepened. See also JHN 17:23; COL 1:27; 1JN 3:24; REV 3:20

title: 8104: assurance
content: Certainty of a present relationship with God through Jesus Christ and a secure future hope which is based upon divine revelation, centred on the person, promises and action of God and confirmed by the Holy Spirit.

content:

Assurance is based upon the certain knowledge of God

Assurance comes from knowing God through creation

ROM 1:19–1:20 See also PSA 19:1–19:4; ACT 14:17

Assurance comes from knowing God through his mighty acts

The Holy Spirit assures believers by giving inward conviction

ROM 8:16; 1JN 4:13 See also JHN 15:26, JHN 16:8–16:11; ACT 5:32; GAL 4:6

The Holy Spirit assures believers by sealing God's promise

EPH 1:13–1:14 See also ACT 15:8; ROM 5:5; 2CO 1:22, 2CO 5:5; EPH 4:30; 1JN 3:24

title: 8114: discipleship
content: The process of becoming a committed follower of Jesus Christ, with all the spiritual discipline and benefits which this brings.

content:

Learning from Jesus Christ

title: 8134: knowing God
content: A faith-relationship and love-relationship with God involving mind, heart and will, and bringing experience of his presence and power. To know God is to worship him and be transformed by him. Human knowledge of God, which begins with knowledge about him, comes through God's self-revelation.

title: 8135: knowing God, nature of
content:
To know God is not merely to know things about him, such as his character, but also to experience his presence and power. To know God is to be transformed by him. Human knowledge of God is as a result of God's revelation of himself.

The origin of knowing God

Knowing God depends on revelation

title: 8138: monotheism
content:
The central doctrine that there is one true God, who alone is the object of worship. There is none like the LORD; other gods and idols are nothing. Scripture also indicates that there is a network of relationships within the Godhead which is stated in terms of the doctrine of the Trinity.

content: The regeneration or revitalisation that God brings to his people and creation, as part of the process of redemption.

title: 8154: righteousness
content: Scripture identifies a close link between righteousness and faith. Part of “being in a right relationship with God” is believing and trusting in him. The NT does not see faith simply in terms of moral righteousness, but also in terms of a living trusting relationship with God. Scripture affirms the righteousness of God and Jesus Christ in all their activity.

title: 8201: blamelessness
content:
A quality of life apparent in an individual against whom no just charge can be made. This is exemplified supremely in the blameless life and death of Jesus Christ. Though believers remain imperfect in this life, they are counted blameless in God's sight on account of the atoning death of Jesus Christ.

Jesus Christ's human life was blameless

1PE 2:22 See also ISA 53:9; JHN 8:46; 2CO 5:21; HEB 7:26; 1PE 1:19; 1JN 3:5

Jesus Christ's blameless life and death were the perfect fulfilment of the OT sacrifices

EXO 12:5

All other animals used as sacrifices had to be without defect

See also LEV 1:3, LEV 6:6; NUM 6:14, NUM 28:19; DEU 15:21; EZK 45:23; MAL 1:8, MAL 1:13–1:14

title: 8206: Christlikeness
content:
The process by which believers are conformed to the likeness of Jesus Christ, especially in relation to obedience to and trust in God. Through the Holy Spirit, God refashions believers in the image of his Son, who is set before them as a model of the form of the redeemed life.

Believers are to become Christlike

1CO 11:1; PHP 2:5 Paul is arguing that believers must allow God to make them Christlike, which is the natural goal of their process of growing in faith. Christlikeness is not achieved by people merely trying to imitate Jesus Christ, but by God making believers more like his Son in sanctification, through the Spirit. title: 8207: commitment
content: A state of personal dedication to something or someone, which results in actively promoting and working for their good and well-being.

title: 8208: commitment, to God
content:
Commitment to God arises from faith in his promises, is expressed in worship and adoration and leads to obedience to his commands.

Commitment to God commanded

DEU 27:10; JOS 24:14; ROM 12:1–12:2 See also DEU 6:13, DEU 10:12–10:13, DEU 13:4; JOS 22:5 Joshua reiterates Moses' commands; JDG 6:10; 1SA 7:3, 1SA 12:24; 1CH 28:9 David's instructions to Solomon; 2CH 19:9; JER 38:20; 1TH 4:1; 2TI 2:22

Obedience to God's commands as a sign of commitment

DEU 7:9; JOS 24:24; ROM 6:17 See also EXO 19:8; DEU 11:22; 1KI 8:61; NEH 10:29; PSA 40:6–40:8 The reference may be to the ear-piercing that was a sign of slaves' voluntary commitment to their masters; JER 7:23, JER 11:3, JER 38:20, JER 42:6; HAG 1:12; ZEC 6:15JHN 14:15, JHN 15:10 ACT 5:29; ROM 2:13

Love for God and worship of him are hallmarks of commitment

Examples of commitment to God

God's commitment of gifts

1CO 9:17

God's commitment of the faith to believers

JUD 1:3

title: 8209: commitment, to Jesus Christ
content:
Commitment to Jesus Christ is grounded in the knowledge of his saving power and divinity, and expresses itself in adoration and obedience to Jesus Christ.

Jesus Christ commanded people to make the commitment to follow him

MAT 4:19 parallel MRK 1:17MAT 9:9 parallels MRK 2:14, LUK 5:27 See also MAT 19:21–19:22; JHN 1:43, JHN 21:19, JHN 21:22; ROM 15:5; 1CO 1:12 There may have been a “Christ-party” at Corinth, or in contrast with the sectarianism, Paul may be asserting his own commitment to Jesus Christ.

Jesus Christ frequently spelt out the cost of commitment to him

MAT 10:37–10:38 parallel LUK 14:26–14:27MAT 16:24 parallels MRK 8:34, LUK 9:23JHN 12:25–12:26 See also MAT 8:22, MAT 10:39 parallels MRK 8:35, LUK 17:33; MAT 19:21 parallels MRK 10:21, LUK 18:22; LUK 14:28–14:33; 1PE 2:21

Jesus Christ's demand for commitment was sometimes met with a refusal

title: 8210: commitment, to God's people
content:
Commitment to God means a commitment to his people. Believers are meant to be nourished and supported by the church, and to work towards its edification.

Commitment to the church

ACT 2:42; EPH 4:3–4:4; COL 3:15 ROM 12:4–12:10; ; 1CO 12:12–12:27

Commitment to other Christians is an expression of love made known in Christ

title: 8211: commitment, to the world
content:
Though the world is fallen, God still loves the world and is committed to it. Commitment by believers to worldly pursuits and evil is to be avoided as they are called upon to be “in the world” but “not of the world”.

Commitment to this world to be avoided because it is a fallen and sinful place

GAL 1:4; 1JN 5:19 See also 2CO 4:4; EPH 2:2, EPH 6:12; 2PE 1:4; 1JN 2:16–2:17, 1JN 3:1, 1JN 3:13

Though the world is fallen, God still loves it

JHN 3:16 See also 2CO 5:18–5:20

Preoccupation with the things of this world is incompatible with holy living

JAS 4:4; 1JN 2:15 See also JHN 17:14–17:16; ACT 2:40; ROM 12:2; 1CO 7:31; 2CO 6:14–6:17; ISA 52:11; PHP 2:15; COL 3:2; TIT 2:12; JAS 1:27; 1PE 1:14, 1PE 2:11, 1PE 4:3

Commitment to the world is seen especially in materialism

1TI 6:17 See also MAT 6:19, MAT 19:23 parallel LUK 18:24; LUK 12:16–12:21

Spiritual loss

LUK 9:25 parallels MAT 16:26, MRK 8:36 See also MAT 13:22; 2TI 4:10

God's judgment

1CO 11:32 See also JHN 12:31, JHN 16:11; EPH 5:6

LUK 21:34 See also MAT 24:38–24:39; LUK 12:40, LUK 12:46; 1TH 5:1–5:9

title: 8213: confidence
content: A state of self-assurance regarding one's status or ability, often grounded in human achievements. Scripture insists that Christian confidence is to be grounded in what God has done for believers, rather than in what they themselves have achieved.

title: 8214: confidence, basis of
content:
The confidence of believers, is grounded in God's character, actions and trustworthy promises, rather than human achievements.

Confidence originates with God

In his unchanging and faithful nature

NUM 23:19; TIT 1:1–1:2 See also 1SA 15:29; PSA 33:11, PSA 102:27; PRO 3:26; ISA 49:23; MAL 3:6; 2TI 1:12; JAS 1:17

In his covenant

JER 32:40; HEB 9:15 See also GEN 9:16 with all living creatures; GEN 17:7 with Abraham; 2SA 7:13 with the house of David; 2SA 23:5; PSA 89:34; ISA 54:10, ISA 55:3; EZK 16:60; ACT 3:25

In election

DEU 7:6; ROM 8:28 See also ISA 41:9–41:10; JER 31:3; ROM 8:33; 1CO 1:9; 1TH 5:24; 2TI 2:19

In his past deliverances

PSA 22:4–22:5; ROM 8:31–8:32 See also DEU 7:18, DEU 20:1; JOS 1:5; 1SA 17:37; 1KI 8:57; PSA 44:1–44:5, PSA 78:2–78:4; 2CO 1:10

In his word

In his promises

JOS 23:14; HEB 10:23 See also 1KI 8:20; PSA 119:140; 2PE 1:4

ROM 8:16 See also 2CO 1:21–1:22, 2CO 5:5; EPH 1:13–1:14

content:
God-given assurance produces spiritual maturity and stability, so that believers may withstand the adverse conditions of life.

Confidence in God's protection removes fear of disaster

PSA 46:1–46:2 See also EXO 14:13–14:14; PSA 56:3–56:4; ACT 27:22–27:25

Confidence in God's purposes produces hope

PSA 130:7; 2CO 1:10 See also PSA 25:3–25:6, PSA 62:5–62:8, PSA 71:5–71:7; PRO 23:17–23:18; ROM 5:3–5:5; 1TI 6:17–6:18; HEB 6:17–6:19

ISA 41:8–41:10 See also JOS 1:5–1:9; PSA 3:3–3:6, PSA 20:7, PSA 23:4, PSA 27:1–27:4, PSA 138:3; ISA 12:2, ISA 44:8; JER 1:8; ACT 4:13, ACT 9:27, ACT 18:9–18:11; EPH 6:10–6:11

HAB 3:17–3:19; 2TI 3:10–3:11 See also JOB 19:26; PSA 42:9–42:10; EPH 6:13; HEB 10:32–10:35, HEB 11:35–11:39, HEB 12:1–12:2; 1PE 3:14, 1PE 4:12–4:19; REV 3:10

PSA 23:1; EPH 6:10 See also DEU 33:12; PSA 7:9, PSA 28:7, PSA 40:2, PSA 46:1–46:3, PSA 112:6–112:8, PSA 121:1–121:2; PRO 14:26; ISA 32:17; 2CO 1:21; EPH 6:13; 1TI 3:13; 2TI 1:12

title: 8217: conformity
content:
Correspondence in character or behaviour; believers are not to conform to the ways of this world but are to be conformed to the image of Christ.

Believers are not to conform to the ways of this world

ROM 12:2; 1PE 1:14 See also EXO 23:2; LEV 20:23; DEU 18:9 Israel was not to imitate the practices of surrounding nations; 2KI 17:15; EZK 11:12; DAN 1:8 Daniel refused to conform to the ways of Babylon; DAN 3:12; EPH 4:17; COL 3:7–3:8; 1TH 5:6; 1TI 1:9–1:11; 1PE 4:3; 3JN 1:11

content:
The setting apart of people, things, times or places as sacred, for God to use.

title: 8219: courage
content: The quality of being able to act bravely under difficulties or in the face of opposition; being prepared to do dangerous or risky things in obedience to God, in the belief that he will strengthen, guard and protect his people.

title: 8220: courage, in facing enemies
content:
In the OT, courage is shown principally in the leading of God's people against their enemies.

God commands his people to be courageous

JOS 1:6–1:9 The LORD to Joshua as he was about to lead the Israelites into Canaan. See also JOS 1:18, JOS 8:1, JOS 10:8; JDG 7:9–7:11; 2CH 20:15, 2CH 20:17

Recommended by leaders

DEU 1:21 See also DEU 31:1–31:8; JOS 10:25, JOS 23:6; 2SA 10:12; 2CH 32:7

Seen in the behaviour of people of God

1SA 17:32; ACT 4:13 See also JOS 1:10–1:11, JOS 14:12; 1SA 14:6–14:7, 1SA 17:45–17:47; ACT 13:44–13:47 Paul and Barnabas; ACT 19:8–19:10 Paul at Ephesus

title: 8221: courage, as strength from God
content:
God gives strength to his people. He enables them to be courageous through his gift of faith. God proves himself faithful to his promises and enables his people to trust him in everyday life.

Courage through faithful obedience

1CH 22:11–22:13 See also 1CH 28:20; GEN 12:1–12:4; HEB 11:8; GEN 22:1–22:5; HEB 11:17–11:19; 2CH 15:8, 2CH 19:8–19:11; EZR 7:27–7:28, EZR 10:1–10:4; MAT 26:39 parallels MRK 14:35–14:36, LUK 22:41–22:42

Courage under pressure

Courage in prayer

HEB 4:14–4:16 See also GEN 18:27–18:28; 1CH 17:25 parallel 2SA 7:27

title: 8224: dependence
content:
Reliance upon God or upon others. Dependence on God for help with spiritual and physical needs arises out of an awareness of human helplessness, though dependence may be wrongly directed. People may look to others for encouragement and support, but over-dependence is not commended.

Dependence arising from a sense of helplessness

Physical helplessness

ISA 64:6; ; MRK 9:17–9:18 parallels MAT 17:14–17:16, LUK 9:38–9:40; ; ROM 5:6, ROM 7:18

God is to be trusted

title: 8266: holiness
content: The quality of God that sets him utterly apart from his world, especially in terms of his purity and sanctity. The holiness of God is also manifested in the persons and work of Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit. Believers are called upon to become like God in his holiness.

content:
God's people are called to holiness, which involves being distinct from other people. In the OT, this is seen in the command to separate from other nations and from everything that can compromise commitment to the LORD. In the NT believers are called to distance themselves from the ways and values of the world, which can be dishonouring to God and destructive to obedience to him.

title: 8273: holiness, ethical aspects of
content:
Behaviour that reflects the holy character of God himself is to be expressed in both social and personal dimensions of life.

1PE 1:15–1:16 See also LEV 11:44–11:45, LEV 19:2, LEV 20:7; EPH 4:24; 1JN 3:3

Holiness demands a different way of life

Shunning practices that defile

Care for the disadvantaged

A concern for truth and justice

LEV 19:15–19:16 See also LEV 19:11–19:13, LEV 19:35–19:37

Loving one's neighbour

LEV 19:18 See also LEV 19:16–19:17 Most of the OT law can be seen as an expression of holiness.

COL 3:12 See also EPH 4:23–4:24, EPH 4:32–5:2; 2TI 2:22

title: 8275: honesty
content:
Behaviour, in action and words, that aims to convey truth. This quality is an essential aspect of God's own nature and purposes, and is required of those whom he calls to be his people.

Honesty is integral to the gospel

The honesty of God

2SA 7:28 See also PSA 19:7, PSA 33:4, PSA 111:7, PSA 119:142, PSA 119:151; ISA 45:19; JER 10:10; JHN 7:28; ROM 3:4; 1TH 1:9; 1JN 5:20; REV 3:7, REV 15:2–15:3, REV 19:9

The honesty demanded of believers

PSA 15:1–15:2; 2CO 4:2 See also EXO 18:21LEV 19:35–19:36; DEU 25:13–25:16 1KI 9:4–9:5; PRO 11:1; EZK 45:10; ZEC 8:16–8:17; JHN 4:23–4:24; ROM 1:18; 1CO 5:8EPH 4:15, EPH 4:25 PHP 4:81TI 3:8; TIT 1:7 TIT 2:7–2:8

1PE 2:22 See also MAT 22:16 parallel MRK 12:14 Jesus Christ's opponents flattering Jesus Christ, but nevertheless speaking the truth.

Jacob: GEN 30:33, GEN 43:12; 1SA 12:3–12:5 Samuel; ; 1KI 17:24 Elijah; ; 1CH 29:17 David; ; JOB 27:4 Job; ; DAN 6:4 Daniel; ACT 24:16; ; 2CO 1:12, 2CO 2:17, 2CO 4:2

content:

PSA 44:9 See also LEV 26:41; DEU 8:2, DEU 8:16; 1KI 11:39; 2CH 28:19; PSA 107:39; ISA 9:1; 2CO 12:21

LUK 18:14 See also 1SA 2:7; ISA 2:11, ISA 2:17, ISA 5:15, ISA 13:11, ISA 23:9, ISA 25:11, ISA 26:5; DAN 4:37

title: 8277: innocence
content: The state of being devoid of guilt, experience of sin or evil motives or thoughts. Scripture commends this state to believers.

title: 8278: innocence, teaching on
content:
A highly valued quality to be eagerly sought. The OT stresses that the innocent deserve justice rather than evil. In the NT believers are encouraged to attain innocence.

Exhortations to be innocent

MAT 10:16 See also PSA 32:2; ROM 16:19; PHP 2:14–2:15; 1TH 3:13, 1TH 5:23; 2PE 3:14

Ascribing innocence to people

Innocence is ultimately established by God

1CO 4:4 See also COL 1:21–1:22

The need to acquit the innocent

1KI 8:32 See also EXO 23:7; NUM 5:29–5:31; DEU 25:1; PRO 17:15, PRO 18:5

The danger of acquitting the guilty

PRO 17:15 See also PRO 24:23–24:24

The rewards of innocence

PSA 15:1–15:5 See also REV 14:1–14:5

The characteristics of innocence

PRO 21:8 See also PHP 2:14–2:15, PHP 4:8

content:

title: 8281: insight
content:
The spiritual quality that enables a person to appreciate God's mind and will in matters of behaviour, truth and providence, especially where right perception is not obvious. Insight is akin to wisdom and understanding. It is given by God and is to be sought by believers.

Insight is given by God

2TI 2:7 See also PRO 2:6

Insight through angelic instruction

JOB 33:23; ; DAN 9:20–9:22

Insight through Jesus Christ's teaching

LUK 24:45–24:47 See also LUK 24:27; MAT 16:12

Insight through the Holy Spirit

1CO 2:9–2:13 See also ISA 64:4; EPH 3:4–3:5

Human insight cannot comprehend spiritual truth

1CO 2:14 See also JOB 9:11; 1CO 1:20–1:21

Insight into spiritual truth

Insight into the truth about Jesus Christ

COL 2:2–2:3 See also JHN 16:12–16:15

Insight into the believer's hope and power

EPH 1:18–1:19

ACT 10:34–10:35; ; EPH 3:2–3:6

Insight into the number of the beast

REV 13:18

Joseph's insight

GEN 50:20 See also GEN 45:4–45:8

David's insight

2SA 5:12 parallel 1CH 14:2

title: 8282: intolerance
content:
Unwillingness to allow or permit something beyond certain levels. God's intolerance should be the model for God's people, but they should avoid becoming wrongly intolerant.

God is intolerant of evil

God is pure and cannot tolerate evil

HAB 1:13 See also NUM 25:3; JOS 7:1; 2SA 6:7 parallel 1CH 13:10; 2KI 17:11; PSA 5:6; ROM 1:18; REV 21:27

God demonstrates his intolerance as the last resort

JER 44:22 See also EXO 4:10–4:14, EXO 34:6–34:7; NUM 14:18; NEH 9:30; ACT 17:30; ROM 2:3–2:5

Human intolerance should reflect God's attitudes

Human intolerance of God's enemies

JDG 5:31 See also 1SA 17:26; PSA 69:9; MAT 26:51 parallels MRK 14:47, LUK 22:50; JHN 18:10; EPH 5:6–5:7

Human intolerance of ungodliness

EXO 32:19–32:20 See also DEU 6:13–6:15; PSA 119:115; 1TI 4:7; 2TI 2:16, 2TI 3:5; TIT 2:12

TIT 3:10 See also ACT 17:11, ACT 20:30–20:31; GAL 5:11–5:12; EPH 5:6–5:7; COL 2:8; HEB 13:9

JHN 8:5 See also NUM 21:4–21:5; EST 3:8; MAT 23:34–23:35; JHN 7:45–7:51, JHN 16:2

JHN 15:19 See also NUM 11:27–11:29; JDG 12:5–12:6; MAT 21:15–21:16, MAT 23:16, MAT 23:18

MAT 19:13–19:14 parallels MRK 10:13–10:14, LUK 18:15–18:16 The disciples' intolerance is counteracted by Jesus Christ's tolerance.

title: 8283: joy
content: A quality or attitude of delight and happiness, which is ultimately grounded in the work of God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit. Among the many situations in which joy is experienced, Scripture recognises as supreme being accepted in the presence of God.

title: 8284: joy, of God
content: See 1070: God, joy of

title: 8285: joy, of Jesus Christ
content: See 2039: Jesus Christ, joy of

title: 8286: joy, of Holy Spirit
content: See 3020: Holy Spirit, joy of

title: 8287: joy, and human experience
content:
Joy is experienced naturally in many circumstances of life and in human relationships. It is especially important in the life of God's people, who experience joy in response to all that God has done for them.

Poetic images of joy in creation

PSA 96:11–96:13 parallel 1CH 16:31–16:33 See also JOB 39:13; PSA 65:12–65:13, PSA 89:12, PSA 97:1, PSA 100:1; ISA 35:1–35:2, ISA 49:13

Joy arising from specific circumstances

Joy because of the birth of children

LUK 1:13–1:15 See also GEN 30:12–30:13; LUK 1:58

Joy because of victory and deliverance

EXO 18:9; ; 1SA 18:6; ; JER 41:13; ; ZEC 10:7

Joy because of the behaviour of others

PRO 15:30 See also PRO 23:24–23:25; MAT 14:6–14:7; HEB 13:17

Joy because of God's blessings in everyday life

ECC 5:19–5:20

Joy arising from relationships

PHP 4:1 See also PRO 5:18; SNG 1:4, SNG 3:11; ROM 12:15, ROM 15:26–15:27; 1CO 12:26; PHP 1:4–1:6; PHM 1:7

God's people find their joy in him

PSA 4:7, PSA 16:11; HAB 3:17–3:18; PHP 3:1 See also 1CH 16:10; PSA 43:4; PHP 1:23–1:26 knowing Jesus Christ; PHP 4:4

God himself gives joy to his people

NEH 12:43; ; JOB 8:21; ; ECC 2:26; ; ISA 9:3; ; ACT 13:52, ACT 14:15–14:17

1SA 2:1 God's deliverance; ; 2CH 6:41 God's goodness; ; JOB 22:22–22:26 repentance; ; PSA 19:8 the rightness of God's precepts; ; PSA 94:19 God's consolation; ; PSA 122:1 being in God's presence; ; ISA 25:9 God's salvation; ; ISA 58:13–58:14 honouring the Sabbath; ; JER 15:16 God's words; ; JER 31:12 God's generosity; ; LUK 1:46–1:49 recognition by God; ; ROM 15:13 trusting God

1KI 1:39–1:40 See also 1CH 29:21–29:22; 2CH 23:12–23:13

1KI 8:64–8:66 parallel 2CH 7:1–7:10 See also 1CH 29:9, 1CH 29:17

2CH 29:36

title: 8289: joy, of the church
content:
The church is to rejoice in the salvation brought about by Jesus Christ's faithful life and death, and by the power of his resurrection. Even in adversity, believers know the joy of Jesus Christ.

Joy at the coming of Jesus Christ

LUK 2:8–2:11 See also JHN 3:27–3:29, JHN 8:56

Joy as the hallmark of the kingdom of God

ACT 2:46–2:47 See also ACT 15:1–15:3; ROM 15:31–15:32; 2CO 2:3; PHP 2:17–2:18

1PE 1:8–1:9 See also JHN 15:7–15:11; HEB 12:22–12:24; REV 19:7

ACT 16:33–16:34 See also ACT 8:38–8:39; ROM 5:11

ACT 5:41; 1PE 4:12–4:13 See also MAT 5:11–5:12 parallel LUK 6:22–6:23; 2CO 7:4, 2CO 8:1–8:2, 2CO 12:7–12:10, 2CO 13:9; PHP 2:17–2:18; COL 1:24; 1TH 1:6; HEB 10:34; JAS 1:2–1:3; 1PE 1:3–1:6

2CO 7:7 See also 2CO 7:12–7:13; PHP 2:1–2:2 the Philippians' love for one another; PHM 1:7

PHP 1:4–1:6

title: 8291: kindness
content:
The quality of compassion and generosity, characteristic of God's dealings towards the weak and poor, and demanded of believers. The kindness is also shown in the words and deeds of Jesus Christ.

The kindness of God

To all

ACT 14:17 Paul to the pagans at Lystra. See also JER 9:24; LUK 6:35

To his people

ISA 63:7 See also EZR 9:9; ISA 54:8; HOS 11:4

To the king

2SA 22:51 See also 1KI 3:6

To individuals

GEN 19:19 Lot; ; GEN 24:27 Abraham; ; GEN 32:10 Jacob; ; GEN 39:21 Joseph; ; RUT 1:8 Ruth; ; RUT 2:20 Naomi; ; JOB 10:12 Job; ; 2SA 9:1–9:13 Mephibosheth through David

The kindness of Jesus Christ

MAT 9:36 See also MAT 14:14, MAT 20:34; MRK 8:2–8:3; LUK 7:13; ACT 20:35; HEB 4:15

TIT 3:4–3:5 See also ROM 11:22 God's grace extending to the Gentiles while the Jews are judged for their unbelief; EPH 2:7

In the OT

PRO 14:21; DAN 4:27 See also PRO 11:16–11:17, PRO 12:25, PRO 14:31, PRO 19:17, PRO 28:8

In the NT

2SA 10:2–10:4

2CH 24:22

title: 8292: love
content: A caring commitment, in which affection and delight are shown to others, which is grounded in the nature of God himself. In his words and actions, and supremely in the death of Jesus Christ on the cross, God demonstrates the nature of love and defines the direction in which human love in all its forms should develop.

content: See 1085: God, love of

title: 8294: love, and Jesus Christ
content: See 2048: Jesus Christ, love of

content: See 3209: Holy Spirit, and love

title: 8296: love, nature of
content:
Scripture offers an understanding of the source, character and value of love, based on the nature and actions of God.

God is the source of love

content: The holding of religious beliefs that are in harmony with the accepted views of the community of faith. Right belief (orthodoxy) is to show itself in right practice (orthopraxis).

title: 8315: orthodoxy, in OT
content:
The acceptance of God's revelation of himself to his people that should lead to worship and obedience.

Foundational truths about Israel's God

God is one

DEU 6:4

God is unique

DEU 4:39 See also DEU 4:35; PSA 97:9; ISA 44:6–44:8

God is self-existent

EXO 3:14

God is the Creator

ISA 40:28 See also GEN 1:1, GEN 2:7; JOB 38:4

God will not tolerate rivals

EXO 20:3–20:6 parallel DEU 5:7–5:8; ; DEU 8:19–8:20, DEU 13:6–13:8; ; ISA 42:8

God commands universal worship

PSA 86:9–86:10 See also ISA 19:21; ZEC 8:20–8:22

Right belief is passed on through the community of faith

PSA 145:4 See also EXO 12:24–12:27; DEU 6:6–6:8, DEU 6:20–6:25; JOS 4:20–4:24; PSA 78:2–78:6

Right belief demands right practice

Reverent fear

DEU 10:12–10:13

Worship

See also DEU 12:4–12:7; 2KI 17:35–17:39; 1CH 16:28–16:29 parallel PSA 96:7–96:9; PSA 95:6–95:7

Observance of festivals

DEU 16:1–16:2, DEU 16:9–16:17

Offering acceptable sacrifices

LEV 1:2–1:4, LEV 5:5–5:6; ; MAL 1:7–1:8

Faithfulness to the covenant

DEU 29:9–29:15; ; PSA 25:10

Devotion to God

DEU 6:5 See also DEU 11:1; 1CH 22:19; PSA 31:23; HOS 6:6

Trust in God's faithfulness

PSA 4:5, PSA 33:4 See also PSA 37:3–37:5, PSA 115:9–115:11, PSA 119:89–119:93

Obedience

DEU 5:32 See also DEU 6:1–6:3, DEU 26:16–26:19; 1SA 15:22; ISA 30:21; JER 7:21–7:23

Justice in society

MIC 6:8 See also PSA 106:3; PRO 21:3; ISA 1:11–1:17, ISA 56:1

Walking in God's ways

God's ways are right

HOS 14:9 See also PRO 10:29

Walking in God's ways brings his blessing

GEN 18:19; ; DEU 5:33, DEU 28:9, DEU 30:19–30:20

Examples of kings who walked in God's ways

2SA 22:22 parallel PSA 18:21 David; ; 2CH 14:2–14:4 parallel 1KI 15:11–15:12 Asa; ; 2CH 17:3–17:6 Jehoshaphat; ; 2CH 26:4 parallel 2KI 15:3 Uzziah (and Amaziah); ; 2CH 29:2 parallel 2KI 18:3 Hezekiah; ; 2CH 34:2 parallel 2KI 22:2 Josiah

title: 8316: orthodoxy, in NT
content:
Acceptance of the truth, especially about Jesus Christ, that is revealed by the Holy Spirit in the gospel and is passed on through the teaching of sound doctrine.

Orthodoxy is based on Jesus Christ who is the truth

EPH 4:21 See also JHN 1:14, JHN 14:6

Orthodoxy is revealed in the gospel

GAL 1:11–1:12; 2TI 1:13–1:14 See also 2CO 11:3–11:4; GAL 1:6–1:9, GAL 2:5, GAL 2:14; COL 1:5–1:6; 1TI 1:9–1:11

Orthodoxy is expressed in simple summaries of faith

1TI 3:16 See also ROM 1:3–1:4; 1CO 15:3–15:5; PHP 2:5–2:11

Orthodoxy is maintained through God's true ministers

1TI 2:7 See also 1TI 4:6; 2TI 2:2, 2TI 2:15

Orthodoxy must be defended against error

TIT 1:9 See also 1TI 6:20–6:21

Orthodoxy is shown by the attitude to the incarnation

1JN 4:2–4:3 See also 1JN 4:15, 1JN 5:1, 1JN 5:10

Orthodoxy is revealed by the Holy Spirit

JHN 16:13 See also JHN 14:17, JHN 14:26, JHN 15:26; 1JN 2:27

Orthodoxy is demonstrated in believers' behaviour

Walking as children of light

JHN 3:19–3:21; ; EPH 5:8; ; 1JN 1:7

Following Jesus Christ's example

JHN 13:15; ; 1CO 11:1; ; 1PE 2:21; ; 1JN 2:6

Loving and obeying Jesus Christ

JHN 14:15, JHN 14:21, JHN 14:23, JHN 15:10; ; 1JN 2:3–2:5

Right belief requires right action

JAS 2:19 See also JAS 2:14–2:18, JAS 2:20–2:26

Signs of a fall from orthodoxy

False prophecy

1JN 4:1 See also MAT 7:22–7:23; MRK 13:21–13:22 parallel MAT 24:11

Empty religion

MAT 15:9 parallel MRK 7:7 See also ISA 29:13; MRK 7:8–7:9 parallel MAT 15:3

False teaching

1TI 4:1–4:2; 2TI 4:3–4:4 See also 1TI 1:6–1:7, 1TI 6:3–6:5; TIT 1:10–1:14; 2PE 2:1–2:2

Examples of false teachings contrary to orthodoxy

Christians are obliged to obey the entire OT law

GAL 5:1–5:12

Justification comes only through the OT law

GAL 2:15–2:21

The resurrection has already taken place

2TI 2:16–2:18

Christians do not sin

1JN 1:8–1:10

resource.label: 8028: faith, as a body of beliefs

title: 8318: patience
content:
The quality of forbearance and self-control which shows itself particularly in a willingness to wait upon God and his will. Believers are called upon to be patient in their expectations of God's actions, and in their relationships with one another.

God's patience

EXO 34:6–34:7; ROM 2:4 See also NEH 9:30; ISA 48:9, ISA 65:2; JOL 2:13; JON 4:2; NAM 1:3; ACT 17:30; ROM 3:25, ROM 9:22; 1PE 3:20; 2PE 3:9

The patience of Jesus Christ

1TI 1:16 See also MAT 17:17 parallels MRK 9:19, LUK 9:41; JHN 14:9; 2PE 3:15; REV 2:21

Other examples of patience

2TH 1:4 the Thessalonian believers; ; HEB 6:15; ; JAS 5:11 Job; REV 1:9, REV 2:2

Patience is part of the fruit of the Spirit

GAL 5:22 See also COL 1:10–1:11

God's people should exercise patience

PRO 19:11; COL 3:12 See also PRO 14:29, PRO 16:32, PRO 25:15; MAT 6:14–6:15, MAT 18:35

People who need particular patience

Christian leaders

2TI 4:2 See also 2TI 3:10

Christian masters

EPH 6:9

Patience is necessary in church life

EPH 4:2 See also ROM 15:1; COL 3:13; 1TH 5:14

God's word is to be received with patience

HEB 13:22 See also PRO 2:1–2:5; 2TI 4:3

Patience is a characteristic of love

1CO 13:4

Patience is an aspect of faith and hope

PSA 33:20; JAS 5:7–5:8 PSA 5:2, PSA 27:14, PSA 37:7, PSA 37:34, PSA 38:15; PSA 119:166, PSA 130:5–130:6; ; PRO 20:22; ; ISA 8:17, ISA 30:18; ; LAM 3:24, LAM 3:26; ; MIC 7:7; ; ZEP 3:8; ; ACT 1:4 Jesus Christ's instructions to the apostles to wait for the Holy Spirit; ; ROM 8:25, ROM 12:12; ; TIT 2:13; ; HEB 6:12, HEB 6:15 the example of Abraham; ; JAS 5:10; ; REV 6:11

title: 8319: perception, spiritual
content:
The ability to see beneath the outward form to the underlying, often hidden, reality. It is a necessary gift in dealing with people, understanding spiritual teaching and interpreting events. Perception is important for effective service, though is often lacking, even among God's people.

Perception in dealing with people

God's knowledge of human hearts

PSA 139:1–139:4 See also PSA 17:3, PSA 44:21; PRO 24:12

Jesus Christ's perception of those around him

JHN 2:24–2:25 See also ISA 11:1–11:4; MAT 9:3–9:4 parallels MRK 2:7–2:8, LUK 5:21–5:22; JHN 4:16–4:19; REV 2:23

True understanding by God's servants

NEH 6:1–6:2; ; JOB 21:27; ; ACT 5:1–5:3

Perception of spiritual truth

Recognising God's ultimate authority

REV 4:1–4:2 See also 2KI 6:15–6:17; DAN 7:8–7:14

Understanding Jesus Christ's teaching

MAT 13:10–13:11 parallels MRK 4:10–4:11, LUK 8:9–8:10 See also MAT 13:16–13:23 parallels MRK 4:13–4:20, LUK 8:11–8:15 The parable of the sower is about the way Jesus Christ's teaching in parables is received.

Understanding who Jesus Christ is

MAT 16:15–16:17 parallels MRK 8:29, LUK 9:20 See also ACT 8:30–8:35; ISA 53:7–53:8

Understanding about Jesus Christ's death and resurrection

LUK 24:45–24:46 See also LUK 24:30–24:35; JHN 12:16

Perception to interpret events

2SA 5:11–5:12 The building of a palace in the newly captured Jerusalem confirms to David his election by God; ISA 43:9–43:12 Through his miraculous direction of his people's history, God is perceived as the one, true God. See also ISA 41:18–41:20, ISA 64:4; JON 1:12 Jonah recognises God's hand in the storm; ACT 10:34–10:35 Through the circumstances of his guidance, Peter realises that God's salvation is for Gentiles too.

Perception leading to effective service

1KI 3:9 parallel 2CH 1:10 See also 1SA 16:7–16:13 Samuel perceives that David is to be king; 2KI 4:8–4:10 A Shunammite's perception of Elisha leads her to extend hospitality to him; HEB 11:27 Moses' perception of the invisible God

Lack of perception

By those in the OT

ISA 43:19 See also EXO 5:2 Pharaoh; NUM 22:31–22:34 Balaam; DEU 32:28–32:29 Israel in the wilderness; ISA 29:10–29:12 the people of Jerusalem; ISA 42:20 Israel

By some Jews in the NT

MAT 13:13–13:15 parallels MRK 4:12, LUK 8:10; ; ISA 6:9–6:10; ; LUK 12:56; ; JHN 3:3–3:4; ; ACT 28:26

By Jesus Christ's disciples

MAT 15:16 parallel MRK 7:18 not understanding what makes a person unclean; ; MAT 16:9 parallel MRK 8:17–8:18 not understanding about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees; ; MAT 16:22 parallel MRK 8:32 Peter cannot accept that Jesus Christ must be crucified; ; JHN 14:9 Philip does not understand that Jesus Christ reveals the Father; ; JHN 20:9 not understanding about the resurrection; JHN 20:14, JHN 21:4

title: 8320: perfection
content: The state of completion and total self-sufficiency, characterised by an absence of any flaw or fault. This perfection is found in God himself and is the ultimate goal of the Christian life.

title: 8321: perfection, divine
content:
The state of being whole, complete or without defect in any way.

Only God is absolutely perfect

In his nature and character

DEU 32:4 See also ECC 3:14; MAT 5:48; ROM 11:33–11:36

In his word

PSA 12:6 See also PSA 19:7; PRO 8:8–8:9, PRO 30:5; 2TI 3:16–3:17; JAS 1:25

In his morality

HAB 1:13 See also 2SA 22:26–22:27; JOB 4:17; 1JN 3:3

In his will and providence

2SA 22:31 parallel PSA 18:30 See also ROM 12:2; JAS 1:17

In his knowledge

JOB 37:16 See also PSA 139:4; ISA 40:13–40:14; HEB 4:13

In his faithfulness

ISA 25:1

God's perfect creation

In its original condition

GEN 2:1–2:2 See also GEN 1:10, GEN 1:12, GEN 1:18, GEN 1:21, GEN 1:25, GEN 1:31; ISA 40:25–40:26; HEB 4:3

The coming new creation

1CO 13:10 See also 2PE 3:13; REV 21:1–21:5, REV 22:1–22:5

God's perfect self-revelation in Jesus Christ

JHN 14:9 See also JHN 1:14; 2CO 4:4; COL 1:15; HEB 1:3

The moral perfection of Jesus Christ as God's Son

1PE 2:22 See also ISA 53:9; 2CO 5:21; HEB 2:10, HEB 4:15, HEB 5:9, HEB 7:26; 1JN 3:5

The perfect sacrifice of Jesus Christ

HEB 9:14 LEV 22:21; ; NUM 19:2; 1PE 1:19

title: 8322: perfection, human
content:
Human wholeness in the image of God, given at creation and lost in the fall, is to be fully restored in Jesus Christ.

Humanity was created perfect

GEN 1:26–1:27 See also GEN 5:1; EZK 28:12–28:15 The king of Tyre is described in terms of the creation and fall of humanity; JAS 3:9

Perfection was lost through sin

ROM 3:23 See also GEN 2:17, GEN 3:16–3:19, GEN 3:23; JOB 15:14–15:16; EZK 28:15–28:17; ROM 1:21

The need for moral perfection

DEU 18:13 See also GEN 17:1; JOB 25:4; PSA 24:3–24:4

Human inability to keep God's law perfectly

HEB 7:19 See also HEB 7:11, HEB 10:1

Perfection and redemption

God's purpose for believers

COL 1:22 See also DAN 11:35, DAN 12:10; EPH 5:27 God's purpose for the church; HEB 10:14, HEB 11:40, HEB 12:23; JAS 1:4; JUD 1:24

The aim of Christian ministry

COL 1:28 See also 2CO 11:2

The aim of the Christian

PHP 3:12 See also 2CO 13:9–13:11; EPH 4:13; HEB 6:1; JAS 1:4

Characteristics of perfection

Perfect love

MAT 5:48 Jesus Christ patterning his disciples' love on the love God has for all people. See also 1JN 4:12, 1JN 4:18

Perfect holiness

2CO 7:1 See also PHP 1:10, PHP 2:15; JAS 1:27; 2PE 3:14

Perfect obedience

1TI 6:14; ; 1JN 2:5

Perfect speech

JAS 3:2

Perfect unity with other believers

JHN 17:23 See also 1CO 1:10; COL 3:14

Perfect joy

JHN 15:11 See also JHN 3:29, JHN 16:24; 1JN 1:4; 2JN 1:12

Perfect peace

ISA 26:3 See also PSA 119:165; PHP 4:7

Perfect knowledge

1CO 13:9–13:12 See also ROM 15:14 Although complete knowledge is inaccessible here and now, believers have all they need to live the Christian life; COL 2:2

Perfection in describing human physical beauty

2SA 14:25–14:27; ; SNG 4:7, SNG 5:2, SNG 6:9

False claims to perfection

JOB 36:4; ; PSA 64:6, PSA 119:96; ; EZK 27:3–27:4; ; PHP 3:6

title: 8324: purity
content: An absence of blemish or stain, especially sin. The state of being morally and spiritually pure, which is seen by Scripture as the result of being the people of God and also as an expected distinguishing mark of the church.

title: 8325: purity, nature of
content:
The OT recognises a close link between outer cleanliness and inner purity. In the NT, special emphasis is placed on inner purity resulting from spiritual renewal.

Physical cleansing from impurity by washing or refining

GEN 18:4; ; JOB 9:30; ; PSA 12:6

Ritual impurity must be avoided or cleansed

LEV 10:10–10:11 See also ISA 35:8, ISA 52:1, ISA 52:11; MRK 7:2, MRK 7:4

Sexual sources of ritual impurity

Childbirth

LEV 12:2 See also LEV 12:5; LUK 2:22

Sexual intercourse

EXO 19:15; ; LEV 15:18; ; 1SA 21:4

Seminal emission

LEV 15:16–15:17; ; DEU 23:10–23:11; ; 1SA 20:26

Menstruation

LEV 15:19–15:20; ; 2SA 11:2–11:4; ; EZK 18:6

Abnormal discharge

LEV 15:1–15:2, LEV 15:25–15:27; ; MAT 9:20 parallels MRK 5:25, LUK 8:43

Other sources of ritual impurity

Dead bodies

NUM 19:11–19:16

Unclean creatures

GEN 7:2 See also LEV 11:24, LEV 11:46–11:47; DEU 14:3; HOS 9:3

Skin diseases

LEV 13:45 See also MAT 8:2–8:4 parallels MRK 1:40–1:44, LUK 5:12–5:14

Mildew

LEV 14:36

Contact with a sin offering

LEV 16:26

Cleansing from ritual impurity

LEV 14:8 See also LEV 16:26; NUM 19:17–19:21, NUM 19:9, NUM 19:17–19:21, NUM 31:22–31:23 Fire is also a purifying agent.

Contact with God demanded purity

EXO 19:10 See also EXO 19:14–19:15, EXO 30:18–30:21; HEB 10:22

Ritual purity is not required under the new covenant

MAT 15:11 parallel MRK 7:15 What concerns God is moral impurity, associated with actions, not ritual impurity, associated with food, etc. See also ACT 10:12–10:15, ACT 21:26 Paul took part in Jewish purification rites in accordance with his Jewish heritage; ROM 14:14; GAL 2:11–2:12 Peter temporarily relapsed into the habit of treating Gentiles as unclean; GAL 2:14–2:15; 1TI 4:4

title: 8326: purity, moral and spiritual
content:
Moral and spiritual purity is demanded by God of his people. God calls his people to be holy, just as he is holy.

Divine purity

The purity of God

HAB 1:13 See also JOB 4:17; PSA 18:26; 1JN 1:5

The purity of Jesus Christ

1JN 3:3 See also MAT 17:2; HEB 7:26

Fellowship with God demands purity

PSA 24:3–24:4; MAT 5:8 See also PSA 51:6, PSA 73:1

God's people are to live pure lives

COL 3:5 See also LEV 18:30; JOB 31:1; PSA 51:10; 1CO 5:7–5:8 Yeast is a symbol of sin; 1CO 6:15–6:20; 1TH 4:3; TIT 1:15, TIT 2:5; HEB 13:4; JAS 1:27, JAS 4:8

Purity is unobtainable by human effort

Because of the sinful human nature

JOB 14:4 See also JOB 15:14, JOB 25:4; ECC 7:20

Because of the tendency to idolatry

HOS 8:5

Because of self-deception

PRO 30:12 See also PRO 20:9

Because of an unwillingness to be cleansed

EZK 24:13

Symbols of purification from sin

PSA 51:7 See also ISA 6:6 fire; MRK 1:4 water baptism; 2CO 11:2 virginity; 2PE 3:14 spotlessness

God promises to purify his people

EZK 36:25 See also ZEP 3:9; ZEC 13:1

Purification through Jesus Christ

Through pardon offered in his death

HEB 9:14 See also HEB 12:24; 1JN 1:7

Through his word

JHN 15:3 See also JHN 13:10

Through his presence in resisting temptation

JAS 4:7–4:8 See also 1PE 5:9

Through hope built on his promises

TIT 2:12–2:13 See also 1JN 3:3

Purification through judgment

In the OT

LEV 18:28 See also DEU 13:5, DEU 17:7, DEU 17:12; JDG 20:13; MAL 3:2–3:4

In the NT

1CO 5:13

Symbols of purity

Whiteness

DAN 7:9 See also PSA 51:7; ISA 1:18; MAT 17:2 parallel MRK 9:3; MAT 28:3; MRK 16:5; JHN 20:12; REV 1:14

Light

1JN 1:7 See also JOB 25:5; EZK 1:27; 2CO 6:14; EPH 5:8–5:9

Washing

PSA 26:6 See also PSA 51:2

Fire

DAN 7:9–7:10 See also ISA 33:14; EZK 8:2; REV 1:14–1:15

title: 8328: quietness
content:
A calm, peaceful and restrained attitude to life and way of approaching God frequently commended in Scripture even in adverse circumstances. It is also a condition experienced by God's friends and enemies when confronted by his majesty.

Quietness of life

A quiet manner of life commended

1TI 2:1–2:2 See also PSA 35:20, PSA 131:1–131:2; MAT 12:19; ISA 42:2; 1TH 4:11; 2TH 3:12; 1TI 2:11; 1PE 3:1–3:4

A quiet temperament

GEN 25:27

Quiet activity

MAT 1:19 See also JDG 4:21; RUT 3:7; EZK 24:17; ACT 16:37

The wisdom of being quiet

AMO 5:13 See also GEN 34:5; JDG 18:19–18:20; EST 7:4; PRO 15:18; ECC 9:17; ACT 19:35–19:36

Quietness in different circumstances

In peace and rest

PSA 23:2 See also 1CH 4:40; PRO 17:1; ISA 32:17; MRK 6:31

After conflict

1CH 22:9 See also JOS 11:23, JOS 14:15; JDG 3:11, JDG 5:31, JDG 8:28; 2CH 14:1, 2CH 20:30; ISA 14:7; JER 30:10 parallel JER 46:27; ZEC 1:11

When in distress

2SA 13:20; ; NEH 8:9–8:11; ; ISA 7:4

Because of a sense of shame

GEN 3:8; ; NEH 5:8; ; MRK 9:34

When before a higher authority

JDG 3:19; ; MRK 1:25 parallel LUK 4:35

God's quiet voice

1KI 19:12–19:13

Absence of quietness

Because of inner conflict

JOB 3:26 See also RUT 3:18; JOB 6:24; ROM 7:21–7:24

Because of sin

ISA 57:20–57:21

The quietness of God

God chooses quietness

ISA 18:4 See also JOB 34:29; ISA 42:14; EZK 16:42

God rejects quietness

ISA 62:1

God brings quietness

PSA 76:8 See also PSA 46:10, PSA 65:7, PSA 89:9, PSA 107:29; ISA 24:8, ISA 25:5; ZEP 3:17; MAT 8:26 parallels MRK 4:39, LUK 8:24

Quietness before God

Being quiet before God

PSA 37:7; ISA 30:15 See also EXO 14:14; LAM 3:26; 1CO 14:28, 1CO 14:34–14:35; REV 8:1

Quietness in prayer

MAT 6:6 See also NEH 2:4; MRK 6:46 parallel MAT 14:23; LUK 5:16, LUK 6:12, LUK 9:18

Quietness as calmness

In contrast with the storm

MAT 8:26 parallels MRK 4:39, LUK 8:24 See also PSA 107:30; JON 1:11–1:15

In contrast with rashness

ECC 10:4 See also PRO 15:18

In contrast with unrest

ISA 7:4 See also NEH 8:11

In contrast with anger

EZK 16:42

title: 8329: readiness
content:
A state of preparedness for future needs or happenings, whether predictable or uncertain. God through Jesus Christ prepared all that was necessary for the salvation of sinners. God's people are exhorted to be ready for warfare (physical and spiritual), death and the second coming of Jesus Christ. All humanity should be ready for future judgment.

God has prepared everything for the salvation of sinners

MAT 22:4 A wedding banquet is often used to portray the blessings of salvation and the gathering of Jesus Christ with the redeemed in heaven. See also LUK 14:16–14:17; 1PE 1:5

Exhortations to and descriptions of readiness for war

Against earthly enemies

JOL 3:9–3:10 See also 1KI 20:12; 1CH 12:23–12:35, 1CH 12:33–12:37; 2CH 25:5; JER 51:11–51:12; DAN 11:10

Against spiritual forces of evil

EPH 6:11–6:18

God's people should always be ready

To face temptation

1PE 5:8 See also PSA 39:1; MAT 26:41 parallels MRK 14:38, LUK 22:46; 1CO 10:12

To face death

2KI 20:1 parallel ISA 38:1 See also GEN 46:30; ACT 21:13

To serve

EPH 4:11–4:12; 1PE 1:13 See also NUM 8:11; 1SA 25:41; JHN 9:4; 2CO 8:19, 2CO 9:2; 2TI 2:21; TIT 3:1

To speak the truth

1PE 3:15 See also PRO 22:17–22:18; JER 1:17; 2TI 4:2

For the second coming of Chirst

1JN 2:28 See also MAT 24:42–24:44, MAT 24:45–24:51 parallel LUK 12:42–12:46; MAT 25:1–25:12, MAT 25:13; MRK 13:33–13:37; LUK 12:35–12:40; 1TH 5:8; REV 3:11, REV 16:15, REV 19:7

All humanity should be ready for future judgment

LUK 12:47–12:48 This is one of many parables that Jesus Christ taught about his second coming and the need to be ready when he returns. See also AMO 4:12; 1PE 4:5

title: 8330: receptiveness
content:
An openness to people and ideas which needs to be tempered by discernment. It is an attitude which God desires and which he shows to all who call to him.

Receptiveness as a human quality

It is characterised by an open attitude

MAT 13:16–13:17 See also PRO 18:15, PRO 20:12

It is an aspect of love

JHN 19:26–19:27 See also RUT 4:3–4:5, RUT 4:13; MAT 18:5 parallels MRK 9:37, LUK 9:48; MAT 25:35; ACT 2:44–2:45, ACT 4:32; 1CO 13:6–13:7; GAL 4:14

Thoughtful receptiveness requires discernment

1JN 4:1 See also 1CO 2:14; PHP 1:10; 1TH 5:21; HEB 5:14

Thoughtless receptiveness is dangerous

2CO 11:3–11:4 See also DEU 11:16; 1KI 11:4; PRO 7:21; COL 2:8; HEB 13:9; 2JN 1:10

Spiritual receptiveness is fruitful

JHN 15:5 See also PSA 1:3; PRO 3:5–3:6, PRO 6:20–6:22; JER 17:7–17:8; JHN 20:29

God is receptive to human beings

To their needs

MAT 9:36 See also 2KI 14:26; PSA 103:13–103:14; ISA 63:9; MAT 6:8, MAT 15:32 parallel MRK 8:2–8:3; LUK 7:13; 1PE 5:7

To their cries

PSA 38:9 See also EXO 3:7; 1KI 9:3 parallel 2CH 7:12; PSA 6:8–6:9, PSA 40:1; ISA 65:24; 1PE 3:12

To their repentance

HOS 14:1–14:4 See also 2SA 12:13; EZK 18:27–18:28; JOL 2:13; JON 3:10, JON 4:2; LUK 15:7, LUK 15:10, LUK 18:13–18:14

God's receptiveness may be withdrawn

ZEC 7:13 See also PSA 66:18; PRO 21:13; ISA 59:2; JER 11:11; MAT 7:23, MAT 27:46 parallel MRK 15:34; PSA 22:1; JAS 1:7

People should be receptive to God

Spiritual receptiveness begins by receiving Jesus Christ

JHN 1:12–1:13 See also MAT 10:40; ACT 2:41, ACT 16:14; COL 2:6

Spiritual receptiveness requires openness to God's Spirit

1CO 2:12–2:16 See also ROM 8:5, ROM 8:16; 1CO 7:40; GAL 5:16, GAL 5:25; REV 2:7

Receptiveness involves seeking and listening

ISA 50:4–50:5 See also DEU 4:29; 1CH 28:9; PSA 119:11; PRO 8:34; MAT 7:8 parallel LUK 11:10; LUK 10:39; EPH 1:18; JAS 1:19

title: 8331: reliability
content:
The quality of consistency and dependability which is the basis for confidence and reliance. It is exemplified by God in his changelessness and is required of God's people in their service and witness. Scripture gives warning, too, of those things which may prove unreliable.

title: 8333: reverence
content: The proper sense of awe, respect and wonder that is inspired and demanded by an encounter with, or meditation upon, the character and activity of the living God.

content:

title: 8341: separation
content:
A setting apart. Separation is at the heart of the biblical idea of holiness. God is separate from his creation and has set apart his people from the world. Sin causes alienation between God and humanity, making necessary the reconciling work of Jesus Christ. The end of the age will bring the final separation between the righteous and the wicked.

title: 8342: servanthood
content: The state of being the servant of others, especially of God. Scripture stresses the privileges and responsibilities of being a servant of God and points to Jesus Christ as the model of servanthood.

title: 8343: servanthood, in society
content:
Servants and slaves were an important feature of everyday life in biblical times. The idea of servanthood is used both literally and metaphorically throughout Scripture.

Laws of servanthood

EXO 21:2–21:6 parallel DEU 15:12–15:18 The words “servant” and “slave” are the same in Hebrew, but according to OT law, an Israelite servant was to be accorded more rights than a foreign slave. See also GEN 17:13; EXO 12:44, EXO 20:10 parallel DEU 5:14; LEV 25:39–25:55; DEU 21:10–21:14, DEU 29:10–29:11; 1CH 2:34–2:35

title: 8347: spiritual growth
content: Scripture uses a number of images to emphasise that believers are meant to grow in their faith, understanding, holiness and commitment. It also provides advice on how this may be achieved.

title: 8348: spiritual growth, nature of
content:

title: 8356: unselfishness
content:
Putting the concerns and interests of others before one's own. Jesus Christ was the supreme example of this and believers should follow his example, denying themselves in order to serve others.

In his life and work

JHN 5:30; ROM 15:3 See also MAT 15:32; JHN 13:3–13:5; 2CO 8:9

In his dying for others

MAT 20:26–20:28 parallel MRK 10:43–10:45PHP 2:5–2:8 See also ISA 53:3–53:12; JHN 10:17–10:18; ROM 5:6–5:8; 1CO 15:3; 2CO 5:14; 1TH 5:10; 1PE 2:22–2:24, 1PE 3:18; 1TI 2:6

content: A lack of strength, whether physical or spiritual. Scripture attributes weakness to human sin and foolishness and urges believers to find their true strength in God alone.

Divine action

GEN 32:25 Through wrestling with God, Jacob carried a physical reminder for the rest of his life. See also GEN 32:32; HEB 11:21

Disobedience

title: 8361: wisdom
content: The quality of knowledge, discernment and understanding characteristic of God himself. True wisdom, seen in the ministry of Jesus Christ, is a gift of the Holy Spirit. Scripture affirms that true human wisdom is a gift from God and points out the folly of trusting in mere human wisdom.

title: 8365: wisdom, nature of human
content:
The human quality which enables the planning and successful achievement of a desired goal. It may be expressed as technical skill, practical instruction and astuteness in political affairs. True wisdom includes spiritual discernment and, above all, the reverence and knowledge of God.

title: 8366: wisdom, source of human
content:
True wisdom belongs to God and may be given by him alone. It cannot be received by those who put confidence in worldly wisdom which is based upon human cleverness and insight without God's revelation and which will come to nothing.

True wisdom comes from God

content:

title: 8401: challenges
content:
God makes demands on his people and, often through spiritual leaders, confronts believers with their sin. He also calls to account false gods and those who exalt themselves against him. The wicked vainly challenge God by questioning his authority, seeking to resist his power and opposing his people.

title: 8402: claims
content:
The assertion of rights and recognition due. God as Creator and Redeemer makes claims on his world and on his people. The claims of Jesus Christ about himself as God and Messiah call for a response. title: 8403: commands
content: Demands made of his people, or obligations laid upon his people, by God. Scripture stresses that being the people of God involves responsibilities as well as privileges, and sets out the demands which God justly makes of his people.

title: 8408: decision-making
content: The ability to arrive at a decision after due consideration of all the factors involved. The Christian life involves making decisions at many levels. Scripture offers guidance concerning how such decisions should be made, and provides examples of good and bad decision-making.

content:

content: Giving someone confidence and courage to do something. Scripture encourages believers to trust in God and to rely on the enabling of the Holy Spirit.

title: 8424: evangelism
content: The proclamation of the good news of Jesus Christ, which arises naturally from believers' love for God and appreciation of all that God has done for them. The NT stresses the importance of evangelism, and provides guidance as to how it should be carried out.

Evangelising households

ACT 16:34 The conversion of the head of the household was often accompanied by the conversion of the whole family group. See also JHN 4:53; ACT 11:14, ACT 18:8

Using literature in evangelism

JHN 20:30–20:31 See also LUK 1:1–1:4; ACT 1:1–1:2

Rejection of the message

HEB 4:2 See also ROM 10:16; ACT 13:50–13:51, ACT 17:32, ACT 18:6

title: 8428: example
content:
A person who acts as an illustration or model. Scripture provides examples of both good and bad conduct for the guidance of believers.

Scripture provides examples to inform and warn believers

Israel is an example to believers

1CO 10:6 See also 1CO 10:11

Job as an example of perseverance and patience

JAS 5:10–5:11

The example of Jesus Christ is of special importance to Christians

JHN 13:15; 1CO 11:1 See also MAT 11:29, MAT 16:24; PHP 2:5–2:11; 1TI 1:16; HEB 3:1–3:2, HEB 12:2; 1PE 2:21

The apostles set an example for believers to follow

PHP 3:17 See also 2TH 3:7

Christian leaders are to provide examples to their people

1PE 5:3; TIT 2:7 See also 1TI 4:12

Examples drawn from everyday life

GAL 3:15; ; JAS 3:4

Biblical examples to be imitated

Faith

MAT 15:22 a Canaanite woman; ; JHN 4:4–4:29 a Samaritan woman; ; JHN 20:24–20:29 doubting Thomas; ; ROM 4:18–4:21 Abraham; ; HEB 11:4–11:38 various OT figures

Forgiving one's enemies and assailants

GEN 33:1–33:11 Esau; ; GEN 45:5–45:15 Joseph; ; 1SA 24:8–24:22 David; ; LUK 23:34 Jesus Christ; ; ACT 7:59 Stephen

Generous giving

RUT 2:15–2:19 Boaz; ; JOB 29:11–29:16 Job; ; MRK 12:41–12:44 a widow; ; ACT 10:2 Cornelius

Praise

EXO 15:1–15:2 Moses; ; EXO 18:9–18:12 Jethro; ; 1CH 29:10–29:13 David; ; DAN 2:19–2:23 Daniel; ; LUK 1:57–1:68 Zechariah

title: 8429: fasting
content: Abstaining from food, and possibly drink, for a limited period of time as a mark of religious commitment and devotion or as an expression of repentance for sins.

title: 8430: fasting, nature of
content:
Scripture frequently refers to individuals fasting and describes the different kinds of fast which may be undertaken.

Kinds of fasting

Abstaining from food and drink

EZR 10:6 See also DAN 9:3; ACT 23:12

Abstaining from food only

1SA 1:7 See also DAN 6:18

The duration of fasting

One day: the normal fast period

LEV 23:32; ; JDG 20:26; ; 2SA 1:12

Three days

EST 4:16; ; ACT 9:9

Seven days

1SA 31:13 parallel 1CH 10:12; ; 2SA 12:16–12:20

Forty days

These 40-day fasts are all in unique circumstances and are not prescribed: EXO 34:28; ; 1KI 19:8; ; MAT 4:2 parallel LUK 4:2

Regular observances of fasting

Those prescribed by the Law

LEV 16:29–16:31 NIV footnote at verse 29. See also LEV 23:26–23:32; NUM 29:7; ACT 27:9

Those observed in Jewish tradition

ZEC 8:19 See also EST 9:30–9:31; ZEC 7:2–7:5

Those observed by the Pharisees

LUK 18:11–18:12

Involuntary fasts

Those imposed by decree

2CH 20:3 See also 1SA 14:241KI 13:8–13:9, 1KI 13:16 1KI 21:9; JER 36:9

Those imposed by circumstances

ACT 27:33; ; 2CO 6:5, 2CO 11:27

Voluntary fasts

NEH 1:4 See also LUK 2:37

title: 8431: fasting, reasons for
content:
Scripture identifies a number of situations in which fasting is appropriate.

Situations in which fasting is appropriate

Bereavement

1CH 10:11–10:12 parallel 1SA 31:11–31:13 See also 2SA 1:11–1:12, 2SA 3:31–3:35

Distress

EST 4:3 See also 1SA 1:7, 1SA 20:34; 1KI 21:4–21:6; PSA 109:24; DAN 6:18; ACT 27:33

Penitence

1SA 7:5–7:6 See also NEH 9:1–9:3; DAN 9:3–9:6 Daniel identifies himself with the sin of the people; DAN 9:20; JOL 1:13–1:14, JOL 2:12–2:15; JON 3:5–3:9

Seeking God's intervention

2SA 12:15–12:17 See also 2CH 20:2–20:4; EZR 8:21; EST 4:15–4:16; PSA 35:13–35:14

Seeking guidance

JDG 20:26–20:28 See also DEU 9:9 Moses fasts before the revelation of the Law; DAN 9:1–9:3, DAN 9:20–9:23, DAN 10:1–10:2, DAN 10:12; ACT 13:1–13:3 The church receives direction through the Holy Spirit while fasting.

Indicating earnestness

ACT 23:12–23:13

title: 8432: fasting, practice of
content:
Although fasting is a negative practice, it is not an end in itself but is to be undertaken for a positive purpose.

Fasting is not an end in itself

Fasting as empty ritual is condemned

JER 14:11–14:12 See also ISA 58:1–58:7; ZEC 7:4–7:7

Fasting as mere show is condemned

MAT 6:16–6:18 See also MAT 9:14–9:15 parallels MRK 2:18–2:20, LUK 5:33–5:35 Jesus Christ repudiated fasting for its own sake whilst granting that there is a time and a place for it.

Fasting imposed for false motives

1SA 14:24–14:30

Attitudes appropriate to fasting

Humility

PSA 35:13 See also 1KI 21:27–21:29; EZR 8:21; PSA 69:10

Repentance

1SA 7:6 See also NEH 9:1–9:3; JOL 1:13–1:14, JOL 2:12–2:15

Fasting and prayer

NEH 1:4 See also EZR 8:21–8:23; PSA 35:13; DAN 9:3; MAT 17:20 parallel MRK 9:29; LUK 2:37, LUK 5:33; ACT 13:3, ACT 14:23; 1CO 7:3–7:5 The motivation here is similar to that in abstaining from food.

Fasting and worship

ACT 13:2 See also LUK 2:37

title: 8434: giving
content: Dedicating or offering something or oneself to others or to God. Scripture stresses the importance of giving. The generosity and love of God in giving his only Son to die for his people is understood to lead to an obligation, on their part, to love God and others in return.

title: 8435: giving, of oneself
content:
The submission of the self to the will of God, in thanksgiving and service.

Jesus Christ's self-giving as an example to believers

1JN 3:16 See also MAT 16:24 parallels MRK 8:34, LUK 9:23; MRK 10:45; JHN 15:13; ROM 15:3; GAL 1:4; EPH 5:1–5:2, EPH 5:25; PHP 2:5–2:8; TIT 2:14

Why self-giving is reasonable service to God

God's people belong to him by creation

DEU 32:6 See also PSA 100:3; REV 4:11

God's people belong to him by redemption

1CO 6:19–6:20 See also REV 5:9

All good things are given by God

1CH 29:14 See also DEU 8:18; ACT 17:25; 1CO 4:7; 1TI 6:17

God's people giving themselves

To God

ROM 12:1 See also 2CO 8:5

To one another

2CO 8:5 See also 1CO 16:15

To holy living

ROM 6:19 See also PRO 23:26; ROM 12:1

To the service of God

1CO 15:58 See also JDG 5:2; 1CH 29:5; 2CH 17:16; PSA 40:7–40:8; ISA 6:8; ACT 6:4; ROM 1:9; 1TI 4:15

To a life of self-denial

LUK 14:33 See also MAT 16:24 parallels MRK 8:34, LUK 9:23; LUK 14:26; ROM 15:2; 1CO 8:13, 1CO 10:33; 2CO 12:15; PHP 3:8

To martyrdom

DAN 3:28 See also ACT 20:24, ACT 21:13; REV 12:11

Rewards of self-giving

MAT 10:39 See also MAT 19:27–19:29 parallels MRK 10:28–10:30, LUK 18:28–18:30; MRK 8:35 parallel LUK 17:33

The giving of thanks

PSA 50:23 See also 1CH 16:8; EPH 5:4; PHP 4:4–4:7; COL 2:7, COL 3:15; HEB 12:28

title: 8436: giving, of possessions
content:
Making one's possession available for God's service in the way in which he directs, as a practical recognition that all possessions come from him.

Ministries that require the giving of material possessions

The relief of the poor

PRO 28:27 See also LEV 25:25; DEU 15:7–15:8; ISA 58:7; MAT 19:21 parallels MRK 10:21, LUK 18:22; LUK 12:33; ROM 12:13; GAL 2:10

The support of God's servants

1TI 5:17–5:18 See also NUM 3:48, NUM 5:9; 2KI 4:8–4:10; MAT 10:10; GAL 6:6; PHP 4:15–4:18

The care of widows and orphans

JAS 1:27 See also DEU 26:12; RUT 2:5–2:12; 1TI 5:3–5:4

Obedience to God

2CO 9:7 See also EXO 30:11–30:16; LEV 12:6–12:8; DEU 14:28; MAL 3:8–3:10; MAT 22:21 parallels MRK 12:17, LUK 20:25; ROM 13:6–13:7

Gratitude for God's generosity

1CH 29:14 See also GEN 28:20–28:22; DEU 26:9–26:10; 1SA 1:27–1:28

1JN 3:17 See also 2CH 28:15; MAT 7:9–7:11; LUK 10:33–10:35

MAT 10:8 See also 2CO 8:8–8:9, 2CO 9:15

title: 8437: giving, of talents
content:
All human abilities and skills derive from God and are to be dedicated to his glory and the good of others.

1PE 4:11 See also EXO 35:10, EXO 35:25; 1KI 7:40; 1CH 9:13; PSA 33:2–33:3, PSA 137:4–137:5; 1CO 10:31

For the good of others

1PE 4:10 See also 1CO 12:7, 1CO 14:12; EPH 4:12

Rewards according to use or misuse of talents

MAT 25:21 See also MAT 25:23–25:30 parallel LUK 19:17–19:26

title: 8438: giving, of time
content:
People are stewards of a deposit of time given by God, and will be held responsible for the way in which they use it.

Time is governed by God

God determines every lifespan

JOB 14:5 See also PSA 31:15, PSA 74:16–74:17, PSA 139:16; ACT 17:26

God will demand an account of how time has been spent

ECC 3:17 See also MAT 12:36; 1PE 4:3–4:5

Time may be squandered

In ungodly living

1PE 4:3 See also JOL 2:25; EPH 2:2–2:3; COL 3:5–3:7

By neglecting God-given opportunities

JER 8:20 See also PRO 20:4; MAT 25:11–25:12; LUK 13:25, LUK 19:44; ACT 24:25; REV 2:21

Time may be saved

By understanding its brevity

PSA 90:12 See also JHN 12:35; 1CO 7:29–7:31

By remembering its uncertainty

JHN 9:4 See also ECC 8:5–8:7; JAS 4:13–4:15

By making the most of present opportunities

EPH 5:16 See also PSA 32:6; ECC 12:1; EST 4:14; MAT 4:17; MRK 1:15; 2CO 6:1–6:2; GAL 6:10; COL 4:5; HEB 3:7–3:13

PSA 119:164 See also PSA 4:4, PSA 55:17; LAM 3:40; DAN 6:10, DAN 6:13; MRK 1:35; 1CO 11:28

In work

PSA 104:23 See also EXO 20:9 parallel DEU 5:13; ROM 13:6

With one's family

DEU 24:5 See also DEU 6:7; ECC 9:9; 1TI 3:4

In fellowship

1CO 16:7 See also ACT 2:42, ACT 20:7; HEB 10:25

LUK 10:41–10:42 See also PSA 1:1–1:3; HAG 1:2–1:4; MAT 6:33; ACT 13:46–13:47, ACT 17:16–17:17

title: 8440: glorifying God
content:
The giving of glory to God through acts of praise and obedience. Believers are to glorify God in their lives, as Jesus Christ glorified him in his life.

Believers are to glorify God

PSA 96:1–96:9 parallel 1CH 16:23–16:29ISA 42:12 See also ISA 43:5–43:7, ISA 66:18–66:19; HAB 2:14

God is entitled to be glorified

PSA 96:4–96:9 parallel 1CH 16:25–16:29 See also PSA 29:1–29:2, PSA 115:1; ISA 24:14–24:15

Glorifying God is the believer's natural response to him

PSA 118:28 See also PSA 34:3, PSA 69:30, PSA 86:12

God is glorified in Jesus Christ

JHN 13:31 See also JHN 14:13, JHN 17:4

Reasons for glorifying God

His holiness

PSA 99:9 See also REV 15:4

His great deeds

PSA 86:8–86:10 See also ISA 25:1; 2CO 4:13–4:15

His loving mercy

PSA 63:3 See also PSA 115:1; ROM 15:8–15:9

His righteous judgments

REV 14:7 See also EZK 28:22–28:23; ROM 11:33–11:36; REV 11:13

Means of glorifying God

By praising God

REV 4:11, REV 7:12 See also LUK 2:13; ROM 11:33–11:36, ROM 16:27; HEB 13:20–13:21; 1PE 4:11; 2PE 3:18; JUD 1:25

By living for God

1CO 10:31 See also ROM 4:20; 1CO 6:20; 2TH 1:11–1:12; 1PE 4:10–4:13

By doing good works and bearing fruit

JHN 15:8; PHP 1:9–1:11 See also MAT 5:16; GAL 5:22–5:26; HEB 13:20–13:21; 1PE 2:12

1CH 29:10–29:13 David; ; DAN 4:34–4:37 Nebuchadnezzar; ; LUK 1:46 Mary, the mother of Jesus Christ; ; LUK 2:13 the angels; ; LUK 2:20 the shepherds; JHN 13:31–13:32, JHN 17:1–17:4; REV 4:11, REV 7:12

title: 8441: goals
content:
Jesus Christ's basic aim was to do his Father's will. Believers have the same objective, which Jesus Christ and the Holy Spirit enable them to achieve.

God's goals

To live with his people

LEV 26:11–26:12 See also PSA 23:6; ZEC 2:10; JHN 14:23; REV 21:3

To build his church in Christ

MAT 16:18 See also EPH 2:19–2:22; REV 21:2

To perfect his church in Christ

EPH 5:26–5:27 See also PSA 138:8; PHP 1:6; COL 2:10

Jesus Christ's goals

To do his Father's will

JHN 6:38 See also MAT 26:39 parallels MRK 14:36, LUK 22:42; JHN 4:34, JHN 5:30; HEB 10:7, HEB 10:9

To preach the gospel

LUK 4:43 parallel MRK 1:38 See also LUK 4:18–4:19; ISA 61:1–61:2

To save the lost

LUK 19:10 See also MAT 15:21–15:28 parallel MRK 7:24–7:30; LUK 15:7 parallel MAT 18:14; LUK 15:10

Jesus Christ achieved his goals

JHN 17:4 See also LUK 13:32; JHN 12:31, JHN 19:28, JHN 19:30

Believers' goals

To please God

2CO 5:9 See also ROM 14:18; EPH 5:10, EPH 5:17; COL 1:9–1:10

To know God

PHP 3:8 See also JHN 17:3; PHP 3:10; 2PE 3:18

To be faithful to Jesus Christ

JHN 15:4 See also MAT 10:22 parallel MRK 13:13; MAT 24:13; PHP 3:14; 2TI 4:7; HEB 12:2; REV 2:26

To love one another

JHN 13:34 See also MAT 22:34–22:40 parallels MRK 12:28–12:31, LUK 10:25–10:28; JHN 15:12; 1CO 13:13, 1CO 16:14; 1TI 1:5; 1JN 4:11–4:12

To live at peace

ROM 12:18 See also MRK 9:50; 2CO 13:11; 1TH 4:11

To spread the gospel

MAT 28:19–28:20 See also ACT 20:24; ROM 11:14, ROM 15:20; 1CO 9:16; 2TI 4:2

To grow to maturity

EPH 4:13 See also MAT 5:48; ROM 8:29; 2CO 3:18, 2CO 7:1, 2CO 13:11

REV 7:9–7:10 See also JHN 6:40; 1CO 15:51–15:52; 2CO 5:4–5:5; 1TH 4:17; 1JN 3:2

JHN 14:2–14:3 See also JHN 6:39; ROM 8:38–8:39; EPH 1:13–1:14; PHP 1:6; 2TI 1:12, 2TI 2:11–2:13; REV 3:5, REV 3:21

title: 8442: good works
content:
Acts designed specifically to benefit others, which are characteristic of God. He requires and enables his people to do good, although such is contrary to their sinful human nature. Salvation does not depend on good works, but leads to them.

Good works are characteristic of God

JER 32:36–32:40 See also PSA 119:17, PSA 119:65, PSA 125:1–125:4; JER 32:41; MIC 2:7; ZEC 8:14–8:15; ACT 10:37–10:38

Good works are unnatural for sinful human beings

JER 13:23 See also PSA 5:9, PSA 10:7, PSA 14:1–14:3 parallel PSA 53:1–53:3; PSA 36:1–36:4, PSA 140:3; ECC 7:20; ISA 59:7–59:8; JER 4:22; ROM 3:9–3:18, ROM 7:13–7:23

God's people are encouraged to do good works

GAL 6:9–6:10 See also PSA 37:3; ECC 3:12; MAT 5:38–5:48 parallel LUK 6:27–6:36; 1PE 3:8–3:13; PSA 34:12–34:16; 1PE 4:19

God is pleased with the good works of his people

HEB 13:16 See also 1PE 2:20, 1PE 2:15, 1PE 3:17

Good works will be rewarded

JHN 5:28–5:29 See also LUK 6:35; ROM 2:5–2:11; GAL 6:9–6:10; 1TI 6:17–6:19

Good works as evidence of repentance

PSA 34:14 See also PSA 37:27; 2TI 2:20–2:21; JAS 2:14–2:21, JAS 2:26, JAS 3:13; 1PE 3:10–3:12

Good works as evidence of God's grace in the lives of believers

2CO 9:8 See also ACT 9:36; PHP 2:12–2:13; COL 1:10–1:12

Good works are the purpose of the new creation

EPH 2:10 See also 2TI 2:21, 2TI 3:16–3:17; 1PE 2:13–2:15

MAT 12:9–12:14 parallels MRK 3:1–3:6, LUK 6:6–6:11 See also LUK 13:10–13:17; JHN 9:1–9:41

content:
The process of development and maturing, used to refer to the progress of the kingdom of God and the spiritual development of believers. Scripture uses images of growth (such as seeds, plants and infants) to stress the dynamic nature of personal faith and the kingdom of God.

Images of growth

Infancy to maturity

EPH 4:13–4:15 See also 1CO 3:1–3:2, 1CO 13:11, 1CO 14:20; HEB 5:12–5:14; 1PE 2:2

Seeds and plants

LUK 8:14–8:15 parallels MAT 13:22–13:23, MRK 4:19–4:20 See also 2CO 9:10

The apostles worked and prayed for growth in believers

2CO 13:9 See also COL 1:28, COL 4:12

In faith

2CO 10:15–10:16 See also 2TH 1:3

In knowledge

2PE 3:18 See also EPH 1:17–1:18, EPH 3:16–3:19; COL 1:10; 2PE 1:3, 2PE 1:6

In love

1TH 4:10 See also PHP 1:9; 1TH 3:12; 2PE 1:7–1:8

Growth comes from God

COL 2:19 See also 1CO 3:6–3:7; 2CO 9:10; PHP 1:6

1PE 2:1 See also ROM 8:13–8:14; 2CO 7:1; GAL 5:24; EPH 4:22–4:24; COL 3:5–3:10

Moving on from basic teaching

HEB 6:1–6:2 See also HEB 5:11–5:14

1CO 14:20 See also ROM 12:1

Persevering in faith

JAS 1:4 See also PHP 2:12, PHP 3:12; 2PE 1:5–1:8

Contributing to growth in the church by exercising gifts

EPH 4:11–4:12 See also 1CO 14:1–14:5; EPH 4:13–4:16

COL 1:6 See also MAT 13:31–13:33 parallels MRK 4:30–4:32, LUK 13:18–13:21; MRK 4:26–4:29

ACT 4:4 See also ACT 2:41, ACT 2:47, ACT 5:14, ACT 6:7, ACT 9:31, ACT 11:21, ACT 14:1, ACT 16:5

title: 8444: honouring God
content:
Giving the reverence and respect to God which is his due. All God's people have a duty to honour him in every aspect of their lives, while unbelievers and even animals can also honour him.

NUM 27:12–27:14 See also NUM 20:7–20:12

1SA 2:27–2:30 See also LEV 10:1–10:3; 2CH 26:18; JHN 12:26

title: 8445: hospitality
content: Acts of generosity and friendship towards strangers. God's people are called to be hospitable as part of their duty to others and in gratitude for the salvation they have received from God. Showing hospitality includes the responsibility to protect those received as guests.

resource.label: 8446: hospitality, a duty of God's people

title: 8446: hospitality, a duty of God's people
content:
Hospitality is commanded by God

HEB 13:2 See also ISA 58:6–58:7; JHN 13:12–13:15; ROM 12:13; 1PE 4:9

Hospitality is a responsibility of leaders

1TI 3:2 See also 1TI 5:9–5:10; TIT 1:8

Hospitality indicates true discipleship

JOB 31:32 See also MAT 25:35

Hospitality crosses social barriers

Of race

LEV 19:33–19:34 See also EXO 22:21, EXO 23:9

Of class and status

LUK 14:12–14:14 See also JAS 2:2–2:4

Hospitality is to be offered to Christian ministers

ROM 16:1–16:2 See also COL 4:10; 3JN 1:5–1:10

Hospitality is to be refused to false teachers

2JN 1:10–1:11

PSA 23:5–23:6; REV 3:20 Jesus Christ comes as a willing guest to the repentant, as a sign of renewed fellowship. See also ISA 25:6; MAT 22:1–22:14; LUK 14:15–14:24, LUK 19:1–19:10; JHN 14:2–14:3

DEU 23:3–23:4 See also MAT 10:14 parallels MRK 6:11, LUK 9:5; MAT 25:41–25:45

title: 8447: hospitality, examples of
content:
Scripture provides many examples of friendship and generosity towards strangers, and encourages believers to be hospitable in turn.

Examples of hospitality in the OT

GEN 18:2–18:5 See also GEN 19:1–19:3 Lot entertains visitors from God; GEN 24:22–24:25 Abraham's servant is welcomed in Rebekah's home; EXO 2:20 Moses is welcomed by a priest of Midian; JDG 13:15 Manoah receives the angel of the LORD.JDG 19:1–19:4, JDG 19:20–19:21 2SA 17:27–17:29 hospitality shown to David and his people; 1KI 17:7–17:16 The widow of Zarephath cares for Elijah despite her poverty; 2KI 4:8–4:10 a Shunammite provides for Elisha; NEH 5:17 Nehemiah shows hospitality to fellow Jews.

Hospitality shown to Jesus Christ

MAT 9:10 parallels MRK 2:15, LUK 5:29 Jesus Christ received hospitality from people of all social backgrounds. See also MAT 8:14–8:15 parallels MRK 1:29–1:31, LUK 4:38–4:39 at Peter's houseMAT 26:6–26:7 parallel MRK 14:3; JHN 12:1–12:3 LUK 7:36 at the house of Simon the Pharisee; LUK 10:38 at the home of Mary and Martha; LUK 14:1 at the house of a prominent Pharisee; LUK 19:5–19:7 at Zacchaeus' house; LUK 24:29 with disciples in Emmaus; JHN 2:2 at the wedding at Cana

Hospitality assisted the mission of the apostles

Hospitality shown to the disciples

MAT 10:11–10:12 parallels MRK 6:10, LUK 9:4 Jesus Christ sends out the Twelve. See also LUK 10:5–10:7

ACT 10:32 at the home of Simon the tanner; ; ACT 10:48 with Cornelius and his family

ACT 16:15 at the home of Lydia; ; ACT 16:34 at the house of the Philippian jailer; ; ACT 18:2–18:3 with Aquila and Priscilla in Corinth; ; ACT 21:8 at the house of Philip; ; ACT 21:16 at the home of Mnason in Jerusalem; ; ACT 28:2 on Malta; ; ACT 28:7 at the home of Publius; ; ROM 16:23 with Gaius; ; PHM 1:22 as a guest of Philemon

1CO 16:19 See also ACT 2:46; ROM 16:3–16:5; COL 4:15; PHM 1:2

title: 8449: imitating
content:
Following the example or copying the actions of another person. Christians are called upon to become Christlike. Becoming like Jesus Christ is, however, the result, not the condition, of conversion.

The people of God are to imitate God

LEV 11:44–11:45 See also LEV 19:2, LEV 20:7, LEV 20:26, LEV 21:8; 1PE 1:16; EPH 5:1

The people of God are to imitate Jesus Christ

Jesus Christ is the example for believers

MAT 16:24 parallels MRK 8:34, LUK 9:23JHN 13:15 See also MAT 11:29; JHN 13:34; ROM 13:14; 1CO 11:1; EPH 5:2; PHP 2:5; COL 3:13; 1PE 2:21, 1PE 4:1

God works in believers making them like Jesus Christ

ROM 8:29 See also 2CO 4:10–4:12; COL 3:9–3:10

Good examples to imitate

Paul's example

1CO 4:16 See also 1CO 11:1; PHP 3:17, PHP 4:9; 1TH 1:6; 2TH 3:7–3:9

2CO 9:2; ; 1TH 2:14; ; HEB 6:12

Christian leaders are to set examples which can be imitated

1TI 4:12 See also TIT 2:7–2:8; HEB 13:7; 1PE 5:3

HEB 12:1; ; JAS 5:10–5:11

God's people are not to imitate bad examples

Israel must not imitate other nations

LEV 20:23; ; DEU 18:9; ; 2KI 17:15

God's people must not imitate the ungodly

EXO 23:2; ; PSA 1:1; ; PRO 1:10–1:15; ; MAT 23:2–23:3; ; 1CO 15:33; ; 2PE 3:17; ; 1JN 3:11–3:12; ; REV 2:14

No-one can obtain salvation by imitating Jesus Christ

JHN 3:16–3:18 Jesus Christ teaches that salvation (eternal life) is a consequence of faith in him. He never links salvation with imitating him or any other act or acts. See also EPH 2:8–2:9; 2TI 1:8–1:9

title: 8450: martyrdom
content:
The term “martyr” comes from the Greek word for “witness”, reminding believers that the supreme act of witness for the gospel is to give up one's life for its sake.

Jesus Christ as martyr

Jesus Christ had to suffer and die

MRK 8:31 In that Jesus Christ gives up his life, he may be thought of as a martyr. But the NT stresses that he is far more than this. Through his death alone come all the benefits of salvation, in which all believers can share. See also ISA 53:10

Jesus Christ's life is given as a ransom for believers

MAT 20:28 parallel MRK 10:45 See also LUK 9:22; JHN 10:11; ACT 2:23

MAT 14:10–14:12 parallel MRK 6:27–6:29

title: 8451: mortification
content:
The act of self-denial or the “putting to death” of sinful instincts in order to have freedom from sin and to live in the power of the Holy Spirit. The NT stresses that this act of humiliation comes about through the grace of God. It is the result of, not the condition for, conversion.

Examples of mortification through humility

2SA 10:1–10:5 See also MAT 27:3–27:5

Examples of mortification through self-denial

LEV 16:29–16:31 See also EXO 19:15; LEV 23:27–23:32; NUM 29:7

Mortification as the basis for discipleship

Self-denial is essential

MRK 8:34–8:35 parallels MAT 16:24–16:25, LUK 9:23–9:24 See also 1JN 3:16

The necessity of putting to death sinful human nature and the world's values

ROM 8:13; COL 3:5 See also MAT 5:29–5:30; GAL 5:24, GAL 6:14; 1PE 2:11

Dying to self is a means of knowing freedom from sin

ROM 6:6–6:7 See also EPH 4:22–4:23

The importance of sharing in the death of Christ

GAL 2:20 See also ROM 6:3, ROM 7:4; 2CO 4:11–4:12; PHP 3:10; COL 2:20; 2TI 2:11

The example of Paul

1CO 9:27 See also 2CO 11:23–11:33; GAL 6:17

Mortification is not the same as self-infliction

COL 2:23 See also PHP 3:2–3:3; COL 2:20–2:22; 1TI 4:1–4:5

resource.label: 2363: Jesus Christ, preaching and teaching of

title: 8453: obedience
content: A willingness to submit to the authority of someone else and to actually do what one is asked or told to do. Scripture lays particular emphasis upon the need for believers to obey God, stressing his trustworthiness. This obedience is especially clear in the life and death of Jesus Christ.

title: 8454: obedience, to God
content:
A willingness to submit oneself to the will of God and to put it into effect. Scripture emphasises the necessity for God's laws to be followed, gives examples and reasons, and describes the rewards.

Obedience is demanded of God's people

LEV 25:18; 1SA 15:22 See also DEU 26:16, DEU 32:46; ROM 6:16–6:18; 1PE 1:14–1:16

Examples of obedience in the OT

JOS 11:15 See also GEN 6:22, GEN 12:1–12:4, GEN 22:2–22:3; EXO 40:16; JON 3:3

The example of Jesus Christ

MAT 26:39 parallels MRK 14:36, LUK 22:42JHN 14:31 See also JHN 17:4; ROM 5:19; PHP 2:8; HEB 5:8

Jesus Christ is obeyed

By the wind and the waves

MAT 8:26–8:27 parallels MRK 4:39–4:41, LUK 8:24–8:25

By evil spirits

MRK 1:27 parallel LUK 4:36

Obedience and love

JHN 14:15; 1JN 5:3 See also PSA 119:167; 1JN 2:5, 1JN 3:10; 2JN 1:6

Obedience and faith

HEB 11:8; MAT 7:21 Obedience to the will of God demonstrates the reality of a person's faith in Jesus Christ. See also ROM 1:5; JAS 2:14–2:26

God rewards those who obey him

EXO 19:5; JHN 15:10 See also DEU 5:29; 1KI 3:14; 2KI 18:5–18:7; MAT 7:21, MAT 7:24–7:25 parallel LUK 6:47–6:48; MAT 12:50 parallels MRK 3:35, LUK 8:21; JHN 12:26, JHN 14:21, JHN 14:23, JHN 21:4–21:6; 1JN 2:17

MAT 7:24–7:27; JAS 1:22 See also PSA 119:9–119:11; JON 3:3; LUK 11:28; JHN 17:6; JAS 2:14–2:20

Examples of people who obeyed God

GEN 6:9 Noah; GEN 12:1–12:4, GEN 17:23; PSA 119:30, PSA 119:100–119:106; ACT 4:19–4:20, ACT 5:29; PHP 3:7–3:14 Paul

content: See 2057: Jesus Christ, obedience of

content:
Scripture teaches that all people, Christians included, should submit not only to God himself but also to divinely instituted secular authorities.

Obedience is owed to rulers

ROM 13:1–13:7 See also 1TI 2:1–2:3; TIT 3:1; 1PE 2:13–2:14, 1PE 2:17

Jesus Christ expounds this principle

MRK 12:17 parallels MAT 22:21, LUK 20:25

HEB 13:17 See also 1PE 5:5

Obedience is owed within the household

EPH 6:1–6:3 See also PRO 15:5; COL 3:20

Jesus Christ sets the example

LUK 2:51

Obedience to secular authority is limited by obedience to God

ACT 5:29 See also ACT 4:19

content:
The commendation of peacemakers

MAT 5:9 See also PRO 12:20; ROM 14:19

The importance of pursuing peace

ECC 10:4; ; ROM 12:18; ; TIT 1:6; ; HEB 12:14; ; JAS 3:17

GEN 13:8–13:9 Abraham; ; 1SA 25:14–25:31 Abigail; ; EST 10:3 Mordecai; ; ISA 53:5 the suffering servant

title: 8459: perseverance
content:
Enduring in a course of action or belief. In its negative sense, it can mean being stubborn; in its positive sense, it means continuing commitment to the gospel of Jesus Christ.

Human perseverance in sin

2KI 17:41; ISA 1:5; ROM 1:32 See also EXO 9:1–9:3; DEU 29:19; JDG 14:17; 2KI 13:11; DAN 12:10

God's perseverance in calling Israel to obedience

NEH 9:30–9:31 See also EXO 32:14; 1KI 3:6; ISA 40:28; JER 26:13; JON 3:10

HEB 12:1–12:3 See also MAT 17:17 parallel MRK 9:19; 2TH 3:5

Christians' perseverance in faith

COL 2:6–2:7, COL 1:10–1:12 See also MAT 24:12–24:13, MAT 10:22; JHN 15:4–15:10; ROM 11:22; 1CO 1:8; 2CO 10:15; PHP 2:12; COL 1:23; 2TH 3:4; HEB 6:1, HEB 10:36–10:38; 2PE 3:18

content:

EXO 29:18; PHP 4:18 See also EXO 29:25, EXO 29:41; LEV 1:9, LEV 3:5; NUM 15:3, NUM 29:2; EZR 6:10; HEB 13:16

PRO 15:8

Doing God's will

HEB 13:20–13:21 See also MAT 7:21; EPH 6:6; 1JN 2:17
