NEH 5:19; PSA 19:14 See also EXO 32:11; NEH 13:31; PSA 90:17, PSA 104:34; DAN 9:17

GEN 6:8 Noah; EXO 33:12–33:13, EXO 33:17; DEU 33:23 Naphtali; ; 1SA 2:26 Samuel; ; 1KI 3:10 Solomon; ; LUK 1:30 Mary; ; HEB 11:5 Enoch

title: 8461: priorities
content: Scripture stresses that God must be allowed to rule at the heart of a person's life.

resource.label: 8463: priority, of faith, hope and love

title: 8462: priority, of God
content:
Scripture provides examples of individuals who have allowed God to take priority in their lives, and also of those who have allowed something or someone else to take priority.

God's glory made a priority

MAT 6:9

Commands to put God first

MAT 4:10 parallel LUK 4:8 See also DEU 6:13; 1CH 16:29

GEN 5:22, GEN 5:24 Enoch; ; GEN 6:9 Noah; ; GEN 12:4 Abraham; ; JOS 24:15 Joshua; ; 2KI 20:3 Hezekiah; ; DAN 3:16–3:18 Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego; ; DAN 6:10 Daniel; ; JHN 3:29–3:30 John the Baptist

title: 8463: priority, of faith, hope and love
content:
Putting God first--living according to his word--serves the glory of God and also the best interests of believers, by giving them true wisdom for daily living.

The wisdom of making faith a priority

HEB 11:6

Putting the fear of God before other considerations

PSA 31:19 See also EXO 1:17; NEH 5:15; PRO 1:7

Preferring God's way to sinful advice

PSA 1:1–1:2 PRO 3:13–3:14, PRO 8:19, PRO 8:32; NUM 31:16; ; 1KI 12:28

Choosing imaginative action rather than laziness or fearfulness

NUM 13:30 See also 1SA 25:33; EPH 5:16MAT 25:10, MAT 25:26–25:27, MAT 25:44–25:45, MAT 26:40

Patient waiting rather than impetuous action

PSA 40:1 See also PSA 27:14, PSA 37:5–37:6, PSA 62:5, PSA 123:2; PRO 3:5–3:6; ISA 40:31; HOS 12:6; JHN 2:4–2:5; REV 2:10

GAL 5:16 Merely “human” activity betrays a failure of love for God. See also PSA 147:10–147:11; ISA 31:1–31:3; ROM 8:5

Inner sincerity rather than outward appearance

ROM 12:9 See also 1SA 16:7; EPH 6:5; COL 3:22

Actions rather than mere words

JAS 2:18 See also MAT 7:21–7:22; 1JN 3:18

Peace rather than disharmony

ROM 12:18 See also ROM 14:19; HEB 12:14

Truth rather than falsehood

PRO 12:19 See also ACT 5:4; COL 3:9

title: 8465: progress
content:
The process of development and growth, of special importance in the life of believers. Scripture stresses the importance of progress, both of the individual believer and of the church, and the need to work towards that goal.

Progress in the Christian life should be expected

2CO 3:18; EPH 4:15 See also JOB 17:9; PSA 84:5, PSA 84:7, PSA 92:12; PRO 4:18; ROM 8:29–8:30

Believers are to strive for progress in their Christian lives

PHP 2:12 See also PSA 18:29; 1CO 9:24–9:27; PHP 3:12–3:14; 1TH 3:12; 2TH 1:3; 1TI 4:15; HEB 6:1; 1PE 2:2; 2PE 1:5–1:8, 2PE 3:18

Progress in the Christian life brings assurance

HEB 3:14 See also MAT 10:22 parallel MRK 13:13; MAT 24:13; HEB 6:9–6:11

The church is expected to progress

MAT 16:18, MAT 13:31–13:32 parallels MRK 4:30–4:32, LUK 13:18–13:19EPH 4:16 See also ACT 2:47, ACT 4:4, ACT 5:14, ACT 6:7, ACT 11:21

title: 8466: reformation
content:
The process of bringing religious practices and beliefs back into line with the word of God. The OT portrays Israel as requiring reformation at several points in her history. God's people continue to need to review their beliefs and practices in the light of God's word.

The continual need to turn from idolatry

1SA 7:3 Idolatry was the besetting sin of Israel and the point at which all reforms had to begin. See also GEN 35:2; JOS 24:14–24:24; JDG 6:25–6:27; 2KI 10:18–10:27, 2KI 11:17–11:18 parallel 2CH 23:16–23:17; 2CH 19:3, 2CH 33:15; 1CO 10:14; 1JN 5:21

The reform of Asa

He removed idols

1KI 15:12–15:13

He repaired the altar of the temple

2CH 15:8, 2CH 15:18

As a result the people sought and found God

2CH 15:9–15:15

The reform of Hezekiah

He removed idols and even local shrines dedicated to God

2KI 18:4 parallel 2CH 31:1

He established worship in the renovated and consecrated temple

2CH 29:3–29:7, 2CH 29:15–29:28

The covenant between God and his people was renewed

2CH 29:10–29:11, 2CH 29:29–29:31, 2CH 30:1–30:27, 2CH 31:2–31:19

The reform of Josiah

He repaired the temple

2KI 22:3–22:7 parallel 2CH 34:8–34:13

He ended false worship

2KI 23:4–23:24 parallel 2CH 34:3–34:7; ; 2CH 34:33

The results of Josiah's reform

2KI 22:11–22:20 parallel 2CH 34:19–34:28 The prevailing attitude was that God would ensure that no disaster would befall his chosen people. Now the need to turn from sin and complacency was reiterated and repentance ensued; ; 2KI 23:1–23:3 parallel 2CH 34:29–34:32; ; 2KI 23:3 parallel 2CH 34:31–34:32; ; 2KI 23:21–23:23 parallel 2CH 35:1–35:19

The reforms of Ezra and Nehemiah

The problem of intermarriage was dealt with

EZR 10:2–10:3 The objection to intermarriage was based on religious not racial grounds. It led to a corruption of the faith. See also EZR 9:1–9:15, EZR 10:5–10:17; NEH 13:23–13:27

The temple was purified

NEH 13:4–13:13

The Sabbath-rest was reaffirmed

NEH 13:15 See also NEH 13:16–13:22

Incomplete reforms

2KI 10:28–10:29 See also 1KI 15:14 parallel 2CH 15:17; 2KI 3:2–3:3, 2KI 12:2–12:3

The call to reform

To Israel

JER 7:3 See also 2CH 7:14; ISA 1:16–1:17, ISA 55:6–55:7; JER 18:11, JER 26:13, JER 35:15; ZEC 1:3; ACT 3:19–3:26

To the church

REV 3:2–3:3 See also 1CO 5:1–5:13; REV 2:5, REV 3:15–3:20

To individuals

JAS 1:21 See also ROM 12:2; 2CO 6:14–7:1; EPH 4:22–4:24; COL 3:5–3:10; JAS 1:22–1:25, JAS 4:7–4:10

title: 8467: reminders
content:
The means of calling to mind important matters or events. Scripture stresses the importance of being reminded of God's dealings with his people in the past.

The importance of being reminded of God's words and deeds

1CO 15:1; 2PE 1:12 See also 2PE 3:1

Reminders of God's covenant and faithfulness

GEN 9:12–9:16 See also GEN 17:9–17:14

Reminders of God's intervention in history

JUD 1:5 See also EXO 12:14–12:20 parallel DEU 16:1–16:8; EXO 13:3–13:10, EXO 17:14; 1CO 11:23–11:26; 2PE 1:12–1:16

Reminders to people of their sin or shortcomings

HEB 10:3–10:4 See also GEN 41:9; EXO 30:16; NUM 5:11–5:15; EZK 29:16

Reminders to people to be faithful to God

NUM 15:38–15:40 See also ROM 11:22; HEB 12:1–12:3; 2PE 3:1–3:2

Reminders to people of their potential and gifts from God

2TI 1:6 See also 1TI 4:14

Reminders to God's people on matters of faith and conduct

ROM 15:15 See also DEU 31:9–31:13; 1CO 4:17, 1CO 15:1–15:2; TIT 3:1–3:2

title: 8468: renunciation
content:
The deliberate rejection or disavowal, especially of a person or object.

Renunciation of the LORD

JDG 2:12; ISA 1:28; ACT 3:13 See also EXO 32:8; JOS 22:16; 2KI 22:17; 1CH 28:9; JER 5:19; MAT 24:10; 2TI 2:12

Renunciation of evil

In repentance

PSA 37:27 See also JER 35:15; EZK 14:6; DAN 4:27; 2CO 4:2; 1TI 6:20

To find God's mercy

2CH 7:14 See also PRO 28:13; EZK 18:21; JON 3:10

Self-renunciation and the Christian life

An integral part of discipleship

MAT 16:24 parallels MRK 8:34, LUK 9:23 See also MRK 10:28; LUK 5:28, LUK 14:33; PHP 3:8

The example of Jesus Christ

MRK 10:45 See also JHN 10:17; PHP 2:7–2:8

title: 8469: respect
content: An attitude of reverence and deference, reflecting an appreciation of the significance of the person or thing that is esteemed.

title: 8470: respect, for God's character
content:
God's revelation of himself calls for deference, honour and a response of right living.

Respect for God's name

PSA 29:2 See also EXO 20:7 parallel DEU 5:11; EXO 23:20–23:21; LEV 18:21, LEV 19:12, LEV 22:31–22:33, LEV 24:10–24:16; PSA 86:9–86:11; JER 3:16–3:17; MAL 2:1–2:2

Respect for God's presence

EXO 3:5–3:6 See also EXO 33:19–33:23; PSA 89:7; ISA 6:1–6:5; ZEP 1:7; ZEC 2:13

Respect for God's word

DEU 4:2 See also DEU 12:32; JOS 1:7–1:8; PRO 30:5–30:6; 2PE 1:19–1:21; REV 22:18–22:19

Respect for God's ark and sanctuary

LEV 19:30 See also 1SA 6:19–6:20; 2SA 6:1–6:7; ECC 5:1–5:2; HAB 2:20; MAT 21:12–21:13 parallels MRK 11:15–11:17, LUK 19:45–19:46, JHN 2:13–2:17; JER 7:11

Respect for God's servants

1TH 5:12–5:13 See also ACT 23:1–23:5; EXO 22:28; ACT 28:7–28:10; PHP 2:29–2:30; 1TI 5:17–5:18; HEB 13:7, HEB 13:17

Respect for God leads to godly living

EXO 20:20 See also 2CH 6:30–6:31; PRO 16:6; HEB 11:7; 1PE 1:14–1:17

title: 8471: respect, for human beings
content:
Each individual, created in the image of God, should be honoured and esteemed, and this should be worked out in every area of life.

Human beings are to be respected

They are made in the image of God

GEN 9:5–9:6 See also PRO 14:31, PRO 17:5; COL 3:9–3:11; JAS 3:9–3:10

The bounds of life belong to God

EXO 20:13 parallel DEU 5:17 See also EXO 21:22–21:25 NIV footnote at verse 22; 2SA 1:14–1:15, 2SA 4:9–4:12; 1KI 2:31–2:33; PSA 139:13–139:16

The equality and dignity of human beings is commanded

DEU 1:16–1:17 See also EXO 23:2–23:3; LEV 19:15; DEU 16:18–16:19; PRO 24:23–24:25, PRO 28:21; ACT 10:24–10:28, ACT 10:34–10:35; JAS 2:1–2:9; 1PE 2:17

Respect in the family

Respect for parents is commanded

EXO 20:12 parallel DEU 5:16 See also LEV 19:3; PRO 1:8; MAL 1:6; MAT 15:4–15:6 parallel MRK 7:10–7:13; MAT 19:19 parallel LUK 18:20; EPH 6:1–6:3; COL 3:20; HEB 12:9

Disrespect for parents is condemned

DEU 27:16 See also EXO 21:17; LEV 20:9; PRO 30:17; ISA 45:10; 2TI 3:1–3:2

Examples of those who respected their parents

GEN 9:20–9:23 Shem and Japheth; ; GEN 47:11–47:12 Joseph; ; 1SA 22:3 David; ; 1KI 2:19 Solomon; ; 1KI 19:20 Elisha; LUK 2:51; ; JHN 19:25–19:27

Respect in marriage

EPH 5:33 See also EPH 5:21–5:25; COL 3:18–3:19; 1PE 3:6–3:7

Respect for children

MAT 18:10 See also LEV 20:1–20:5; MAT 18:5–18:6 parallels MRK 9:36–9:37, LUK 9:47–9:48; MAT 19:13–19:15 parallels MRK 10:13–10:16, LUK 18:15–18:17; EPH 6:4; COL 3:20–3:21

Respect for leaders

Leaders must have gained respect

DEU 1:13–1:15 See also 1SA 9:6; PRO 31:23; 1TI 3:2–3:11

Leaders must be given respect

1SA 26:9–26:11 See also 1SA 24:1–24:7; 2KI 3:14; ROM 13:1–13:7; 1TH 5:12; HEB 13:17

Respect for old age

LEV 19:32 See also JOB 32:4–32:7; LAM 5:12; 1TI 5:1–5:2; TIT 2:2; 1PE 5:5

Respect at the place of work

DEU 24:14–24:15 See also LEV 19:13; EPH 6:5–6:9; COL 3:22–4:1; 1TI 6:1–6:2; 1PE 2:18

title: 8472: respect, for environment
content:
Although God created the universe and retains ultimate ownership of it, he has delegated responsibility for the well-being of the earth to the human race. This stewardship includes the care of the animal kingdom and the earth's natural resources.

God's creation is to be respected

The earth belongs to God

PSA 24:1–24:2 See also EXO 19:5–19:6; LEV 25:23; 1CH 29:14; PSA 50:9–50:12, PSA 89:11; HAG 2:8

Responsibility to rule and care for the earth has been delegated to the human race

GEN 1:26–1:28 See also GEN 9:1–9:3; PSA 8:6–8:8, PSA 115:16; HEB 2:8; JAS 3:7

God himself maintains a caring supervision of his creation

MAT 6:26–6:30 parallel LUK 12:24–12:28 See also DEU 11:10–11:15; PSA 65:9–65:13; MAT 5:45

Respect for all nature and animals

DEU 20:19 NIV footnote. See also EXO 23:4–23:5, EXO 23:10–23:11; DEU 22:4, DEU 22:6–22:7, DEU 25:4; PRO 12:10

Respect and care for the earth's natural resources

EXO 23:10–23:11 See also LEV 25:1–25:7; NEH 10:31

title: 8474: seeing God
content:
Perceiving God in all his fulness. Scripture stresses that God, as spirit, is invisible to sinful human beings. He has, however, been revealed in Jesus Christ, who is his perfect likeness, and he will be seen in all his glory at the end of history when he comes in judgment.

No human can see the face of God in all his fulness

1TI 6:15–6:16 See also DEU 4:10–4:12; JHN 6:46; 1TI 1:17; 1JN 4:12

Privileged individuals may catch a glimpse of God

EXO 33:21–33:23 See also GEN 16:13–16:14 Hagar; NUM 12:5–12:8 Moses; JDG 6:11–6:24 Gideon; JDG 13:2–13:23 Manoah and his wife

Threat of death on seeing the face of God

EXO 33:20 See also GEN 32:24–32:30; EXO 19:21, EXO 24:9–24:11

Seeing God in a vision

ISA 6:1 See also 1KI 22:19 parallel 2CH 18:18 Micaiah; EZK 1:1–1:28 Ezekiel; ACT 7:55–7:56 Stephen

God may be seen in Jesus Christ

JHN 14:8–14:9; COL 1:15 See also JHN 1:1–1:18; 1JN 5:20

The hope of seeing God at the resurrection

1CO 13:12 See also JOB 19:26–19:27; PSA 17:15; MAT 5:8; 1CO 13:12; HEB 12:14; REV 1:7

title: 8475: self-denial
content:
The willingness to deny oneself possessions or status, in order to grow in holiness and commitment to God. This practice is commended and illustrated by Jesus Christ himself, and underlies Christian fellowship within the church.

The wisdom of self-denial

PRO 23:20–23:21 See also PRO 25:16

Examples of self-denial in order to put God first

DAN 1:8; HEB 11:25 See also LEV 23:29; JER 35:6; DAN 10:3; LUK 1:15, LUK 7:33 parallel MAT 11:18

Self-denial is a requirement of following Jesus Christ

MAT 16:24 parallels MRK 8:34, LUK 9:23ACT 21:13; PHP 3:7; 1PE 2:11 See also MAT 5:29, MAT 6:10, MAT 9:9 parallels MRK 2:13–2:14, LUK 5:27–5:28 the calling of Matthew; MAT 10:37–10:38 parallel LUK 14:26–14:27 the cost of being a disciple; MAT 18:8 parallel MRK 9:43; MAT 19:21 parallel LUK 18:22 the rich young man; MAT 19:27 parallels MRK 10:28, LUK 18:28 Peter left everything to follow Jesus Christ; MAT 19:29 parallels MRK 10:29–10:30, LUK 18:29–18:30 the rewards of self-denial for the sake of the gospel; LUK 5:11, LUK 14:33, LUK 21:34; ACT 20:24; ROM 6:2, ROM 6:6, ROM 6:11, ROM 8:13, ROM 12:1, ROM 13:14; 1CO 6:12, 1CO 9:25–9:27; 2CO 8:5 the example of the Macedonian churches; GAL 2:20, GAL 5:16, GAL 5:23; COL 3:3, COL 3:5; 2TI 2:21; TIT 2:12–2:13; JAS 4:7; 1PE 4:2

Self-denial for the sake of others

RUT 2:11; PHP 2:4 Esther put her own life at risk for the sake of her people See also EXO 32:32; EST 4:16ROM 14:21, ROM 15:1; 1CO 8:13, 1CO 9:23 1CO 10:24, 1CO 10:33, 1CO 12:15; EPH 4:2, EPH 5:21; PHP 2:17, PHP 2:20–2:21 the example of Timothy; COL 1:24; 2TI 2:10; TIT 3:2; 1PE 3:8, 1PE 5:5

Self-denial and the example of Jesus Christ

MAT 26:39 parallels MRK 14:36, LUK 22:422CO 8:9 See also PSA 40:7; ISA 53:7; MAT 11:29; JHN 13:1–13:17; ROM 15:3; EPH 5:1–5:2; PHP 2:5–2:8

title: 8476: self-discipline
content:
The dedicated training, through the study of Scripture, prayer and self-control, which enables Christians to be more effective witnesses to the gospel, to lead lives more pleasing to God, and to win the crown that awaits those who are victorious over sin.

Self-discipline is training oneself to be godly

1TI 4:7 See also ROM 13:14; 1CO 9:24–9:27; EPH 4:23–4:24; PHP 3:12–3:14; COL 3:12; 2TI 1:7; HEB 5:14, HEB 12:1

Self-discipline and the study of Scripture

PSA 119:9–119:11; 2TI 3:16–3:17 See also DEU 29:29

Self-discipline involves learning through experience

TIT 2:12 See also ROM 5:3–5:5

Self-discipline should transform the whole person

A Christian's thoughts should be disciplined

2CO 10:5 See also ROM 12:3ROM 12:2; EPH 4:23 1PE 4:7

A Christian's speech should be disciplined

PSA 141:3 See also JAS 3:2–3:12

A Christian's behaviour should be disciplined

ROM 14:20–14:21

A Christian's body should be disciplined

1CO 9:27 See also ROM 6:12–6:13, ROM 8:13; EPH 4:22; COL 3:5; JAS 3:2

Self-discipline prevents God's discipline

1CO 11:31–11:32

Physical self-discipline is of some value, but only in this life

1TI 4:8 See also 1CO 9:25

An elder should be self-disciplined

TIT 1:8

Examples of those who exercised self-discipline

See also GEN 22:9–22:14 Abraham; GEN 39:8–39:12 Joseph; 2SA 11:11–11:13 UriahDAN 1:8, DAN 1:11–1:13 MAT 4:4 Jesus Christ; 1CO 8:13 Paul

Self-discipline strengthens believers when faced with temptation

MAT 5:29 parallel MRK 9:47; ; ROM 8:13; ; GAL 5:24

The reward for self-discipline is a crown and a prize

1CO 9:25 See also 1CO 9:24, 1CO 9:27; PHP 3:14; COL 2:18; 1TH 2:19; 2TI 4:8; JAS 1:12; 1PE 5:4; REV 2:10, REV 3:11

title: 8477: self-examination
content: Reflection on one's own character, motives and actions, in order to judge whether they are truly in accordance with Christian values.

title: 8478: self-examination, teaching on
content:
Self-examination should take place on the basis of God's revelation of himself and the example he sets believers in Jesus Christ. It is especially important before confessing one's sins.

The importance of self-examination

HAG 1:5 See also PSA 4:4, PSA 77:6; HAG 1:7, HAG 2:15, HAG 2:18; 1CO 11:28; 2CO 13:5; HEB 3:12

A lack of self-examination leads to pride and self-delusion

1CO 11:28–11:29 See also MAT 7:5; JHN 8:7; ROM 2:1–2:4

Self-examination is not easy because of humanity's fallen nature

PSA 19:12–19:14 See also JER 17:9

God helps believers in their self-examination

PSA 26:2 See also JOB 7:17–7:18, JOB 13:9, JOB 13:23; PSA 11:4–11:5, PSA 139:23–139:24; PRO 5:21; JER 17:10, JER 20:12

The purpose of self-examination is to lead people to God and amendment of life

LAM 3:40–3:42 See also PSA 42:5, PSA 42:11, PSA 43:5; JAS 1:23–1:25

Self-examination is especially important when ministering to others

GAL 6:1 See also ROM 14:4; GAL 6:3–6:4; 1TI 4:16; JAS 3:1

title: 8479: self-examination, examples of
content:
Scripture provides numerous examples of self-examination, and its results. In particular, self-examination is often portrayed as leading to repentance.

Self-examination in the experience of Israel

Self-examination at the entry into the promised land

JOS 7:1–7:26, JOS 24:14

Self-examination during the war with the Philistines

1SA 14:24–14:47

Self-examination at the time of the exile

JER 31:18–31:20

Self-examination after returning from exile in Babylon

NEH 8:9; ; HAG 1:5–1:12, HAG 2:15–2:19

Self-examination by other nations

JON 3:1–3:10

Self-examination in the experience of individuals

King David

PSA 51:3–51:6 See also 2SA 12:1–12:13; PSA 32:3–32:5

Job

JOB 42:1–42:6

The psalmists

PSA 119:59 See also PSA 42:5, PSA 42:11, PSA 43:5

The lost son

LUK 15:17–15:20

The disciples

MAT 26:22 parallel MRK 14:19

Judas

See also MAT 26:25, MAT 27:3–27:5

title: 8481: self-sacrifice
content:
The willingness to leave one's possessions or to give them to others; to deny oneself to the point of death or to give oneself in the service of God or other people.

Self-sacrifice as forfeiting one's present comfort for the sake of others

RUT 2:11 See also GEN 44:33–44:34; HEB 10:34, HEB 11:24–11:27

Self-sacrifice as giving one's possessions to others

Jesus Christ commends the willingness to give away one's possessions

MAT 19:21 parallels MRK 10:21, LUK 18:22 See also LUK 12:33

God rewards those who give their possessions away

LUK 18:28–18:30 parallels MAT 19:27–19:29, MRK 10:28–10:30

Sacrificing one's possessions as demonstrated in the life of the church

See also ACT 2:44–2:45, ACT 4:32–4:37; 2CO 8:1–8:5

Self-sacrifice as leaving all and following Jesus Christ

Such sacrifice is a condition of discipleship

LUK 14:33 See also MAT 10:37 parallel LUK 14:26 This means loving Jesus Christ over and above one's immediate family.

Those willing to leave everything to follow Jesus Christ

LUK 5:27–5:28; ; PHP 3:8

Self-sacrifice as the metaphorical laying down of one's life for others

Followers of Jesus Christ are required to give themselves in the service of others

JHN 12:24–12:25 See also MAT 10:38 parallel LUK 14:27; MAT 16:24–16:25 parallels MRK 8:34–8:35, LUK 9:23–9:24; LUK 17:33; 1JN 3:16–3:18

Examples of those who demonstrated such self-sacrifice

2CO 4:10–4:11 See also 1CO 9:19–9:23, 1CO 15:30–15:31; 2CO 11:23–11:29, 2CO 12:15

Self-sacrifice as the literal laying down of one's life

Jesus Christ warns his disciples to be prepared to give their lives

MAT 10:21–10:22 parallels MRK 13:12–13:13, LUK 21:16–21:17

Sacrificing one's life is of no value without love

See also 1CO 13:3

Examples of those willing to give their lives for the sake of God and others

ACT 20:23–20:24 See also EXO 32:32; 1CH 11:15–11:19; EST 4:14–4:16; MAT 26:39 parallels MRK 14:35–14:36, LUK 22:42; PHP 2:17

Examples of those who gave their lives in God's service

ACT 7:59–7:60 See also JDG 11:36–11:38; PHP 2:5–2:8; HEB 11:36–11:38; REV 20:4

title: 8482: spiritual warfare
content: The struggle against the forces of evil, which is a constant feature of the life of faith. Scripture locates the origins of spiritual warfare in the rebellion of Satan and his angels against God and affirms the hope of God's final victory over such forces through Jesus Christ's death and resurrection.

title: 8483: spiritual warfare, causes of
content:
Spiritual warfare has its origin in a rebellion of many angels against God. Satan is seen as the prince of this world, leading an array of forces opposed to God. Although disarmed by Jesus Christ on the cross, they remain a powerful threat to the church and to individual believers.

Satan and his angels fall

2PE 2:4 See also ISA 14:12–14:15; EZK 28:12–28:19 Some believe the kings of Babylon and Tyre to be types of Satan; 1TI 3:6; JUD 1:6

Satan and his angels comprise a well-organised army

EPH 6:12 See also COL 1:13

Satan and his angels will ultimately be fully disarmed by Jesus Christ

COL 2:15; REV 12:7–12:9 See also MRK 3:27 parallel MAT 12:29; LUK 10:18; JHN 12:31; HEB 2:14; 1JN 3:8

Satan persecutes the church

REV 12:13 The woman is here thought to be symbolic of the church. See also REV 2:10, REV 13:7 The dragon is here thought to be symbolic of the world's persecution (empowered by Satan) of the church.

Satan opposes the gospel

2CO 4:4 See also MAT 13:19 parallels MRK 4:15, LUK 8:12; MAT 13:38–13:39; 1TH 2:2, 1TH 2:18

Examples of opposition to the first Christians

ACT 6:8–6:14, ACT 7:54–7:58 Stephen stoned to death; ; ACT 8:1–8:3 Saul causes havoc in Jerusalem.; ACT 13:6–13:12, ACT 13:44–13:45, ACT 17:13, ACT 18:6, ACT 18:12; ACT 9:23, ACT 14:5, ACT 14:19, ACT 16:16–16:24, ACT 17:5–17:6, ACT 19:23–19:29, ACT 20:3, ACT 21:27–21:36; ACT 23:12–23:15, ACT 25:3

Satan attacks individual believers

REV 12:17 See also JOB 2:7; LUK 22:31–22:32; 2TI 3:12; 1PE 5:8

resource.label: 8787: opposition, to God's person and work

title: 8484: spiritual warfare, enemies in
content:
Christians are at war with the world, the flesh and the devil. Satan empowers the world to attack believers externally, persecuting, deceiving and seducing them. Internally, sinfulness frustrates the efforts of believers to serve God fully.

The world is an enemy

JAS 4:4 “world” here refers to the sinful human race, hostile to the truth and to the people of God. See also ROM 12:2; 1JN 2:15–2:17, 1JN 5:4

The world hates Christians

JHN 15:19–15:20 See also MAT 5:10–5:12 parallel LUK 6:22; JHN 16:2, JHN 17:14; 1PE 4:12–4:16; 1JN 3:13; REV 13:7 The beast may represent the world's antichristian persecution.

The world has its own false teaching and religion

COL 2:8 See also 1TI 4:1; 2TI 4:3–4:4; 1JN 4:1; 2JN 1:7–1:11; JUD 1:3–1:4; REV 13:11, REV 19:20 This beast is thought to represent antichristian religion.

The world seeks to seduce Christians

1JN 2:16 See also LUK 12:15, LUK 12:19; 2TI 4:10; TIT 2:12; HEB 11:24–11:25; REV 17:1–17:5 Babylon may represent the world's seduction.

Sinful human nature is an enemy

GAL 5:17; 1PE 2:11 See also ROM 6:12, ROM 7:14–7:23, ROM 8:13; GAL 5:24; COL 3:5; HEB 12:4; JAS 4:1

The devil is an enemy

1PE 5:8 See also MAT 13:39 parallels MRK 4:15, LUK 8:12; JHN 17:15; 2TH 3:3; REV 2:10, REV 12:17

He seeks to tempt Christians

1TH 3:5 See also GEN 3:1–3:6; HEB 2:18, HEB 4:15

He seeks to deceive

title: 8485: spiritual warfare, as conflict
content:
The warfare believers must fight is spiritual, personal, intense and continual. It calls for courage, determination and prayer, and therefore believers must stand in God's strength and use the armour he has provided.

General descriptions of spiritual conflict

It is spiritual

EPH 6:12 See also ZEC 4:6; 2CO 10:3–10:4; GAL 5:17; 1PE 2:11

It is personal

LUK 22:31–22:32 See also ROM 7:23; 2TI 3:12, 2TI 4:18

It is strenuous

HEB 12:4 See also JHN 16:33; PHP 1:27–1:30; 1PE 4:12–4:13

It is continual

EPH 6:13 See also 2TI 2:3; HEB 3:13; REV 12:10

How believers are to fight

With courage

1CO 16:13 See also JOS 1:9, JOS 10:25; 2CH 32:6–32:8

With determination

1TI 6:12 See also 2TH 1:4; HEB 10:23; 1PE 5:9–5:10

With watchfulness

1PE 5:8 See also 1CO 16:13; GAL 6:1; EPH 6:18

With prayer

EPH 6:18 See also EXO 17:11; MAT 6:13 parallel LUK 11:4; MAT 26:41 parallels MRK 14:38, LUK 22:46; ACT 12:5; 2TH 3:2

Standing in God's strength

EPH 6:10 See also 1SA 17:45; 2SA 22:40; PSA 18:32–18:36, PSA 118:8; EPH 3:16; PHP 4:13; 2TI 2:1

Using the armour of God

EPH 6:11 See also ROM 13:12–13:14; 2CO 10:4; EPH 6:13–6:17

title: 8486: spiritual warfare, armour
content:
The armour of God refers to the resources that Christians possess for defending themselves against the attacks of the world, the flesh and the devil.

God is the believer's strength and shield

PSA 28:7–28:8 See also GEN 15:1; DEU 33:29; PSA 3:3, PSA 7:10, PSA 119:114

Believers should be rightly clothed for battle

ROM 13:12–13:14 See also EPH 4:22–4:24; COL 3:9, COL 3:12–3:14; 1PE 4:1

Believers should put on the full armour of God

The belt of truth

EPH 6:14 PSA 119:95, PSA 119:116; ; EPH 4:14–4:15; ; COL 2:8; ; 2TI 1:13–1:14; ; 1PE 1:13

The breastplate of righteousness

EPH 6:14 PRO 4:23, PRO 13:6; ; ISA 61:10; ; ZEC 3:1–3:4

The gospel of peace

EPH 6:15 JHN 14:27, JHN 16:33; ; PHP 4:6–4:7

The shield of faith

EPH 6:16 ROM 1:17; ; HAB 2:4; ; 1PE 5:9; ; 1JN 5:4

The helmet of salvation

EPH 6:17 1TH 5:8–5:9; ; TIT 2:11–2:14; ; 1JN 3:3

The Christian's spiritual weapons

2CO 10:4

The sword of the Spirit

EPH 6:17 PSA 119:11; ; 2TI 3:16–3:17; ; HEB 4:12

The armour of God is worn with prayer

EPH 6:18 PSA 55:16–55:18; ; HEB 4:16; ; JAS 5:16

title: 8488: tithing
content:
The practice of offering to God a tenth of the harvest of the land and of livestock, as holy to the LORD. The idea is also used in a more general sense, meaning offering one-tenth of one's income to the Lord.

Tithing was practised before the giving of the OT law

GEN 14:18–14:20 Abraham offered a tenth of the goods taken in battle, apparently in thankfulness to God for victory. See also GEN 28:22; HEB 7:1–7:3

Tithing under the law

Tithing extends to all kinds of produce and livestock

LEV 27:30–27:32 Cereal and fruit offerings could be commuted to money. See also 2CH 31:5–31:6; NEH 10:35–10:38, NEH 13:12

All tithes were paid to the Levites

NUM 18:21–18:24; ; NEH 10:37–10:38; ; HEB 7:5

Tithes were to be paid in a designated place

DEU 12:5–12:6, DEU 14:22–14:29, DEU 26:2 Tithes were paid in Jerusalem, or every three years in towns where the tithe feast was eaten.

Levites offered a tenth to the LORD

NUM 18:25–18:29; ; NEH 10:39

Uses of the tithe

Support of the Levites

NUM 18:21 See also 2CH 31:4

The tithe meal

DEU 14:23

A three-yearly gift to the poor

DEU 14:28–14:29

Tithing of minor items must not lead to neglect of major matters

MAT 23:23 See also LUK 11:42, LUK 18:9–18:14

Freewill offerings were made in addition to the tithe

They were given freely

EXO 36:3 See also LEV 7:12–7:18; NUM 15:3; EZR 1:4; PSA 54:6; EZK 46:12

They were given according to ability

DEU 16:10 See also DEU 16:17; ACT 11:29; 1CO 16:2; 2CO 8:12 There is no specific command in the NT for the church to tithe, but many commands to give generously and to support the Lord's work.

Blessing promised to those who tithe

MAL 3:10 See also PRO 3:9–3:10

Failure to tithe and abuses of the tithe

MAL 3:8–3:10 See also LEV 27:33; 1SA 8:15, 1SA 8:17; NEH 13:10

title: 8489: urgency
content:
The urgency of the call to repent

In the preaching of John the Baptist

MAT 3:2 parallels MRK 1:4, LUK 3:3

In the preaching of Jesus Christ

MRK 1:15 See also MAT 4:17; LUK 13:3

In the preaching of Peter

ACT 2:38 See also ACT 3:19

In the preaching of Paul

ACT 20:21, ACT 26:20

The urgency of the need to proclaim the gospel

2TI 4:1–4:2 See also JHN 4:35–4:37; 2CO 6:2; 1TH 5:2 in the light of the coming day of the Lord

Examples of urgent summons by officials

NUM 22:37; ; 1SA 21:8; ; DAN 3:22

title: 8490: watchfulness
content: The state of being alert and expectant; watching over someone in one's care or waiting for the arrival of someone important or for some significant event. Scripture lays particular emphasis on the need to watch for the second coming of Jesus Christ.

title: 8491: watchfulness, divine
content:
The Lord's alertness to the needs of his people, his constant care for them and his awareness of the power and evil intent of their enemies.

The Lord's watchfulness over his people in danger or trouble

PSA 121:1–121:8 See also EXO 3:16; DEU 32:9–32:10; EZR 5:5; PSA 1:6, PSA 11:4–11:5, PSA 17:8, PSA 32:6, PSA 33:16–33:18, PSA 34:7, PSA 127:1, PSA 145:20; ZEC 9:8, ZEC 12:4; MAT 10:29–10:31; JHN 10:1–10:9; 2TI 1:12

The Lord's watchfulness means that his people's needs are met

PSA 146:9 See also GEN 28:15, GEN 48:15; DEU 2:7, DEU 11:12; 2CH 16:9; JOB 10:12, JOB 29:2; JER 24:6, JER 31:28; DAN 9:18

The watchfulness of a shepherd

PSA 23:1, PSA 28:9; ; ISA 40:11; ; MAT 2:6; ; JHN 10:1–10:9

The Lord's watchfulness means that he hears his people's prayers

PSA 34:15 See also 1KI 8:28–8:30 parallel 2CH 6:20; 1KI 9:3 parallel 2CH 7:16; NEH 1:6; 1PE 3:12

The Lord's watchfulness with a view to correction

JER 7:25–7:26 See also JER 7:13, JER 11:7, JER 25:4, JER 32:33; 2SA 22:28; JOB 33:11; JER 16:16–16:17

The Lord's watchfulness in seeking out those who have gone astray

EZK 34:16 See also MAT 18:12 parallel LUK 15:4; 1PE 2:25

People are vulnerable without the Lord's watchfulness

MAT 9:36 See also 1KI 22:17 parallel 2CH 18:16; ISA 13:14; EZK 34:11–34:12

title: 8492: watchfulness, of leaders
content:
Leaders must be alert to the needs of those they serve and also to the dangers that surround believers in the world. The OT teaching on watchmen provides an indication of the importance of watchfulness and the responsibility of those called to be watchful.

Leaders are required to be watchful

EZK 3:17 See also EZK 33:7–33:9; JHN 21:16

They are accountable to God

EZK 3:18 See also MRK 13:34–13:35; HEB 13:17

They must warn against false teachers

ACT 20:31 Elders are called overseers in Acts 20:28; 1Ti 3:2; Tit 1:7; 1Pe 5:2. See also JHN 10:1–10:3; ACT 20:29; 2TI 4:2–4:5; TIT 1:9–1:11

Examples of leaders' warnings to churches

1CO 4:14 See also ROM 16:17; GAL 5:21; 1TH 4:1; TIT 3:10; REV 22:18

Leaders' watchfulness in prayer

ISA 62:6–62:7 See also 1SA 12:23; ROM 1:9–1:10; EPH 1:16; PHP 1:4; 2TH 1:11

Leaders need to watch over their own lives

ACT 20:28 See also MRK 14:29–14:30; 1TI 3:2–3:7, 1TI 4:15–4:16; TIT 1:6–1:8; JAS 3:1; 3JN 1:9–1:10

Watchmen sometimes fail to be watchful

ISA 56:9–56:12; ; EZK 34:1–34:10; ; ZEC 10:2–10:3

title: 8493: watchfulness, of believers
content:
Alertness to dangers and blessings in the Christian life, and also to opportunities to do good.

Watchfulness for dangers

1PE 5:8 See also PRO 4:23

The danger of false teaching

MAT 7:15 See also PSA 94:8; PRO 8:33–8:34; MAT 24:4–24:5; MRK 8:15; ROM 16:17; 1CO 16:13

The danger of temptation

MAT 26:41 parallel MRK 14:38 See also DEU 4:15; 1KI 2:4; LUK 12:15, LUK 17:1–17:3; 1CO 10:12; GAL 6:1; 2JN 1:8

The danger of neglecting the word of God

DEU 4:9 See also JOS 22:5; 1KI 2:3; HEB 2:1, HEB 12:25; 2PE 1:19

The danger of damage to the Lord's work

NEH 4:9, NEH 7:3

The danger of speaking sinfully

PSA 39:1, PSA 141:3; ; PRO 13:3, PRO 21:23; ; JAS 1:26, JAS 3:5–3:8; ; 1PE 3:10

Watchfulness for blessings

PSA 25:15, PSA 59:9, PSA 123:1–123:2, PSA 130:5–130:6; ; ISA 40:9; ; MIC 7:7; ; LUK 2:25, LUK 2:36–2:38

Watchfulness and prayer

COL 4:2–4:3 See also MAT 26:41 parallel MRK 14:38; MRK 13:33; LUK 21:36; EPH 6:18; 1PE 4:7

Watchfulness for the return of Jesus Christ

MAT 24:42–24:44 See also MAT 25:1–25:13; MRK 13:32–13:37; LUK 12:35–12:40, LUK 21:32–21:36; 1TH 5:4–5:8; REV 16:15

Watchfulness for opportunities to serve the Lord

1PE 3:15 See also EPH 5:15–5:16; COL 4:5–4:6

Meeting the needs of others

EPH 6:18 See also MAT 26:36–26:40; GAL 6:10; TIT 3:1

Contrast with the watchfulness of unbelievers with evil intent

PSA 37:32 See also 1SA 18:9, 1SA 19:11; PSA 10:8; JER 20:10; MAT 26:16; MRK 3:2; ACT 9:24

Warning against neglect of watchfulness

REV 3:2–3:3

title: 8495: witnessing
content: The task of declaring what has happened, especially in relation to the life, death and resurrection of Jesus Christ. Believers are given the responsibility of proclaiming the good news of Jesus Christ to the world at all times and in all places.

title: 8496: witnessing, importance of
content:
Sharing the good news about God and Jesus Christ with others is a work to which some believers have a special calling, but in which all believers are to take part.

Witnessing is sharing the truth of God

PSA 145:10–145:12; LUK 24:46–24:48 See also 1CH 16:7–16:9; PSA 71:15; MAT 27:54 parallels MRK 15:39, LUK 23:47; JHN 1:35–1:36, JHN 4:29

Believers are commanded to witness

MAT 28:18–28:19 See also ISA 12:4–12:5; MAT 24:14 parallel MRK 13:10; ACT 1:8, ACT 9:15–9:16

Special ministries of witnessing

By the prophets

JHN 1:6–1:8 See also JER 1:4–1:9; EZK 33:7–33:9; JON 1:2, JON 1:9; JHN 1:15, JHN 1:29, JHN 1:36; ACT 10:43

By Jesus Christ

JHN 18:37 See also JHN 3:31–3:34; REV 1:5, REV 3:14

By the apostles

ACT 4:33 See also ACT 2:32, ACT 10:39–10:42, ACT 13:30–13:31; 1JN 1:1–1:3

By Christian leaders

2TI 1:8 Paul, in prison for his faith, encourages the young leader, Timothy. See also ACT 8:5; EPH 4:11

Witnessing is a task for all God's people

1PE 2:9, 1PE 3:15 See also PSA 26:6–26:7, PSA 107:1–107:2ISA 43:10, ISA 43:12, ISA 44:8 ISA 52:7; ACT 8:4

Witnessing is a major aspect of Christian living

ROM 10:9–10:10 See also MAT 10:32–10:33 parallels MRK 8:38, LUK 12:8–12:9; 2CO 4:13; 1JN 2:23, 1JN 4:15

Examples of witnessing to Jesus Christ

MAT 16:16 parallels MRK 8:29, LUK 9:20 Simon Peter; ; LUK 2:16–2:17 shepherds; ; JHN 1:40–1:42 Andrew; ; JHN 1:49 Nathanael; ; JHN 11:27 Martha; ; JHN 20:28 Thomas; ; ACT 8:37 the Ethiopian eunuch

Witnessing recounts personal experience

ISA 63:7 See also PSA 66:16; JER 51:10; DAN 4:2; MAT 9:27–9:31; MRK 1:40–1:45; JHN 9:25; ACT 4:20

Witnessing to the resurrection of Jesus Christ

ACT 2:32 See also LUK 24:33–24:35; ACT 5:30–5:32; 1CO 15:3–15:7

content:
Scripture provides teaching, supported by examples, concerning when believers should witness, the methods they are to use, and the manner of doing it.

When and where to witness

In the home and family

MRK 5:18–5:19 parallel LUK 8:38–8:39 See also 2KI 5:1–5:3; JHN 1:41

To individuals

JHN 1:40–1:42 See also JHN 4:7–4:26; ACT 8:30–8:35

To assembled groups

ACT 17:17 See also ACT 5:42, ACT 16:13, ACT 19:8–19:9

Methods of witnessing

Sharing personal testimony

JHN 4:29 See also ACT 22:3–22:8 Paul uses the account of his conversion in witnessing.

Explaining the Scriptures

ACT 8:30–8:35 See also ISA 53:7–53:8; PSA 119:172; ACT 17:1–17:3, ACT 17:10–17:12

Using prophetic gifts

1CO 14:24–14:25

Answering questions

COL 4:6 See also JHN 9:8–9:11, JHN 9:15–9:17, JHN 9:24–9:25; 1PE 3:15

Through writing

JHN 20:31 See also LUK 1:1–1:4

Through holy living

MAT 5:16 See also 1PE 3:1–3:2

Through acts of devotion

With love

MRK 10:21 See also PHP 1:15–1:17

With urgency

2CO 5:20 See also EZK 33:7–33:9

Fearlessly

EPH 6:19–6:20 See also ACT 4:29

Clearly and courteously

1PE 3:15 See also ACT 26:1–26:3; COL 4:4–4:6

title: 8498: witnessing, and Holy Spirit
content:
Christian witnessing is made effective through the empowering, strengthening and guiding of the Holy Spirit. Witnessing is an aspect of spiritual warfare, and believers need supernatural aid to face Satan's opposition.

The Holy Spirit supports believers in witnessing

ACT 5:31–5:32 See also JHN 15:26–15:27

The Holy Spirit empowers effective witness

ACT 1:8; 1CO 2:1–2:5 See also LUK 4:14–4:19, LUK 24:48–24:49

He confirms the testimony of believers

1TH 1:5; ; HEB 2:3–2:4

He convinces people of their need

JHN 16:7–16:11

He brings people to new birth

JHN 3:5–3:8

The Holy Spirit guides believers in witnessing

ACT 8:39–8:40 See also ACT 8:29–8:35, ACT 16:6–16:7

Witnessing and spiritual warfare

REV 12:11 See also EPH 6:15–6:17

Witnessing and persecution

Witnessing results in persecution

REV 1:9 See also ACT 4:17, ACT 5:40, ACT 7:54–7:60 Stephen's witnessing leads him to become the first Christian martyr. The English word “martyr” comes from the Greek word for “witness”; ACT 22:22–22:25; EPH 6:19–6:20; COL 4:3–4:4; 2TI 1:8; REV 2:12–2:13, REV 6:9, REV 17:6

Supernatural help to face persecution

MAT 10:18–10:20 parallels MRK 13:9–13:11, LUK 21:12–21:15ACT 7:55 See also ACT 5:18–5:19, ACT 18:9–18:10

Witness is promoted by persecution

ACT 8:1–8:5; ; PHP 1:12–1:14

title: 8602: prayer
content: Fellowship with God through Jesus Christ, expressed in adoration, thanksgiving and intercession, through which believers draw near to God and learn more of his will for their lives. Scripture stresses the vital role of the Holy Spirit in stimulating and guiding prayer.

resource.label: 8603: prayer, as a relationship with God
8604: prayer, as a response to God

title: 8603: prayer, as a relationship with God
content:
Prayer is based on God's love for believers. Through his grace, he gives them things which they do not deserve, while through his mercy he shields them from those things which they do deserve.

God's children can turn to their Father in prayer

Under the old covenant

ISA 64:8–64:9 See also PSA 103:13–103:14; ISA 63:16

Under the new covenant

MAT 6:9–6:13 parallel LUK 11:2–11:4 See also MAT 6:6, MAT 7:7–7:11 parallel LUK 11:9–11:13; ROM 8:15; GAL 4:6

Jesus Christ's prayer life with his Father

MRK 14:36 parallels MAT 26:39, MAT 26:42, LUK 22:42 See also JHN 17:1–17:26

It is possible to approach God in prayer because of Jesus Christ's sacrifice

HEB 10:19–10:22 See also EPH 3:12; HEB 7:15–7:19

Prayer reflects a longing after God

PSA 42:1–42:2; JER 29:12–29:13 See also PSA 130:5–130:6, PSA 145:18–145:19; PRO 8:17; ISA 26:9, ISA 33:2; LAM 3:25

title: 8604: prayer, as a response to God
content:
Prayer offers believers a means of acknowledging the character and purposes of God and the opportunity to seek guidance concerning his will for them.

The direction of prayer is upwards towards God

PSA 123:1–123:2 See also PSA 25:1, PSA 86:4, PSA 121:1–121:2, PSA 143:8, PSA 145:15

Fellowship with God through prayer

PSA 73:23–73:26 See also EXO 33:11; 1KI 8:57–8:59; PSA 16:2, PSA 145:17–145:20; MAT 18:20

The habit of prayer

LUK 5:16 See also NEH 2:4 Nehemiah felt so close to God that it was automatic for him to speak to God and the king almost simultaneously; DAN 6:10–6:11, DAN 6:13

Contemplative prayer as a response to God's presence

PSA 27:4 See also 1CH 16:10–16:11 parallel PSA 105:3–105:4; PSA 27:8; ISA 55:6; JER 29:13; ACT 17:27–17:28; HEB 11:6

Prayer of acceptance in response to God's call

1SA 3:10 See also ISA 6:8; REV 3:20

Prayer of confession

In response to God's holiness

1JN 1:5–1:9 See also ISA 6:3–6:7, ISA 55:7–55:9

In response to sin being exposed

PSA 51:1–51:2 See also PSA 51:3–51:12

Prayer of co-operation in response to God's purposes

JHN 15:7–15:8 See also PSA 119:105–119:106; LUK 1:38; JHN 15:16

Prayer of confidence in response to God's mercy and grace

HEB 4:16 See also NEH 1:4–1:7; PSA 123:1–123:2; JAS 1:5–1:8

title: 8605: prayer, and God's will
content:
Prayer is concerned not only with the well-being of the one who prays. A vital aspect of its purpose is to allow the will of God to be done, and to bring glory and honour to his name.

True motives for prayer

The desire that God's name be honoured

MAT 6:9–6:13 parallel LUK 11:2–11:4 See also NUM 14:13–14:16; JOS 7:7–7:9; 2SA 7:25–7:26; 1KI 18:36–18:37; PSA 115:1; JHN 17:1

The desire that God's will be fulfilled

MAT 6:9–6:13 parallel LUK 11:2–11:4 See also MAT 26:39 parallels MRK 14:36, LUK 22:42; MAT 26:42; HEB 10:7 Submission to God's will characterised Jesus Christ's prayer life.

God answers prayer that accords with his will

1JN 5:14–5:15

Petitioners may enquire of God to discover his will

PSA 143:10 See also GEN 25:22–25:23; JDG 1:1–1:2; 2SA 2:1; 1CH 14:14–14:15

The Holy Spirit helps believers to pray in God's will

ROM 8:26–8:27

God's response to prayers allows believers to discern his will

2CO 12:7–12:9 See also EXO 33:18–33:20; 2SA 12:15–12:18; JOB 19:7–19:8; PSA 35:13–35:14

God does not respond to the prayers of the wicked

JHN 9:31 See also PSA 66:18; PRO 15:8; ISA 1:15, ISA 59:1–59:2; LAM 3:44; 1PE 3:12

title: 8606: prayer, and Holy Spirit
content: See 3221: Holy Spirit, and prayer

title: 8607: prayer, God's promises concerning
content:
God promises to hear and respond to the prayers of his people, when they pray in the name of his Son and according to his will.

God expects his people to make requests of him in prayer

MAT 7:7–7:11 parallel LUK 11:9–11:13 See also MAT 21:22

God promises to answer prayer in the name of Jesus Christ

JHN 14:13–14:14, JHN 15:7 See also JHN 15:16, JHN 16:23–16:24

God promises to respond to the prayers of his people in times of need

PSA 91:14–91:16 See also PSA 50:14–50:15

God promises to hear the prayers of the oppressed

PSA 10:17 See also EXO 22:22–22:23, EXO 22:26–22:27; PSA 102:19–102:20; ISA 41:17

God promises to hear the prayers of the truly penitent

2CH 7:14 See also EZK 36:37; ZEC 10:6, ZEC 13:8–13:9

God promises to hear the prayers of his obedient people

1JN 3:22

The need in prayer to have confidence in God's promises

MRK 11:24; 1JN 5:14 See also MAT 18:19

title: 8608: prayer, and worship
content:
Worship is turning to God in awe, praise and joy, as his people realise how wonderful he is. Prayer is a natural part of worship: to know God is to want to worship him and pray to him.

Worship is a fundamental requirement of life

All nations are exhorted to worship God

1CH 16:28–16:29 See also PSA 29:1–29:2, PSA 96:9

Israel is commanded to worship God

2KI 17:36 See also PSA 95:6–95:7, PSA 99:4–99:5

Right attitudes in worship are imperative

Reverence and humility characterise acceptable worship

HEB 12:28–12:29 See also PSA 5:7, PSA 95:6, PSA 138:2; ECC 5:1

Honesty, without hypocrisy, characterises acceptable worship

AMO 5:21–5:24 See also MAT 15:7–15:9 parallel MRK 7:6–7:7; ISA 29:13; LUK 18:9–18:14; JHN 4:24

Prayer can focus on different aspects of God's character

Prayer can focus on God's holiness

EXO 15:11 See also PSA 77:13, PSA 96:9, PSA 99:5

Prayer can focus on God's glory

PSA 19:1–19:6 See also PSA 29:1–29:2, PSA 138:5; ROM 16:27; PHP 4:20; JUD 1:25

Prayer can focus on God's majesty

PSA 104:1–104:4 See also PSA 8:1, PSA 76:4, PSA 96:4–96:6

Prayer can focus on God's kingship

PSA 97:1 See also PSA 9:7, PSA 22:3, PSA 93:1, PSA 95:3, PSA 102:12

Prayer can focus on God's love and compassion

PSA 103:1–103:18 See also PSA 111:4, PSA 118:1–118:4, PSA 145:17–145:20

Prayer can focus on God's justice and righteousness

PSA 97:2 See also PSA 7:17, PSA 9:8, PSA 97:6, PSA 111:3

Prayer can focus on God's creative activity

NEH 9:6 See also PSA 90:2, PSA 95:3–95:7, PSA 102:25–102:27, PSA 104:5–104:9, PSA 104:24–104:26

title: 8609: prayer, as praise and thanksgiving
content:
Prayer embraces praising God for who he is, thanking him for what he has already done, and looking forward with joy to what he has promised to do in the future.

Scripture exhorts God's people to praise and thank him

PHP 4:6 See also PSA 66:1, PSA 68:4, PSA 95:1–95:2, PSA 105:1–105:3; EPH 5:19–5:20; COL 4:2; 1TH 5:16–5:18; HEB 13:15

Praise and thanksgiving in prayer for God's goodness towards his people

Praise and thanksgiving for deliverance and salvation

PSA 65:1–65:5 See also PSA 66:5–66:6, PSA 81:1–81:7, PSA 124:1–124:8; JON 2:1–2:9

title: 8611: prayer, for others
content:
Believers should pray, not only for their own needs, but for those of others. Scripture provides many examples of intercession, and commends it as pleasing to God.

1SA 7:5–7:9 See also 1SA 12:19–12:23

title: 8612: prayer, and faith
content:
Effective prayer depends on faith, especially on a willingness to trust in God's faithfulness to his promises to his people.

Faith is necessary in order to approach God

HEB 11:6

Faith is necessary to receive benefits from God

MRK 6:5–6:6; JAS 5:16–5:18 See also EPH 3:12; HEB 10:22

Faith is necessary for effective prayer

MAT 21:21–21:22 parallel MRK 11:22–11:24JAS 1:5–1:8 See also JAS 5:14–5:15

Jesus Christ responded to people's need on the basis of faith

MAT 9:27–9:30 See also MAT 8:5–8:13 parallel LUK 7:1–7:10; MAT 9:20–9:22 parallels MRK 5:25–5:34, LUK 8:43–8:48; MAT 15:21–15:28 parallel MRK 7:24–7:30

title: 8613: prayer, persistence in
content:
An answer to prayer may not come immediately. Petitioners are to continue praying earnestly. This requires patience, determination and, at times, a willingness to wrestle with God for the desired outcome.

The principle of persistence in prayer

Prayer should be made with patience and perseverance

PSA 40:1, PSA 88:1 See also 1CH 16:11; PSA 116:2

Jesus Christ taught his disciples to persist in prayer

LUK 18:1–18:8 See also LUK 11:5–11:10

Persistence in prayer was exemplified in the early church

ACT 1:14 See also ACT 2:42

Paul exhorted the churches to practise persistent prayer

EPH 6:18 See also ROM 12:12; 1TH 5:17

Examples of persistence in prayer

Abraham pleads persistently for Sodom

GEN 18:23–18:33

Jacob persists in wrestling with God

GEN 32:24–32:32

Moses persists in interceding for Israel

DEU 9:25–9:29 See also EXO 32:31–32:32

1SA 1:10–1:11

content:
Sometimes God does not seem to answer prayer, causing his people to doubt him. Scripture affirms God's faithfulness to those who pray according to his will, and points out that the human understanding of a situation is limited.

Examples of God's servants questioning his promises

title: 8616: prayerlessness
content:
Without prayer any relationship with God is impoverished because vital communication is lost.

Reasons for prayerlessness

Unbelief

PSA 14:1–14:4 parallel PSA 53:1–53:4 See also JOB 21:15; ROM 3:11

Self-reliance

JER 17:5 See also ZEP 3:2

Worship of other gods

DEU 32:17–32:18 See also JER 2:5–2:6, JER 2:8

Guilt as a result of disobedience

GEN 3:9–3:12 Adam and Eve did not respond to their sin by praying. On the contrary they sought to hide from God; ; JON 1:1–1:6 Jonah tried to run away from God.

Tiredness

LUK 22:45 See also MAT 26:40 parallel MRK 14:37; MAT 26:43–26:45 parallel MRK 14:40–14:41

Discord in relationship

1PE 3:7

Joshua, after a great victory

JOS 7:2–7:5 Joshua devised his own plan in attacking Ai and did not seek the LORD until after he suffered a disastrous defeat.

King Ahaziah, turning to idols

2KI 1:16 See also 2KI 1:1–1:6

The nominal religion of Israel

God's judgment

JAS 4:2 See also 2KI 17:15; JER 2:5

content:
Scripture provides guidance concerning what attitudes and actions are appropriate for effective prayer. It also identifies a number of motives which are likely to lead to prayers being unanswered.

Obedience

1JN 3:21–3:22 See also 1SA 15:22; JER 7:22–7:23

Righteousness

JHN 15:5–15:8 See also PSA 63:1–63:8

Prayerfulness involves a heart that is right with God

MAT 26:41 parallels MRK 14:38, LUK 22:40 See also MIC 7:7; LUK 21:36; COL 4:2

content:
The prayer life of the NT provides a pattern from which the modern church can learn, both in terms of the importance of prayer, and also matters for prayer.

Prayer was at the centre of the life of the early church

They prayed when they met together

ACT 1:14 See also ACT 2:42, ACT 4:23–4:31, ACT 12:12, ACT 20:36, ACT 21:5

ACT 13:2–13:3 See also ACT 1:24–1:25, ACT 6:6, ACT 14:23

ACT 12:5 See also ACT 7:59–7:60, ACT 12:12, ACT 16:22–16:25

ACT 9:40 See also ACT 28:7–28:8

The importance of prayer

title: 8620: prayer, practicalities of
content:
Scripture commends a life of prayer, characterised by simplicity of expression, sincerity of heart and trust in the promises of God. It gives guidance on how, when and where to pray.

Scripture stresses the importance of prayer

1TH 5:16–5:18 See also ACT 6:3–6:4; ROM 12:12

Judgment comes on those who do not pray

PSA 79:6 See also PSA 53:4; JER 10:21; ZEP 1:4–1:6; JAS 4:2

Prayers should be expressed simply

MAT 6:7–6:8 See also ECC 5:1–5:3; LUK 18:9–18:14

Prayer should not be ostentatious

MAT 6:5–6:6 See also MAT 14:23 parallel MRK 6:46; LUK 5:16

Sitting while praying

Kneeling while praying

Lying prostrate while praying

MRK 1:35 See also PSA 5:3, PSA 119:147

Praying all night

LUK 6:12 See also 1SA 15:11; LUK 2:37

JHN 4:21–4:24

DAN 6:10; MAT 6:6 See also 1KI 8:28–8:30

Praying outside a building

MRK 1:35; LUK 5:16 See also ACT 10:9, ACT 21:5

ACT 13:2–13:3 See also EZR 8:23; NEH 1:4; PSA 35:13; DAN 9:3; LUK 2:37, LUK 5:33; ACT 14:23; MAT 17:21 parallel MRK 9:29

title: 8622: worship
content: The praise, adoration and reverence of God, both in public and private. It is a celebration of the worthiness of God, by which honour is given to his name.

title: 8623: worship, of God alone
content:
God alone is worthy of worship; the worship of other gods is forbidden. In the NT worship is offered to the Son of God.

God alone is to be worshipped

He alone is worthy of worship

1CH 16:25 The English word “worship” means literally “worth-ship”. See also PSA 48:1, PSA 96:4–96:5, PSA 145:3; 2SA 22:4

The worship of God the Father

JHN 4:23 See also PHP 2:11

The worship of God the Son

MAT 2:11, MAT 14:33; JHN 20:28 See also MAT 28:16–28:17; JHN 9:35–9:38; PHP 2:9–2:11; HEB 1:6; REV 5:8–5:14

Angels worship God

PSA 103:20, PSA 148:1–148:2 See also PSA 29:1–29:2; ISA 6:1–6:4; EZK 10:1–10:18; REV 4:8–4:9

The worship of other gods forbidden

content:

title: 8625: worship, acceptable attitudes in
content:
True worship is not the mechanical repetition of rituals, but should be wholehearted and reverent. It should be based upon trustful and obedient lives, in that obedience is itself to be seen as an act of worship.

Worship should be in accordance with God's commands

GEN 22:2 See also GEN 12:1, GEN 12:7–12:8; DEU 30:16–30:20; 1SA 15:22; PSA 40:6–40:8; JER 7:2; DAN 3:28; ACT 13:2; ROM 12:1

Worship should not be mechanical

JHN 4:23–4:24 See also HEB 10:1

Worship should give God the honour due to him

1CH 16:29 parallel PSA 96:8–96:9

Worship of mere human devising is unacceptable

ISA 29:13 See also LEV 10:1; MAT 15:7–15:9 parallel MRK 7:6–7:7; PHP 3:3; COL 2:23

Worship should be orderly and reverent

1CO 14:40 See also 1CH 16:37–16:42; 1KI 18:30–18:39; 1CO 14:26

Worship should be grounded in godly and obedient living

MIC 6:6–6:8; ROM 12:1 See also PSA 15:1–15:5, PSA 24:3–24:4; 1TI 2:10

Preparation for worship

HEB 10:22–10:23 See also GEN 4:4; JAS 4:8; HEB 7:19, HEB 11:4

content:

To others

content:
Scripture stresses the importance of regular worship, while at the same time recognising that believers may worship God spontaneously.

Several times a day

DAN 6:10 See also 1CH 16:37; PSA 119:164; ACT 3:1; HEB 10:25

On holy days

2CH 8:12–8:13 See also EZK 46:3

At the three annual pilgrim festivals

DEU 16:16 EXO 12:1–12:20; ; LUK 2:41; EXO 34:22; ; ACT 2:1; EXO 23:16; ; LEV 23:33–23:36; ; NUM 29:12–29:39; ; DEU 16:13–16:15

content:

Deliverance

content:
An attitude of worship characterised by love and reverence towards God. It can also describe the love between man and woman.

DEU 10:12

content:
A Hebrew term expressing the ideas of truth and reliability, often used in prayer and adoration.

The response of the people represents a solemn, formal acceptance of God's commandments; PSA 72:19, PSA 106:48; ROM 9:5 “Amen” can mean either “Yes indeed, it is so” or “So be it”; ROM 11:36, ROM 16:25–16:27; 1CO 14:16; GAL 1:3–1:5; PHP 4:20; 1TI 1:17, 1TI 6:15–6:16; 2TI 4:18; HEB 13:20–13:21; 1PE 4:11, 1PE 5:10–5:11; 2PE 3:17–3:18; JUD 1:24–1:25; REV 1:4–1:7, REV 19:4 the worship of heaven

title: 8636: asking
content:
The act of making requests of another, as an expression of dependence. Scripture encourages believers to ask things of God in prayer, and gives guidance concerning the motivation in doing so.

Asking as an aspect of human relationships

Examples of everyday requests

JOS 4:20–4:22; ECC 7:10; 1PE 3:15 See also EXO 3:22; DEU 32:7; 1SA 12:19 The people asked for a king; 2KI 2:3; NEH 2:1–2:2; DAN 2:10–2:11; MAT 2:1–2:2 the Magi seek the king of the Jews; LUK 2:46 Jesus Christ asks questions in the temple; JHN 4:9; ROM 16:1–16:2; GAL 2:9–2:10; PHM 1:21

PHP 4:2–4:3 See also GEN 50:17; EXO 5:15; LUK 23:20; ACT 25:3; 1TH 4:1

title: 8638: benedictions
content:
Prayers invoking God's blessing upon others. They are often spoken at a time of impending separation, although they may sometimes constitute greetings.

title: 8642: celebration
content:
Although there are examples of private celebrations in Scripture, most celebration is associated with the acts of God. The enemies of God's people also celebrate, but in the end it is the triumph of God's purpose that is celebrated.

Celebrations in everyday life

Wedding: JDG 14:10; ; MAT 22:2–22:3; MAT 14:6 parallel MRK 6:21–6:22 birthday; ; LUK 5:29 for an honoured guest; ; LUK 15:22–15:24 family reunion

The Israelites celebrated God's acts

Celebrating God's gifts of harvest: Pentecost and Tabernacles

EXO 23:16, EXO 34:22; ; LEV 23:15–23:21, LEV 23:33–23:36, LEV 23:39–23:43; ; NUM 28:26, NUM 29:12; ; DEU 16:9–16:10

Celebrating their deliverance from slavery in Egypt: Passover

EXO 13:3 See also EXO 12:14, EXO 23:15, EXO 34:18; NUM 9:2; DEU 16:1

EST 9:18–9:19

2SA 6:12–6:15 parallel 1CH 15:27–15:28

The bringing of the ark of the covenant to the temple

1CO 11:26

content:
The act of remembering particular people, places or events in order to reflect on and be thankful for God's faithfulness.

LUK 22:19; 1CO 11:23–11:26

content:
A form of words that offers praise to God, especially for his work of creation and redemption. Scripture records a number of these forms of praise which were used in both public and private worship.

1CH 29:10–29:13 See also PSA 41:13, PSA 72:18–72:19, PSA 106:48, PSA 150:1–150:6

content:

JHN 16:23–16:24 See also JHN 16:13–16:15

title: 8652: importunity
content: Persistence and boldness in making requests to God in prayer and to other people, and persevering until a favourable response is received.

title: 8653: importunity, towards God
content:
Earnestness and perseverance in presenting requests to God on behalf of oneself and others; seen in persistent pleading, faithful intercession and bold appeal.

Perseverance in prayer

Persistence in prayer

PSA 55:17 See also PSA 22:1–22:2, PSA 86:3, PSA 88:1, PSA 88:9; 1TH 5:17; 1TI 5:5MAT 7:7–7:8 parallel LUK 11:9–11:10LUK 18:1 See also LUK 18:2–18:8

EPH 6:18 See also ROM 1:9–1:10; COL 4:12; 1TH 1:2–1:3; 2TI 1:3

Earnestness in prayer

PSA 119:58, PSA 130:1–130:2 See also PSA 55:1–55:2, PSA 61:1–61:2; JON 3:8LUK 22:44 See also HEB 5:7

Boldness in prayer

GEN 18:27; LUK 11:8 See also EXO 33:12–33:16EPH 3:12; HEB 4:16

Further examples of importunity in prayer

GEN 32:26 Jacob wrestles with God; ; DEU 9:18 Moses fasts and prays because of Israel's sin; ; 2SA 12:16 David pleads for his sick child; ; 1KI 18:28–18:29 The prophets of Baal appeal unsuccessfully to their god; ; NEH 1:4–1:6 Nehemiah prays for God's people; ; DAN 10:2–10:3 Daniel waits for the interpretation of his vision; ; LUK 2:37 Anna looks for God to redeem his people.

1SA 1:12–1:16 Hannah prays for a child; ; 1KI 8:22 parallel 2CH 6:12 Solomon prays at the dedication of the Temple; ; JAS 5:17–5:18 Elijah prays for rain to cease; ; EZR 9:5 Ezra prays about the people's sin; ; ISA 38:2–38:3 Hezekiah prays for healing; ; DAN 9:3 Daniel prays for Jerusalem; ; MRK 5:22–5:23 parallel LUK 8:41–8:42 Jairus asks Jesus Christ to heal his daughter; ; JHN 4:47 A nobleman begs Jesus Christ to heal his son; ; ACT 12:5 The early church prays for Peter's release from prison.

content:

content:

MAT 6:9 parallel LUK 11:2 See also MAT 7:21, MAT 16:17; LUK 10:21; EPH 3:14–3:15

A desire for God's perfect will to be done

title: 8660: magnifying God
content:
Giving glory to God through worship and through upright living. God's people are exhorted to praise him and to bring honour to his name.

content:
Spending time in quietness and usually alone, drawing close to God and listening to him, pondering on his word, his creation, his mighty works or other aspects of his self-revelation.

title: 8664: praise
content: The celebration, honouring and adoration of God, in the power of the Holy Spirit, whether by individual believers or communities of believers.

Praise is commanded of God's people

For answered prayer

PSA 28:6 See also PSA 66:19–66:20

title: 8666: praise, manner and methods of
content:

The manner of praise

God is praised in faith

PSA 28:7, PSA 106:12

God is praised through Jesus Christ

HEB 13:15 See also PHP 2:9–2:11

God can be praised at any time and in any place

PSA 104:33, PSA 145:2 See also PSA 146:2

God helps believers to praise him

PSA 51:15 See also PSA 40:3; ISA 61:3

The Holy Spirit moves believers to praise

LUK 1:67; EPH 5:18–5:20 See also LUK 10:21; ACT 2:11, ACT 10:44–10:46; COL 3:16–3:17

In singing

title: 8670: remembering
content:
The process of recalling the past, especially the presence and activity of God in the history of his people. Remembering God's work in the past can lead to praise and rejoicing, and to hope for the future. God himself remembers.

Divine remembering

God always remembers his covenant

1CH 16:15 parallel PSA 105:8 See also GEN 9:14–9:16; EXO 2:23–2:25; PSA 111:5; LUK 1:69–1:73

God always remembers his promises

PSA 105:42 See also DEU 6:20–6:23; JOS 1:3; 2PE 3:9

God always remembers his people

ISA 49:15–49:16 See also GEN 7:24–8:1, GEN 19:29, GEN 30:22; 1SA 1:19–1:20; LUK 1:54–1:55

Situations in which God will not remember

HEB 8:10–8:12 See also JER 31:33–31:34; ISA 65:16–65:17; EZK 18:21–18:24

The Holy Spirit helps believers to remember Jesus Christ and his words

JHN 14:26 See also JHN 2:22, JHN 12:16, JHN 16:4

Human remembering

Believers are to remember God's person

DEU 8:18; PSA 119:55 See also PSA 42:5–42:6; JER 51:50; JON 2:7

Believers are to remember God's acts in the past

ISA 46:9 See also DEU 5:15, DEU 7:17–7:18, DEU 8:10–8:18; 1CH 16:12; MAT 16:9–16:10

PSA 13:5–13:6 See also DEU 26:4–26:11; PSA 66:5–66:6

LUK 24:6–24:8 See also JHN 15:20, JHN 16:1–16:4; ACT 11:15–11:18

title: 8672: striving with God
content:
Striving with God can refer both to the fruitless opposition of the ungodly to God's will and purposes, and to the struggle of the righteous with God, as they seek to find his will and obey it.

The striving of the wicked with God

It is the result of a guilty conscience

ACT 26:14

Striving against God cannot succeed

2CH 13:12 See also PRO 21:30; ISA 8:10; ACT 11:17

It leads to the destruction of those who attempt it

PSA 2:2–2:5 See also JOB 15:20–15:26, JOB 15:30

Ways in which the wicked strive with God

By resisting the Holy Spirit

ACT 7:51

By arguing with God

ROM 9:20 See also JOB 40:2; ISA 45:9–45:11

Through unbelief

NUM 14:1–14:4, NUM 14:10–14:11, NUM 20:13; ; PSA 95:8–95:9

By attacking God's people

ACT 5:39 To attack God's people is to attempt to attack God himself. See also 1SA 17:45; ISA 37:22–37:25; ACT 9:4–9:5

Jacob strives with God

GEN 32:24–32:28 Jacob's struggle with God represents the conflict within himself between self-will and dependence on God. As “Jacob”, the supplanter, he had overcome Esau and Laban, but God demonstrates his superior power in the wrestling match so that as “Israel” he will be submissive to the divine will. See also HOS 12:2–12:5

The striving of the righteous with God

The struggle for righteousness

ACT 24:16 See also LUK 13:24; ROM 7:14–7:25; 1CO 9:25–9:27; PHP 3:10–3:14; 1TI 4:10; HEB 12:4

title: 8674: study
content:
The application of the mind with a view to acquiring knowledge, particularly of the Scriptures. God promises his help to those who give themselves to this work.

The study of the works of the LORD

PSA 111:2 The works mentioned are his acts of providence and grace.

God's people are to study in order to gain wisdom

content:
The offering of thanks, especially for gifts received. Scripture emphasises the importance of giving thanks to God for all his gifts and works, both as an expression of our dependence upon him and gratitude to him.

title: 8678: waiting on God
content:
Being prepared to patiently look towards God for his guidance and accepting the timing he proposes. Waiting on God can lead to an atmosphere of expectation and confidence in God and a realisation of the unreliability of one's own judgment.

Waiting on God is something that is commanded

HOS 12:6 See also PSA 27:14, PSA 37:7, PSA 37:34, PSA 123:2; ISA 30:18

Reasons for waiting on God

JER 14:22 for his providence; ; PSA 25:5 for his salvation; ; PSA 145:15–145:16 for his blessings

Waiting on Christ

JAS 5:7–5:8 “Waiting on Christ” is often seen in terms of waiting patiently for God to bring about the end of all things through the promised second coming of Jesus Christ. See also LUK 12:35–12:40; 1CO 1:7, 1CO 4:5; TIT 2:13; HEB 9:28; JUD 1:21

The benefits of waiting on God

It leads to expectancy

PSA 5:3 See also ROM 8:23; 1CO 4:5; GAL 5:5; TIT 2:13

It leads to hope

PSA 33:20 See also PSA 130:5; ISA 51:5; MIC 7:7

It leads to trust

ISA 8:17

It leads to patience

ROM 8:23–8:25 See also LAM 3:24–3:26; REV 6:9–6:11

GEN 49:18 Jacob; ; PSA 39:7 David; ; ISA 8:17 Isaiah; ; MIC 7:7 Micah; ; MRK 15:43 Joseph of Arimathea; ; LUK 2:25 Simeon

title: 8701: affluence
content:

title: 8702: agnosticism
content:
The inability to decide whether or not God exists. It is characterised by indecision and compromise when faced with the challenge to wholehearted commitment, and is condemned as sinful, inexcusable and unnecessary in the light of God's clear self-revelation.

Agnosticism is inexcusable in the light of God's self-revelation

In the creation

ROM 1:19–1:20 See also PSA 19:1–19:2; ACT 14:17

In the person of Jesus Christ

JHN 1:18 See also JHN 14:9; HEB 1:1–1:3

Agnosticism is sinful

Because God calls for wholehearted commitment

JOS 24:14–24:15 See also EXO 32:26; DEU 6:13–6:14, DEU 30:15–30:19; ACT 14:15

Because God's call demands total obedience

MAT 9:9 parallels MRK 2:14, LUK 5:27–5:28 See also MAT 4:18–4:22 parallel MRK 1:16–1:20

1KI 18:21; 2KI 17:41 See also 2KI 17:29–17:33; 1CO 10:21

title: 8703: antinomianism
content:
A form of spiritual anarchy, which rejects the law as having any place in the Christian life, whether as instructor or as assessor. Paul's teaching that Christians are free from the law is sometimes misunderstood as antinomian. But Paul reveres God's law, and teaches believers, who are free from the law as a system of salvation, to keep it out of gratitude for salvation freely given, and because holiness as defined by the law is the Christian calling.

Antinomianism as a rejection of God's laws

JER 2:20 See also PRO 29:18; JER 5:5; HOS 8:12; 2PE 2:10

EZK 20:13 See also EXO 32:25; JER 2:23–2:25; HOS 8:1; ZEC 7:11–7:12
