JER 6:19 See also EZR 7:26; AMO 2:4–2:5; REV 22:15

title: 8704: apostasy
content: A general falling away from religion or a denial of the faith by those who once held it or professed to hold it. It is frequently described in terms of spiritual adultery and thus provokes the jealous anger of God.

title: 8705: apostasy, in OT
content:
Israel was in danger of abandoning God from her earliest days. The OT frequently warns against apostasy and identifies its likely consequences.

Apostasy in Egypt and in the desert

PSA 78:9–78:41 See also EXO 32:25–32:29 the death of 3,000 after Aaron made the golden calf; LEV 17:7, LEV 20:1–20:6; NUM 14:9–14:12 The people rebel against Moses and Aaron after the return of the spies; NUM 14:31–14:35, NUM 25:1–25:4, NUM 32:10–32:11; DEU 31:16–31:18, DEU 32:15–32:21; PSA 95:7–95:8, PSA 106:13–106:33; HEB 3:15–3:19

Apostasy in the time of the judges

PSA 78:55–78:64 See also JDG 2:6–2:23, JDG 8:27, JDG 8:33–8:34; NEH 9:26–9:31; PSA 106:34–106:39

Apostasy in the kingdom of Israel

HOS 5:3–5:4 See also 2KI 17:7–17:20; HOS 1:2, HOS 4:10–4:19, HOS 7:4

Apostasy in the kingdom of Judah

JER 3:1–3:25 See also 2KI 23:26–23:27; 2CH 29:6–29:9 Hezekiah's reforms to purify the temple; 2CH 30:7–30:9; ISA 1:1–1:6, ISA 30:1–30:5 Judah's alliance with Egypt; JER 2:7–2:13, JER 2:19–2:25, JER 5:5–5:7, JER 7:9–7:15, JER 9:2, JER 13:23–13:27, JER 17:5–17:6, JER 17:13, JER 23:10–23:15 lying prophets denounced; JER 31:22; EZK 6:9, EZK 16:15–16:42, EZK 23:1–23:35; DAN 9:5–9:14

title: 8706: apostasy, warnings against personal
content:
It is possible for individuals to fall away from faith or turn against Jesus Christ. Scripture identifies this danger and warns against its negative consequences.

Personal apostasy described

HEB 6:4–6:8 See also MAT 13:20–13:21 parallels MRK 4:16–4:17, LUK 8:13; MAT 24:10–24:12; GAL 1:6, GAL 5:4; 2TH 2:3; 2TI 4:3–4:4; 1TI 4:1; 1JN 2:19, 1JN 5:16

Warnings against personal apostasy

HEB 10:26–10:31 See also MAT 10:33 parallels MRK 8:38, LUK 12:9; JHN 15:6; 2TI 2:12; HEB 3:12; 2PE 3:17

OT examples of personal apostasy

DEU 13:1–13:11 an unfruitful prophet or relative; 1SA 15:11, 1SA 15:28, 1SA 16:14; ; 2SA 7:15; 2CH 26:16–26:21 King Uzziah; ; 2CH 28:19–28:27 King Ahaz

NT examples of personal apostasy

MAT 26:14–26:16 parallels MRK 14:10–14:11, LUK 22:3–22:6 Judas; ; LUK 13:26–13:27; ; JHN 6:66; ; ACT 5:1–5:11 Ananias and Sapphira; ; 1TI 1:19–1:20 Hymenaeus and Alexander; ; TIT 1:16; ; 2TI 4:10 Demas; ; 2PE 2:1–2:3, 2PE 2:10–2:15, 2PE 2:20–2:22; ; JUD 1:4, JUD 1:8–1:16; ; REV 2:20–2:22 Jezebel

title: 8707: apostasy, dealing with personal
content:
Individual believers can fall away from faith and be restored. Scripture gives examples of such falling away, and offers advice on how such people should be dealt with pastorally.

Warnings of the dangers of personal apostasy

2CO 11:2–11:3 See also PSA 125:4–125:5; LUK 9:59–9:62; GAL 3:1–3:3, GAL 4:8–4:10 Those who return to strict observance of Jewish days and festivals have not understood the gospel.

Warnings against leading others into apostasy

MAT 18:6 See also PRO 28:10; GAL 5:7–5:10

Encouragements to guard against personal apostasy

1CO 10:12–10:13; HEB 3:12–3:14 See also PSA 85:8; MAT 24:10–24:13, MAT 24:24–24:25 parallel MRK 13:22–13:23; COL 1:21–1:23; 1TI 6:20–6:21; HEB 10:35–10:39, HEB 12:1–12:8; 2PE 3:17–3:18; REV 13:5–13:10

Dealing with apostate believers

GAL 6:1 See also 1CO 5:4–5:5; JAS 5:19–5:20; 1JN 5:16–5:17

Examples of those who were restored from apostasy

Samson: JDG 16:20, JDG 16:28–16:30; PSA 51:1–51:17 David; MAT 26:74 parallels MRK 14:72, LUK 22:61–22:62, JHN 18:27 for the account of Peter's reinstatement see Jn 21:15–17; ACT 15:37–15:38 for evidence of John Mark's recovery see 2Ti 4:11

The punishment of apostates

ISA 65:12–65:15; ; EZK 3:20, EZK 18:24–18:26; ; 2TH 2:11–2:12; ; 2PE 2:17

Punishment through misfortune

DEU 28:63; ; AMO 2:4–2:6

Punishment through defeat

NUM 14:43; ; JDG 2:12–2:15

Punishment through rejection

2CH 24:20; ; HOS 4:6

title: 8709: astrology
content:
The study of the stars and planets, based on the pagan assumption that they exercise a decisive influence over human destinies. Scripture rejects such beliefs, insisting upon the total sovereignty of God over his entire creation.

Astrology is to be rejected

The worship of heavenly bodies is forbidden

DEU 4:19; 2KI 17:16 See also 2KI 21:3–21:5 parallel 2CH 33:3–33:5; 2KI 23:4, 2KI 23:11; JOB 31:26–31:28; EZK 8:16–8:18; ZEP 1:5

The consultation of stars is condemned

ISA 47:13 See also JER 8:2

Astrology at the time of Daniel

DAN 2:1–2:13, DAN 4:1–4:7, DAN 5:1–5:8

Astrologers came to worship the newborn Jesus

MAT 2:1–2:10

title: 8710: atheism
content:
The denial of God's existence and thus also the denial of his word, truth and authority. It is seen in the worship of created things, in human boasting and in the decision to live a life without God which results in godlessness and brings God's judgment.

Characteristics of atheism

Denying God's existence

PSA 14:1 parallel PSA 53:1

Worshipping created things

ROM 1:25 See also DAN 5:23; REV 9:20

Denying God's truth

ISA 32:6; ROM 1:18 See also JER 5:12, JER 5:31, JER 11:21, JER 14:14, JER 27:15

Denying God's ability to fulfil his word

JER 17:15 See also ISA 5:19; ACT 17:18; 1TH 4:8; 2PE 3:3–3:4; REV 11:7–11:10

Showing contempt for God's name

LEV 19:12; ; JER 5:2; ; EZK 36:20, EZK 43:8

Boasting against God

PSA 10:3–10:5 See also JOB 15:25; PSA 12:3–12:4, PSA 36:1–36:2, PSA 73:11; PRO 30:9; EZK 35:13; REV 13:6

Not turning to God in trouble

JOB 35:10 See also JOB 36:13; JER 2:8, JER 17:5

Living in ignorance of God

JER 5:4 See also EPH 2:12

Denying Jesus Christ

JUD 1:4 See also 1JN 2:22, 1JN 4:3; 2JN 1:7

Atheism results in godless living

ROM 1:28–1:31 See also GEN 6:5; 1SA 2:12; PRO 11:9; ISA 9:17, ISA 26:10; JER 5:5, JER 23:11; MAL 3:14, MAL 3:18; 1TI 1:9–1:10; JUD 1:18

Atheism brings condemnation

It cannot be excused

JOB 12:7–12:8; ; ACT 14:17; ; ROM 1:19–1:20

It results in lack of hope

JOB 8:13, JOB 15:34, JOB 20:5, JOB 27:8; ; PSA 9:17

It results in God's judgment

ISA 10:6, ISA 33:14; ; JER 5:5–5:6, JER 5:9–5:11, JER 5:29; ; ROM 1:18; ; 1PE 4:17; ; 2PE 3:7; ; JUD 1:14–1:15

God desires to save the atheist

ACT 17:27 See also ISA 55:7; JER 3:12; EZK 18:23, EZK 33:11; ROM 5:6–5:8

title: 8711: covenant breakers
content:
Covenants were central to OT life, with the result that those who broke covenants, and especially those who violated the covenant between God and Israel, were regarded as a serious threat to social stability.

The importance of covenants

The covenant between God and his people

GEN 9:16 See also 2SA 23:5; ISA 24:5, ISA 55:3

God will remain faithful to his covenant

JDG 2:1 See also PSA 105:8; ISA 54:10

Covenants between people

Covenants made in the sight of God were permanently binding

NUM 30:2; 1SA 23:16–23:18 See also DEU 23:21; ECC 5:4

Condemnation of those who break covenants

HOS 6:7 See also PRO 2:17

Examples of covenants between people

GEN 21:27; ; JOS 24:24; ; 2SA 5:3; ; 1KI 5:12, 1KI 20:34; ; JER 34:8

Examples of breaking the covenant with God

Coveting the possessions of others

ECC 4:4 See also EXO 20:17

Stealing

EXO 20:15 parallel DEU 5:19 See also DEU 23:24

Using dishonest weights or scales

LEV 19:35–19:36; PRO 20:23 See also DEU 25:13–25:16; HOS 12:7–12:8; AMO 8:5

Moving boundary stones

PRO 23:10 See also DEU 19:14, DEU 27:17

Extortion

HAB 2:6 See also ISA 10:1–10:2; EZK 22:12; AMO 5:11

Breach of trust

LEV 6:2; ; EZK 16:17

Not repaying loans

PSA 37:21

Not paying fair wages

See also GEN 31:6–31:9

Failing to care for aliens

Aliens living in Israel were regarded as having privileged status amongst Gentiles, and were treated as covenant people in some respects: EXO 23:9; ; DEU 29:9–29:15, DEU 31:12; ; JOS 8:33–8:35

title: 8712: denial of Jesus Christ
content:
The making of a conscious, informed decision not to accept Jesus Christ or his claims and teaching.

Jesus Christ was denied by the Jewish people

JHN 1:11 See also MAT 11:16–11:19 parallel LUK 7:31–7:35; MAT 13:54–13:58 parallel MRK 6:1–6:6; MAT 26:63–26:68 parallels MRK 14:61–14:65, LUK 22:66–22:71; LUK 4:16–4:30; JHN 5:37–5:43; ACT 4:8–4:12; PSA 118:22

The consequences of denying Jesus Christ

Denying Jesus Christ results in judgment

JHN 12:48 See also MAT 12:38–12:42 parallel LUK 11:29–11:32

Denying Jesus Christ means replacement by others

ACT 13:46 See also MAT 21:40–21:41 parallels MRK 12:9, LUK 20:15–20:16; ACT 18:5–18:6

To deny Christ is to be denied by Christ

2TI 2:12 See also MAT 10:32; MRK 8:38

Warnings against those who deny Jesus Christ

2PE 2:1 See also 1JN 2:22–2:23; 2JN 1:7; JUD 1:4

Denial, repentance and restoration: the example of Peter

Peter's denial predicted by Jesus Christ

MRK 14:29–14:30 parallels MAT 26:31–26:34, LUK 22:31–22:34

Peter declares he will never deny Jesus Christ

MRK 14:31 parallel MAT 26:35

Peter denied that he knew Jesus Christ

MAT 26:69–26:75 parallels MRK 14:66–14:72, LUK 22:55–22:62, JHN 18:15–18:18, JHN 18:25–18:27

Peter's restoration to Christ

See also JHN 21:15–21:19; ACT 1:15–1:22, ACT 2:14–2:41

title: 8713: discouragement
content:
A sense of unhappiness arising from a loss of confidence in one's own abilities, in the reliability of God or in the power of the gospel. Discouragement can occur in the Christian life, especially when there is resistance to the gospel or in instances of personal failure. Scripture provides reassurance for those who experience discouragement.

The experience of discouragement

JOB 3:20–3:26 See also NUM 21:4–21:5 the Israelites in the desert; JOS 2:8–2:11 the Canaanites and Rahab; 1SA 17:10–17:11 the Israelites and Goliath; 2KI 19:26 God's judgment on Sennacherib; JOB 5:6–5:7; PSA 38:1–38:14; PRO 1:26–1:27 Wisdom speaks to the sinner; ECC 2:17–2:20 the Teacher's disillusion; ISA 21:2–21:4; JER 45:3 to Baruch; EZK 21:7 God's judgment on Israel; ZEC 10:2; 2CO 1:8–1:9 Paul

Prayer in discouragement

PSA 42:5–42:11 See also DEU 26:6–26:7; 2SA 22:7 David; 2CH 20:9 Jehoshaphat; NEH 9:32; PSA 31:9–31:12; ISA 38:14 Hezekiah; JER 8:18–8:19; JON 2:1–2:2

Endurance in discouragement

ISA 42:3–42:4 See also 2CO 6:4–6:10 Paul; 2TH 1:4; HEB 10:32, HEB 12:3; REV 2:3 concerning the church at Ephesus

Discouragement through disobedience

JER 8:9 See also 1SA 28:15–28:18; JOB 15:24–15:25 Eliphaz to Job; ZEP 1:17

Discouragement and discipline

HEB 12:5–12:7 See also JDG 2:14–2:15; ISA 26:16

Effects of discouragement

PRO 17:22 See also EXO 6:9 the Israelites in Egypt; 2SA 4:1; EZR 4:4 the rebuilding of the temple; JOB 4:5; PRO 15:13, PRO 18:14

Resisting discouragement

DEU 1:21 See also JOS 1:9, JOS 8:1; 1SA 17:32 David reassuring Saul about Goliath; 1CH 22:13 David to Solomon; 2CH 32:7 Hezekiah; JER 51:46; LUK 18:1; JHN 14:1; GAL 6:9; EPH 3:13; 2TI 4:5

God's help in discouragement

ROM 8:35–8:39 See also DEU 31:6, DEU 31:8, DEU 31:23; JOS 1:9; 1CH 28:20; 2CH 20:15, 2CH 20:17; PSA 34:18; ISA 40:29–40:31, ISA 61:1; LUK 4:18; JER 30:10; JHN 16:33; 2CO 7:6 Paul

Warnings not to discourage others

The Israelites discouraged when on the point of entering the promised land

OBA 1:12 See also DEU 1:28 by the spies; NUM 32:7 by the Gadites and Reubenites

General warnings not to discourage others

PSA 109:16; ; ZEC 10:2; ; ACT 15:19 James advises against discouraging the Gentiles; ; COL 3:21

The need to stand with the discouraged

HEB 13:3 See also JOB 6:14; JER 8:21; ROM 12:15; JAS 1:27

title: 8714: dishonesty
content: A way of speaking or acting which leads to people being deceived, misled or cheated.

title: 8715: dishonesty, and God's nature
content:
Dishonesty is contrary to the will and nature of God, and so should not be found among the people of God.

Dishonesty is contrary to the will and nature of God

NUM 23:19 See also 1SA 15:29; ROM 3:4; TIT 1:2

Dishonesty, like sin, is of satanic origin

JHN 8:44 See also GEN 3:1–3:5

God's hatred of dishonesty

PRO 12:22 See also PSA 5:4–5:6; PRO 6:16–6:17; ISA 59:1–59:4, ISA 59:12–59:15

Kinds of dishonesty

In business deals

HOS 12:7 See also DEU 25:13–25:16; PRO 20:14; AMO 8:5; MIC 6:10

In not paying debts

PSA 37:21 See also JAS 5:4

In exploiting the poor

EZK 22:29 See also JOB 24:2–24:11; ISA 32:7; JER 22:13

God's judgment on dishonesty

God's denunciation of dishonesty in general

HOS 4:1–4:2 See also LEV 19:15; JER 7:8–7:10; 1TH 4:6

The dishonesty of liars and false witnesses

PRO 19:9; ACT 5:1–5:10 See also DEU 19:16–19:19; JOS 7:10–7:12 regarding Achan's sin; 2KI 5:19–5:27; PSA 5:6; ISA 29:20–29:21; JER 9:4–9:9; REV 21:8

The dishonesty of false prophets and teachers

JER 14:14–14:15; ; 2PE 2:1–2:3; ; ISA 9:14–9:15; ; JER 28:15–28:16; ; EZK 13:1–13:23; ; ZEC 10:2–10:3; ; 1TI 4:1–4:2

God's demands for making amends for dishonesty

LEV 6:1–6:7; ; LUK 3:12–3:14 This demonstrated that their repentance was genuine; ; LUK 19:8 the result of encountering Jesus Christ; ; LUK 16:1–16:12 Jesus Christ was not commending the steward's dishonesty but his shrewdness.

title: 8716: dishonesty, examples of
content:
Examples of the dishonest behaviour condemned by God.

Dishonest words condemned

Lying

EPH 4:25 See also LEV 19:11; PSA 34:13; COL 3:9–3:10

False witness

EXO 20:16 parallel DEU 5:20 See also MAT 19:17–19:18; MRK 10:19; LUK 18:20; EXO 23:1, EXO 23:7; MAT 26:59–26:60; ACT 6:12–6:14

Swearing falsely

LEV 19:12 See also EXO 20:7; MAT 5:33–5:37

Dishonest actions condemned

Stealing

EXO 20:15 parallel DEU 5:19 See also MAT 19:18 parallels MRK 10:19, LUK 18:20; ROM 13:9

Dishonest dealing

PRO 11:1 See also LEV 19:13; DEU 25:13–25:16; PSA 62:10; ISA 33:15–33:16; TIT 2:9–2:10

Israel condemned for dishonest gain

Bribery and extortion

EZK 22:12–22:13 See also JER 22:13, JER 22:17–22:19; EZK 22:27–22:31; HAB 2:6–2:9

Cheating and dishonest scales

AMO 8:4–8:8 See also LEV 19:35–19:36; MIC 6:10–6:13; MAL 1:14 In this case, they were cheating the LORD.

Examples of dishonesty

GEN 26:15–26:22 Abimelech's servants; GEN 25:29–25:33, GEN 27:6–27:29, GEN 30:31–30:43; GEN 29:21–29:30, GEN 31:19 Rachel; ; GEN 31:36–31:42 Laban; ; JOS 7:11–7:26 Achan; ; 1KI 21:2–21:16 Ahab and Naboth's vineyard

title: 8718: disobedience
content:
The refusal to obey someone, especially someone in a position of authority. Scripture insists on the need to obey God at all times.

Disobedience enters people's hearts for various reasons

Disobedience comes through greed and lust

GEN 3:6 See also GEN 3:11–3:12; EXO 16:19–16:20; JOS 7:20–7:21; 2SA 11:2–11:4

Disobedience arises from impatience

EXO 32:23 See also NUM 20:10–20:11; 1SA 13:8–13:14

Disobedience comes through fear

JER 43:2–43:7; ; JHN 7:13, JHN 12:42; ; GAL 2:12

Disobedience results from pride and arrogance

LEV 10:1 See also EXO 5:2; 2CH 26:16

Unbelief is disobedience

HEB 3:12 See also JER 7:23–7:28; ROM 11:30–11:32 Ro 11:20 makes it clear that the disobedience spoken of here was unbelief; HEB 3:18–3:19, HEB 4:2, HEB 4:6

Lack of love is disobedience

JHN 14:24 See also 1JN 2:9, 1JN 3:15

Disobedience to God leads to punishment

Punishment is applied to individuals

GEN 3:17–3:19 See also GEN 3:23–3:24; LEV 10:1–10:2; NUM 20:12; 1SA 28:18; 2SA 12:14; JON 1:10–1:12; EPH 5:5–5:6

Punishment for the disobedience of unbelief

2TH 1:8–1:9 See also HEB 2:2–2:3

Nations are also punished

GEN 15:14 See also ACT 7:7DEU 11:26–11:28; 1SA 12:15 See also EXO 32:35; DEU 28:15; ISA 13:11

Disobedience, like all sin, can be forgiven

ROM 5:19 See also EPH 2:1–2:5

title: 8719: distrust
content:
Failure to trust another, or a tendency to be suspicious of others' abilities or intentions. Though sometimes justifiable towards other human beings, such an attitude is never acceptable towards God.

Distrust between human beings

GEN 50:15–50:17 Joseph's brothers distrusted him because they could not believe he had forgiven them. See also GEN 32:6–32:8 Jacob distrusted Esau because he thought he was seeking revenge; JDG 11:19–11:20 Sihon distrusted Israel because he suspected a trick; ACT 15:37–15:38 Paul distrusted John Mark, having been let down by him.

Distrust of God

Israel distrusted God

ZEP 3:2 See also DEU 1:32–1:33, DEU 9:23–9:24 Because that generation distrusted God, they failed to enter the promised land; PSA 78:7, PSA 78:22 Israel distrusted God in spite of the miracles he had done for her.2KI 17:14–17:15; JER 13:25

Other examples

Distrust in God involves failure to trust God's promises and placing trust in other things: JER 13:25; ; EZK 33:13; ; MAL 3:6–3:10; ; MAT 19:22 parallel MRK 10:22

Distrust by God

JOB 4:18 See also JOB 15:15; JHN 2:24

Distrust is sometimes justified

PSA 118:8 See also JOB 39:12; PSA 5:9, PSA 44:6, PSA 146:3; JER 7:4, JER 9:4, JER 12:6; MIC 7:5; HAB 2:18

title: 8720: double-mindedness
content:
Indicative of insincerity and hypocrisy. God requires wholeheartedness and sincerity from all people, both in their dealings with others and in their worship of him.

Double-mindedness is characteristic of sinners

JAS 4:8 See also PSA 119:113–119:115

Double-mindedness in dealings with other people

GEN 34:1–34:29; ; JOS 9:3–9:15; ; 1SA 18:17–18:25; ; 2SA 3:22–3:27, 2SA 20:8–20:10; ; NEH 6:1–6:4, NEH 6:10–6:13; ; MAT 26:47–26:50 parallels MRK 14:43–14:46, LUK 22:47–22:48; ; ACT 23:12–23:24

Double-mindedness in daily life

MAT 23:25–23:28 See also MAT 15:10–15:19 parallel MRK 7:14–7:23; LUK 11:39–11:40

Double-mindedness in worship

Idolatry

1KI 18:21 See also 2KI 17:27–17:34, 2KI 17:40–17:41; HOS 10:1–10:2

Insincerity

MAT 15:1–15:9 parallel MRK 7:1–7:13 See also ISA 29:13

Lack of faith in prayer is equated with double-mindedness

JAS 1:5–1:8

God requires wholeheartedness and sincerity

Towards himself

1CH 28:9 See also NUM 14:20–14:24; JOS 14:14; 2CH 31:21; ROM 12:9; 1CO 5:8; 2CO 1:12; 1TI 3:8; JAS 3:13–3:17

Towards other people

COL 3:22 See also 2CH 19:8–19:11; EPH 6:5–6:9

title: 8721: doubt
content: Uncertainty about the truth and reality of spiritual things, as seen especially in a lack of faith in and commitment to God.

title: 8722: doubt, nature of
content:
Doubt leads to insecurity and lack of trust concerning God's willingness and ability to deliver his people. It also leads to a fear of people and situations.

Doubting God's truth

Doubt as a questioning of God's words

GEN 3:1 See also GEN 3:4; ISA 5:19; JER 17:15; 2PE 3:4

Doubt as lack of faith

MAT 21:21–21:22 parallel MRK 11:23–11:24 See also MAT 17:20; MRK 6:6, MRK 16:14; LUK 17:6

Doubt as wavering

JAS 1:6 See also 1KI 18:21; ROM 4:20; EPH 4:13–4:14

Doubt as double-mindedness

JAS 1:8 See also 2KI 17:40–17:41; LUK 16:13; 1CO 10:21; JAS 4:8

Doubt as insecurity about relationship with God

Doubting God's compassion

PSA 77:7–77:9 See also PSA 90:13; HEB 12:5–12:6

Doubting God's concern

JOB 30:20; ISA 49:14 See also PSA 13:1–13:2, PSA 22:1–22:2, PSA 35:17; ISA 40:27; JER 8:18–8:22; LAM 3:8; HAB 1:2

Doubting God's desire to deliver

JER 45:3 See also EXO 5:22–5:23; LAM 2:1–2:9, LAM 3:13–3:20

Doubting God's ability to deliver

PSA 78:18–78:22 See also EXO 14:10–14:12; PSA 78:41–78:43; MAT 8:26 parallels MRK 4:39–4:40, LUK 8:24–8:25

Doubting God's justice

JER 12:1 See also JOB 9:23; PSA 73:13–73:16, PSA 82:2; JER 15:16–15:18; HAB 1:13

Doubt as fear of people and situations

MAT 14:30–14:31 See also GEN 12:12–12:13, GEN 19:30, GEN 26:7; JOS 7:5; 1SA 17:11; ISA 51:12–51:13

title: 8723: doubt, results of
content:
Doubt results in uncertainty and ineffectiveness in the spiritual life of individual believers and of the believing community. God appeals to those who waver to make a clear choice.

Doubt results in spiritual uncertainty

Uncertainty about commitment

LUK 9:57–9:62 parallel MAT 8:19–8:22 See also GEN 19:17, GEN 19:26; EXO 16:2–16:3; MAT 6:24 parallel LUK 16:13; HEB 11:15

Uncertainty about God's power

NUM 13:31 See also DEU 1:29–1:33

Uncertainty about God's love

ISA 40:27 See also DEU 1:27; JOB 9:16–9:18, JOB 30:21

Uncertainty about the meaning of life

JOB 3:16 See also 1KI 19:3–19:4; PSA 42:3–42:4; JER 20:14–20:18; JON 4:3

Uncertainty about teaching

EPH 4:14 See also 1TI 6:20–6:21

Uncertainty about the will of God

JDG 6:17 See also JDG 6:36–6:40; JHN 20:25; 2CO 13:3

Doubt may result in a spiritual decline

Doubt may result in drifting from faith

HEB 2:1 See also 2CH 36:12–36:13; NEH 9:16–9:17; PSA 95:8–95:9; LAM 5:20; HEB 3:12–3:13, HEB 6:4–6:6; 2PE 2:20–2:21

Doubt may result in faithless action

ISA 31:1; ROM 14:23 See also GEN 12:13, GEN 16:2–16:3; EXO 32:1; NUM 20:11–20:12; ACT 7:40; ROM 14:14

Doubt brings the risk of God's judgment

NUM 20:12 See also NUM 11:1, NUM 14:37; HEB 6:7–6:8

Doubt leads to ineffectiveness in prayer

JAS 1:6–1:7 See also MAT 17:20, MAT 21:21 parallel MRK 11:23

Doubt spreads

DEU 1:28 See also NUM 13:32; 2KI 17:14

God's appeal for a clear decision

1KI 18:21 See also DEU 30:15–30:17; JOS 24:15; JHN 20:27; JAS 4:8

title: 8724: doubt, dealing with
content:
Uncertainty may be remedied by gaining assurance from God's word, remembering God's past goodness, reflecting on his power and appealing to his unfailing love. Believers should help the weak with the patience and encouragement that reflects God's own compassion.

Gaining assurance from God's word

PSA 119:147; 1JN 5:13 See also PSA 119:116; JHN 20:31; ROM 15:4; 2PE 1:19

Receiving correction and understanding through God's word

2TI 3:14–3:17 See also PSA 119:130; PRO 6:23; 1CO 10:11

Avoiding idle speculation

EPH 4:14; ; 1TI 6:20–6:21; ; 2TI 2:16, 2TI 2:23; ; TIT 3:9

Remembering God's past deeds

Commemorating God's deeds

EXO 12:14 Religious festivals such as Passover provided a permanent reminder of God's past goodness to his people. See also DEU 16:1; LUK 22:19; 1CO 11:24–11:25

Reflecting on divine power

title: 8727: enemies
content: Opponents or hostile forces which pose a threat to people or nations. Scripture identifies Satan as being the particular enemy of God and notes many enemies of the people of God. Scripture urges caution and courage in dealing with such enemies. Jesus Christ had enemies, and he provides an example of Christian conduct in the face of enemies' threats.

resource.label: 8731: enemy, Satan as the enemy of God

content:

title: 8734: evil
content: The presence of corruption, malevolence and depravity in the world, opposed to God's nature and will. Scripture stresses that evil is a force in its own right, rather than the mere absence of good, and describes its origins and the manner in which God deals with its continuing presence and power in his world.

content:
Although Scripture does not reveal the ultimate origin of evil, it identifies a number of intermediate sources.

ACT 4:3, ACT 5:18, ACT 6:9, ACT 8:1–8:3, ACT 12:1, ACT 13:8, ACT 13:50, ACT 14:5, ACT 14:19, ACT 16:19, ACT 17:5, ACT 17:13, ACT 18:12, ACT 19:29, ACT 20:3, ACT 21:27, ACT 23:12

Evil influences

NUM 25:1, NUM 31:16; ; DEU 18:9; ; HOS 7:9; ; 1CO 5:6, 1CO 8:10; ; 1TI 4:1; ; 2PE 2:18; ; 1JN 2:26

title: 8741: failure
content:
Scripture indicates various ways in which believers may fail God, while emphasising that God will never fail his people.

God will never fail his people

1CH 28:20 See also JOS 1:8–1:9; PSA 89:28

God's righteousness will not fail

ISA 51:6

God's compassion will not fail

LAM 3:22–3:23

God's word will not fail

ISA 55:10–55:11 See also ROM 9:6

Examples of failing God

Failing to abide in him

PSA 14:3 See also PSA 58:3, PSA 78:57; JER 2:19, JER 3:22, JER 15:6; JHN 15:6; 2PE 3:17

Failing to believe in him

JHN 20:27 See also NUM 14:11–14:12; PSA 78:21–78:33; HEB 3:12

Failing to fear him

GEN 20:11 See also EXO 9:30; DEU 25:18; JOB 6:14; LUK 23:40

Failing to honour him

MAL 2:2 See also NUM 20:12; 1SA 2:29–2:30; DAN 5:22–5:23; ROM 2:23

Failing to love him

1CO 16:22 See also JOS 23:10–23:13; MAT 10:37; REV 2:4

Failing to obey him

2KI 17:14–17:20; ; MAT 7:26

Failing to remember him

DEU 8:11, DEU 32:18 See also JDG 3:7, JDG 8:33–8:34; 1SA 12:9; PSA 78:11, PSA 106:21; ISA 17:10

Failing to seek him

2CH 12:14 See also PSA 14:2–14:3, PSA 119:155; ISA 9:13; ZEP 1:6

Failing to serve him

DEU 28:47–28:48 See also JOB 21:14–21:15; JER 2:20; MAL 3:14; ROM 1:25

Failing to trust him

MAT 6:30 parallel LUK 12:28 See also MAT 14:31, MAT 16:8, MAT 17:17–17:20

Peter's failure of Jesus Christ

MAT 26:33–26:35 parallel MRK 14:29–14:31; ; LUK 22:31–22:34; ; JHN 18:25–18:27

title: 8742: faithlessness
content: The lack or absence of faith, or the turning away from a professed commitment to God.

title: 8743: faithlessness, nature and causes of
content:
The abandoning of a commitment to the Lord, seen in disowning him, wandering from the truth and becoming entangled with the world, and resulting in judgment.

Warnings against faithlessness

2TI 2:12–2:13 See also MAT 10:33 parallel LUK 12:9; LUK 9:62; HEB 10:35–10:39; HAB 2:3–2:4

Ways in which faithlessness is seen

Turning away from the Lord

HEB 3:12

Abandoning the gospel of grace

GAL 1:6

Becoming entangled in the world

2PE 2:20–2:22 See also PRO 26:11; 2TI 4:10

Causes of faithlessness

False teaching

2TI 2:17–2:18 See also GAL 1:7, GAL 4:8–4:11; 1TI 4:1–4:3; 2TI 4:3–4:4; 2PE 3:17

Persecution and trials

MAT 13:20–13:21 parallels MRK 4:16–4:17, LUK 8:13 See also MAT 24:9–24:13

Concern for money and possessions

1TI 6:10 See also PRO 30:8–30:9; MAT 13:22 parallels MRK 4:18–4:19, LUK 8:14

Love growing cold

MAT 24:12 See also REV 2:4

Sexual desire

1TI 5:11–5:15

Faithlessness brings punishment

Church discipline

1TI 1:18–1:20 These men had been excluded from the church, a sanctuary from Satan's power.

God's judgment

MAT 10:33 parallel LUK 12:9 See also HEB 6:4–6:6, HEB 10:26–10:27

The faithlessness of those who fall away

The absence of true faith

1JN 2:19

True faith is proved by perseverance

See also JAS 1:2–1:3; 1PE 1:5–1:7

Israel's faithlessness in the OT

Israel's unfaithfulness led to God's rejection

PSA 78:56–78:59

Warnings not to repeat Israel's unfaithfulness

PSA 95:7–95:11; ; HEB 3:7–3:12, HEB 4:1–4:2

title: 8744: faithlessness, as disobedience
content:
A lack of faith and obedience to God, which is seen especially in the lives of unbelievers. However, Scripture makes clear that believers can occasionally lapse into faithlessness towards God.

Faithlessness among the ungodly

In their character and lifestyle

PSA 101:3–101:5, PSA 119:158 See also PSA 10:4, PSA 14:1; JHN 16:8–16:9; 2TH 3:2; TIT 1:15–1:16

Examples of faithless men

1SA 25:2–25:3 Nabal; ; EST 3:5–3:6 Haman; ; MAT 2:16 Herod the Great; ; ACT 19:23–19:27 Demetrius

The faithless appear to prosper

JER 12:1 See also JOB 21:7; PSA 73:3–73:5, PSA 73:12; MAL 3:15

Faithlessness results in judgment

PRO 14:14; JHN 3:36 See also PSA 73:17–73:18, PSA 73:27; MAL 4:1; MRK 16:16; JHN 8:24; 2TH 2:12; REV 21:8

Faithlessness among the Jews

Their failure to trust God for deliverance

ISA 31:1 See also ISA 22:8–22:11, ISA 30:1–30:2, ISA 30:12–30:13

Their rejection of the gospel

JHN 12:37–12:38 See also ISA 53:1; JHN 3:11–3:12, JHN 5:37–5:40, JHN 8:45, JHN 10:25–10:26

Specific examples

MAT 13:58 parallel MRK 6:5–6:6 the people of Nazareth; ; MAT 19:21–19:22 parallels MRK 10:21–10:22, LUK 18:22–18:23 the rich young ruler; ; ACT 28:24 Many Jews reject Paul's ministry in Rome; ; 1TI 1:13 Paul's own persecution of the church arose from unbelief in Jesus Christ.

Israel's estrangement from God

MAT 21:43 See also PSA 118:22; MAT 21:41 parallel MRK 12:9; ROM 9:32–9:33

The acceptance of the Gentiles

ROM 11:17–11:21 The Jews' rejection of the gospel opens the way for Gentiles to be incorporated into the people of God, represented here as branches grafted onto a cultivated olive tree.

Israel's faithlessness is partial and temporary

ROM 11:5 Though the people as a whole have rejected Jesus Christ, a faithful remnant remains; ; ROM 11:11–11:12, ROM 11:23–11:27 God's purpose for the faithful of Israel is their ultimate salvation.

Faithlessness among believers

Lack of faith is rebuked

MAT 14:30–14:31 See also MAT 6:30–6:32 parallel LUK 12:28–12:30 worrying about food and clothing; MAT 8:24–8:26 parallels MRK 4:38–4:40, LUK 8:23–8:25 Fear during a storm at sea; MAT 17:17–17:20 parallels MRK 9:17–9:19, LUK 9:40–9:42 inability to cast out a demon

Causes of faithlessness

MAT 16:8–16:10 failure to learn from the lessons of the past; ; LUK 24:25 failure to accept teaching that has been given

title: 8746: false Christs
content:
Mistaken and deceptive people claiming to be Jesus Christ. Jesus Christ warns his followers to be on their guard against the appearance of such people.

Jesus Christ warns that false Christs will appear

MAT 24:5 parallels MRK 13:6, LUK 21:8 See also MAT 24:23 parallel MRK 13:21

False Christs will perform signs and miracles in order to deceive

MAT 24:24 parallel MRK 13:22

False Christs can be recognised because the return of Jesus Christ will be obvious to everyone

MAT 24:27–24:31 parallels MRK 13:24–13:27, LUK 21:25–21:28 The personal return of the Lord Jesus Christ is not described in terms of an appearance to a select group, but to the whole world. The attempt of anyone to convince others that he is Christ therefore is a sure sign of deception.

title: 8747: false gods
content:
Any gods other than the LORD himself. Some of these divinities took the form of images, others were mythical. Some Israelites became involved in idolatrous worship of such gods. The book of Acts records attempts to deify human beings.

False gods associated with foreign nations in the OT

Amon, the chief god of Egypt

See also JER 46:25

Asherah, a Canaanite goddess

EXO 34:13–34:14 Asherah was the consort of El, the chief Canaanite god. Wooden poles, perhaps carved in her image, were often set up in her honour and placed near other pagan objects of worship. See also DEU 7:5; JDG 6:25–6:30 Gideon destroys an Asherah pole; 1KI 14:15, 1KI 14:23, 1KI 15:13, 1KI 16:33, 1KI 18:19 Elijah summons 400 prophets of Asherah to Mount Carmel.2KI 23:4–23:7, 2KI 23:13–23:16 ISA 27:9; JER 17:2; MIC 5:14

Ashtoreth, a goddess of war and fertility

JDG 2:12–2:13 Ashtoreth, the consort of Baal, was associated with the evening star and was worshipped as Ishtar in Babylon and as Athtart in Aram. To the Greeks she was Astarte or Aphrodite and to the Romans, Venus. See also JDG 10:6; 1SA 7:3–7:4, 1SA 12:10, 1SA 31:10; 1KI 11:5, 1KI 11:33

Baal, a Canaanite and Phoenician god of fertility and rain

JDG 2:10–2:13 Baal, meaning “lord”, was pictured standing on a bull, a popular symbol of fertility and strength. Baal was associated with Asherah and Ashtoreth, goddesses of fertility.

Baal-Zebub, a popular deity of the Philistines

MAT 12:24 parallels MRK 3:22, LUK 11:15 Beelzebub is the Greek form of the Hebrew name “Baal-Zebub”, meaning “lord of the flies”. See also 2KI 1:1–1:6, 2KI 1:16–1:17

Bel, the chief deity of Babylon

ISA 46:1 Bel was another name for the sun god, Marduk. Nebo, the god of learning and writing was the son of Marduk. See also JER 50:2, JER 51:44

Chemosh, the chief god of Moab

1KI 11:7 See also NUM 21:29; 1KI 11:33; 2KI 23:13; JER 48:7, JER 48:13, JER 48:46

Dagon, worshipped in Babylonia and Philistia

JDG 16:23 See also 1SA 5:2–5:7; 1CH 10:10

Molech, the chief deity of Ammon

1KI 11:4–11:5 See also LEV 18:21 The practice of sacrificing children to Molech was common in Phoenicia and the region; LEV 20:2–20:5; 1KI 11:7, 1KI 11:33; 2KI 23:10 Josiah destroyed the area where the altars for child sacrifice were located; 2KI 23:13; ISA 57:9; JER 32:35, JER 49:1, JER 49:3; ZEP 1:5; ACT 7:43

Tammuz, a Babylonian fertility god

EZK 8:14

The worship of false gods was a snare to God's people

Their worship included disgusting rites

1KI 14:23–14:24, 1KI 19:18; ; JER 7:31; ; HOS 13:2

Numerous attempts were made to stop the worship of Baal and other false gods

JDG 6:28–6:32; 1KI 18:17–18:40 See also 2KI 10:18–10:28, 2KI 11:18, 2KI 23:4–23:5, 2KI 23:13

Attempts to stop false worship proved unsuccessful

2KI 21:3 The word “Baal” was not orginally a proper name but came to be used as such. See also 2CH 28:1–28:4; HOS 13:1–13:2

Warnings against and condemnation of, the worship of false gods

PSA 40:4; DAN 3:29 Nebuchadnezzar came to realise the foolishness of worshipping false gods See also PSA 4:2; JER 13:25, JER 16:19; AMO 2:4; ZEP 1:4

The first Christians were confronted with the worship of Greek and Roman deities

Zeus and Hermes

ACT 14:12 Zeus was the patron god of the city of Lystra and his temple was there. Paul was identified as the god Hermes (the Roman Mercury), Zeus' attendant and spokesman.

Artemis

ACT 19:24–19:28 Artemis was the Greek name for the Roman goddess, Diana.

Castor and Pollux

See also ACT 28:11 the two “sons of Zeus”, regarded as the guardian deities of sailors

Attempts to deify human beings

ACT 12:21–12:22, ACT 14:12–14:15, ACT 28:6

title: 8748: false religion
content:
The worship of anything that is not God, including any form of religion that fails to do justice to the glory and majesty of God. Scripture criticises both the practices and the beliefs of false religions.

The nature of false religion

Man-made images are worshipped

ACT 17:29 See also DEU 4:28; PSA 115:4–115:7, PSA 135:15–135:17; ISA 44:10–44:20; JER 10:3–10:5, JER 16:20; DAN 3:4–3:7; ACT 19:26

Created things are worshipped

ROM 1:25 See also 2KI 21:3 parallel 2CH 33:5; JER 8:2, JER 19:13; EZK 8:16

Secular authorities are worshipped

REV 13:4 The dragon in Revelation may be understood as the devil and the beast as the antichrist: the forces at work behind the human authorities that defy the rule of God. See also ACT 12:21–12:23; REV 13:8, REV 13:12

Demons are worshipped

DEU 32:17 See also LEV 17:7; PSA 106:37–106:38; 1CO 10:20; REV 9:20

False religion is based on man-made traditions, myths and philosophies

COL 2:8, COL 2:20–2:23; ; 1TI 1:4, 1TI 6:20

False religious practices

Immorality

1KI 14:23–14:24 See also EZK 16:16–16:17; HOS 4:13–4:14

Human sacrifice

2KI 17:17 See also LEV 18:21; PSA 106:37–106:38

False religion ensnares its adherents

It offers no help in time of need

1SA 12:21 See also JDG 10:14; 1KI 18:29; 2KI 19:12 parallel ISA 37:12; ISA 16:12, ISA 44:17–44:20, ISA 45:20, ISA 46:7, ISA 57:13; JER 11:12

It prevents people from finding the truth

JON 2:8 See also MAT 23:13; LUK 11:52; 2CO 4:4

It devalues, degrades and defiles

2KI 17:15 See also PSA 106:39, PSA 115:8, PSA 135:18; ISA 44:9; JER 2:5; EZK 20:18

It leads to immorality

NUM 25:1–25:2 See also NUM 25:3, NUM 25:6–25:8; ROM 1:23–1:31; REV 9:20–9:21

It enslaves

GAL 4:8 See also DEU 12:30; GAL 4:3, GAL 4:9–4:10; COL 2:8

False religion receives the full force of God's anger

JER 16:18 See also 1KI 13:1–13:3, 1KI 13:33–13:34; 2KI 17:18–17:23; JER 22:8–22:9; MIC 5:13–5:15; NAM 1:14; ZEP 1:4–1:5

title: 8749: false teachers
content:
Those who teach error and in so doing lead others astray. They are to be distinguished from false prophets who are equally condemned in Scripture.

The OT prophets warned God's people against being led astray by false teachers

ISA 9:16; EZK 34:2 See also ISA 3:12, ISA 8:20; JER 2:8, JER 10:21, JER 23:1; EZK 22:26; MAL 2:7–2:8

Jesus Christ condemned false teachers

He opposed legalism and hypocrisy

MAT 5:19

He identified the teachers of the law and Pharisees as false teachers

MAT 23:1–23:33 parallel LUK 11:42–11:52 See also MAT 15:14

He warned his followers against them

MAT 16:6, MAT 16:12 parallels MRK 8:15, LUK 12:1

The condemnation of false teachers in the early church

Paul urges his readers to avoid false teachers

1TI 6:3–6:6 See also ACT 20:29–20:31; ROM 16:17–16:18; 2CO 11:3–11:4 The Corinthian church had been undiscerningly tolerant of Jewish deceivers in their midst; EPH 4:14COL 2:4, COL 2:81TI 1:3–1:4, 1TI 1:7 1TI 4:1–4:3, 1TI 6:20–6:21; TIT 1:10–1:11; HEB 13:9; 2JN 1:9–1:10REV 2:6, REV 2:15 REV 2:14 the followers of Balaam; REV 2:20

Hymenaeus and Philetus are cited as examples of false teachers

2TI 2:17–2:18

Those who teach will be judged particularly strictly

JAS 3:1 See also 2CO 11:13–11:15; GAL 1:6–1:9, GAL 5:10

title: 8750: false teachings
content:
Scripture repeatedly warns against false teachings, which deny or distort some aspect of the gospel. The origin of such teachings is attributed either to human error or to demonic inspiration.

Examples of false teachings

REV 2:14–2:15 See also MAT 5:19; 2TH 2:1–2:2; 1TI 4:1–4:3; REV 2:20

Qualities of false teachings

They are valueless

MAT 15:9 parallel MRK 7:7 See also ISA 29:13; EPH 5:6; COL 2:20–2:23; 1TI 1:3–1:7

They are destructive in their nature

2PE 2:1 See also MAT 7:15; ACT 20:29–20:30; TIT 1:10–1:11

They have the capacity to lead people astray

ACT 20:30 See also EPH 4:14; 1TI 6:20–6:21; HEB 13:9; 2PE 2:14–2:15; 1JN 2:26

They may be popular

2PE 2:2 See also MAT 24:4–24:5 parallel MRK 13:5–13:6; 2TI 4:3; 2PE 2:18–2:19; 1JN 4:1–4:5

They may be accompanied by miraculous signs

MAT 24:24 parallel MRK 13:22 See also 2TH 2:9–2:10; REV 13:11–13:15

The origin of false teachings

Demonic inspiration

1TI 4:1–4:2 See also 2CO 11:3–11:4; 1JN 4:1–4:3; REV 16:13–16:14

Human error

2PE 2:3 See also COL 2:8; 1TI 6:20–6:21

Discerning false teachings

By their content

1JN 4:2–4:3 See also 1CO 12:3; 1JN 2:20–2:23; 2JN 1:7–1:11

By the teacher's lifestyle

MAT 7:15–7:20 See also 2CO 11:20; 1JN 3:7–3:10; JUD 1:4

By their effects

1TI 6:3–6:5 See also 1TI 1:3–1:4; 2TI 2:16–2:18; REV 2:20

The antidote to false teachings

Holding fast to the true gospel

1JN 2:24 See also GAL 1:6–1:9; 1TI 1:18–1:20; 2TI 1:13–1:14

Shunning false teachers

ROM 16:17–16:18 See also 2TI 3:1–3:9; TIT 3:9–3:11; 2JN 1:9–1:11

title: 8751: false witness
content:
The telling of lies about another so as to make them appear guilty when they are innocent. Condemned in Scripture, false witness was experienced by Jesus Christ and is to be expected by those who follow him.

False witness is condemned in Scripture

EXO 20:16 parallel DEU 5:20 See also EXO 23:1; DEU 19:15–19:19; PSA 101:5–101:7; MAT 19:18 parallels MRK 10:19, LUK 18:20

False witness arises from an evil heart

MAT 15:19–15:20 parallel MRK 7:21–7:23

False witness will be subject to judgment

PSA 101:5–101:8; PRO 21:28 See also PRO 19:9; DAN 6:24; MAT 12:35–12:37

Examples of those who were the victims of false witness

Jesus Christ

MAT 26:59–26:61 parallel MRK 14:55–14:59 See also MAT 11:18–11:19 parallel LUK 7:33–7:34

Other examples

1KI 21:8–21:14 Naboth; ; PSA 27:12 David; ; DAN 6:24 Daniel; ; ACT 6:11–6:13 Stephen; ACT 17:5–17:7, ACT 24:5–24:9, ACT 25:7; ; ROM 3:8

False witness against believers is to be expected by them

MAT 5:11–5:12 parallel LUK 6:22–6:23 See also MAT 24:9–24:10; ACT 19:9

title: 8752: false worship
content:
Forms of worship that are not worthy of God, especially worship offered without sincerity and obedience or that is contrary to the commands of God.

Examples of false worship

Worship conducted in disobedience to God

LEV 10:1–10:2 See also NUM 3:2–3:4; 1SA 15:1–15:23; 2KI 17:33

Worship and sacrifices offered by those who were not priests

1SA 13:11–13:14 See also 2CH 26:19–26:20

Insincere worship

ISA 29:13 See also MAT 15:8–15:9; MRK 7:6–7:7; COL 2:23

Worship lacking in due humility and reverence

MAT 6:5 See also LUK 18:10–18:14

Worship conducted in ignorance of God

JHN 4:22 See also ACT 17:22–17:23

Scripture vividly contrasts false worship with true worship

True worship involves the worshipper's heart, soul and mind

DEU 6:5 parallels MAT 22:37, MRK 12:30, LUK 10:27

True worship is costly

2SA 24:24; ; MRK 12:41–12:44; ; ROM 12:1 True worship involves the whole of a person's life and not just formal acts of worship.

True worship is in the spirit

JHN 4:23–4:24 See also ISA 29:23; PHP 3:3; 1TI 2:9; HEB 12:28

title: 8753: favouritism
content:
The unfair treatment of a person or group in preference to another. Favouritism is shown in Scripture as causing division both in the family and in the church. It is warned against in the administration of justice. The human tendency to partiality is contrasted with God's impartial dealings.

Favouritism in family life

Isaac's preference for Esau

GEN 25:23, GEN 25:28

Rebekah's preference for Jacob

GEN 27:6–27:10

Jacob's preference for Joseph

GEN 37:3–37:4

Elkanah's preference for Hannah

1SA 1:5–1:6

The child of a favourite wife must not receive preferential treatment

DEU 21:15–21:16

Favouritism in church relationships

In the treatment of widows

ACT 6:1

James warned against favouring rich Christians

JAS 2:1–2:4, JAS 2:8–2:9

Paul warned Timothy against showing favouritism

1TI 5:21

Justice must be impartial

LEV 19:15 See also EXO 23:3; DEU 16:19; JOB 13:10; PSA 82:2; PRO 24:23, PRO 28:21; MAL 2:9

God has no favourites

ROM 2:11 See also JOB 34:19; MAT 5:45

God has no favourite nation

ACT 10:34–10:35 See also ROM 2:10; EPH 6:8–6:9

God does not differentiate between Jewish and Gentile Christians

ACT 15:7–15:9; ; ROM 10:12–10:13

God judges all without favouritism

DEU 10:17; ; 2CH 19:7; ; ROM 2:9; ; COL 3:25; ; 1PE 1:17

title: 8754: fear
content:
An attitude of anxiety or distress, caused by concern over a threat to one's future. Scripture provides numerous examples of situations in which fear is experienced. It declares, however, that God alone is to be feared, and moments of human fear can be opportunities for deepening faith in him.

Reverent fear of God commended

PRO 1:7 See also DEU 6:13, DEU 31:12–31:13; JOS 4:24, JOS 24:14; 1SA 12:24; PSA 2:11, PSA 34:7–34:9; PRO 15:33; ECC 12:13; ISA 33:6; REV 14:7

Fear of natural phenomena

PSA 91:5; JON 1:4–1:5 See also GEN 19:30; JOB 5:22; ECC 12:5; ISA 7:25; MAT 8:26; REV 11:13

Fear of the unnatural

Fear of thoughts and visions

DAN 4:5; ACT 10:4 See also 1SA 3:15; JOB 4:13–4:15; ISA 21:4; DAN 8:17, DAN 10:11–10:12; MAT 1:20, MAT 28:4; LUK 1:12–1:13, LUK 1:29–1:30, LUK 2:9–2:10

Fear of the unknown or the abnormal

MAT 14:26–14:27 parallels MRK 6:50, JHN 6:19–6:20ACT 5:5 See also EXO 20:18, EXO 34:30 The radiance of Moses' face reflected God's glory and made the Israelites afraid; DEU 5:5; 1SA 4:7; NEH 6:16; JER 10:2; DAN 5:9 Belshazzar's fear at the writing on the wall; JON 1:10; MAT 17:6 the fear of the disciples at the transfiguration; MAT 27:54; MRK 5:33, MRK 9:32, MRK 16:8; LUK 5:10, LUK 8:37 Fear seized the people when the Gerasene demoniac was healed; LUK 9:34; JHN 19:8; ACT 19:17

Fear of embarrassment or shame

GEN 3:10 See also ISA 54:4; JHN 3:20; 2CO 12:20

Fear of the future

JER 51:46 See also ISA 41:23; MRK 10:32; LUK 12:32; ACT 27:24

Fear of persecution

EZR 4:4; JHN 12:42–12:43 See also 1KI 19:3; JHN 7:13, JHN 9:22, JHN 20:19; 1PE 3:14; REV 2:10

Fear of death

HEB 2:14–2:15 See also PSA 55:4–55:5; MRK 5:36 parallel LUK 8:50; ACT 23:10

Fear of people

Of enemies

EXO 14:10; 1SA 7:7 See also NUM 22:3; JDG 7:3; 1SA 17:24, 1SA 17:11; 2SA 10:19; 2CH 12:5; PSA 27:1–27:3, PSA 56:1–56:4; ISA 20:5, ISA 41:5; JER 22:25, JER 41:18; OBA 1:9

Of one's own family

GEN 32:11, GEN 45:3; JDG 9:21 See also GEN 31:31, GEN 32:7, GEN 42:4, GEN 50:19; JDG 6:27

Of particular people

1SA 15:24; 1CO 2:3 See also GEN 26:7; EXO 2:14; DEU 2:4; 1SA 18:15 Saul's fear of David; 2SA 3:11; NEH 2:2 Nehemiah's fear before the king; EST 7:6; JER 26:21, JER 38:19; MAT 2:22; MRK 12:12; LUK 19:21; ACT 9:26 the disciples fear of Paul, not believing his conversion; 1CO 16:10; 2CO 7:15; GAL 2:12

Of human beings in general

PRO 29:25 See also DEU 1:17; ISA 51:7

Fear of judgment

EZK 11:8; ACT 24:25 See also 1SA 28:20; 1CH 21:30; ISA 33:14; JER 17:18, JER 30:5, JER 42:15–42:16; EZK 12:18, EZK 27:35; ZEC 9:5; 1JN 4:18 Christians, assured of God's love, no longer fear judgment; REV 18:10, REV 18:15

Fear as a deterrent

ROM 13:4 See also DEU 13:11, DEU 17:13, DEU 19:20, DEU 21:21; JOB 19:28–19:29

Fear as an opportunity for faith

title: 8755: folly
content: A human attitude of lack of wisdom or contempt for wisdom, which shows itself in a lack of understanding and obedience. Scripture contrasts human foolishness with divine wisdom, and indicates the serious consequences of a rejection of the wisdom of God.

title: 8756: folly, examples of
content:
Human folly is seen in rebellion against God, ignoring his way and will, a failure to understand him: and moral or spiritual irresponsibility.

Examples of human folly

The folly of God's people

JER 4:22 See also DEU 32:6 rejecting God; JER 10:8 worshipping idols; HOS 7:11 seeking foreign help rather than trusting God

The folly of Israel's leaders

JER 10:21 The shepherds are those entrusted with the task of guiding and caring for God's people; EZK 13:3 See also MAT 23:16–23:17

Particular demonstrations of human folly

NUM 12:1–12:11 Aaron and Miriam; 1SA 13:13, 1SA 26:21; 1SA 25:25 Nabal. In Hebrew this name means “fool”.; 2SA 24:10 parallel 1CH 21:8; 2CH 16:7–16:9 Asa, king of Judah; ; ISA 19:11–19:13 Pharaoh's advisors; ; MAT 7:26 the foolish builder; ; MAT 25:1–25:3 the foolish virgins; ; LUK 12:16–12:21 the rich fool; ; GAL 3:13 the Galatian Christians

Paul's ``foolishness''

2CO 11:16–11:21 Paul engages in what he admits is the foolish boasting of his accomplishments in order to challenge the claims of false “apostles”. See also 2CO 11:1, 2CO 12:6, 2CO 12:11

God's wisdom regarded as ``foolishness''

1CO 1:18 See also HOS 9:7; ZEC 11:15; 1CO 1:20–1:25, 1CO 1:27, 1CO 4:10

Human wisdom is foolishness to God

1CO 3:19 See also JOB 12:17; ISA 29:14, ISA 44:25, ISA 55:8; JER 50:36; ROM 1:22

title: 8757: folly, effects of
content:
The attitude that leads to a closing of the mind towards God and his truth, and a false self-confidence, which results in being easily led astray, failure to see danger, unpreparedness and ultimate ruin.

Folly gives a false basis for confidence

Contempt for God's wisdom

PRO 1:7 See also JOB 28:28; PSA 14:1, PSA 85:8, PSA 111:10; PRO 1:20–1:27, PRO 12:1, PRO 18:2

Blindness to God's truth

EPH 5:17 See also PSA 92:6; ECC 5:1–5:4; JER 5:4; LUK 11:39–11:40 hypocrisy in worship; ROM 1:21; 1CO 15:36 failure to understand the nature of death and resurrection; 2TI 2:23; TIT 3:9 futile controversies

Rebellion against God's authority

PSA 107:17; ; JER 5:21–5:25

Self-reliance

PRO 28:26 See also PRO 11:28, PRO 12:15, PRO 14:12; LUK 12:20

Folly cannot be hidden

ECC 10:3 See also PSA 69:5; PRO 12:23, PRO 13:16, PRO 15:2; 2TI 3:9

Folly opens the way to deception

PRO 14:8

Being led astray

PRO 14:15 See also PRO 7:7–7:23, PRO 9:13–9:18; ECC 7:26; HOS 7:11; GAL 3:1

Failing to see danger

PRO 22:3 See also ECC 4:13

Being unprepared

MAT 25:10

The consequences of folly

Destruction and ruin

PRO 1:32 See also PRO 5:23, PRO 10:8; ECC 7:17; 1TI 6:9

Shame

PRO 3:35 See also PRO 18:13; ISA 44:9; JER 8:9

Grief to parents

PRO 17:25 See also PRO 10:1, PRO 15:20, PRO 17:21

Punishment

PRO 16:22 See also PSA 38:5; PRO 18:6, PRO 26:3

Exclusion from God's way of salvation

ISA 35:8 See also MAT 25:10–25:12

Folly is persistent

PRO 27:22 See also PRO 15:14, PRO 26:11

Remedies for folly

The forgiveness of foolish actions

NUM 12:11; ; JOB 42:8; ; PSA 85:8; ; TIT 3:3–3:5

Discipline

PRO 19:25, PRO 21:11, PRO 22:15, PRO 29:15

Wisdom and instruction

PRO 8:5, PRO 14:33; ; ISA 29:24; ; ROM 2:20

title: 8759: fools
content: Those who lack wisdom and understanding, especially in relation to God.

resource.label: 8761: fools, in teaching of Jesus Christ

title: 8760: fools, characteristics of
content:
Scripture portrays fools as those who have rejected God and his ways and are unable or unwilling to appreciate the wisdom of knowing and obeying him.

The world regards Christians as fools

1CO 4:10 See also 1CO 1:26–1:31

The world regards the gospel as foolish

1CO 1:18 See also 1CO 1:20–1:25

Fools do not believe in God

PSA 53:1 parallel PSA 14:1 See also ROM 1:21

Fools do not trust God

HOS 7:11 See also 2CH 16:7–16:9; ISA 19:11–19:13, ISA 30:1

Fools lack knowledge of God

JER 4:22 See also JER 5:4, JER 5:21; PSA 92:6; LUK 24:25; EPH 5:15–5:17

The behaviour of fools

Fools worship idols

JER 10:8 See also JER 10:14 parallel JER 51:17; ROM 1:22–1:23

Fools act in a godless manner

ISA 32:6 See also PSA 94:5–94:8; PRO 10:23; ECC 7:25; JER 4:22

Fools are dishonest

JER 17:11

Fools give vent to their anger

PRO 29:11 See also ECC 7:9

Fools are disobedient

1SA 13:13 See also 2SA 24:10 parallel 1CH 21:8; PSA 107:17; PRO 10:8

Fools despise instruction and discipline

PRO 1:22 See also PRO 1:28–1:33, PRO 5:23, PRO 12:15; ISA 65:2; JER 18:12; EZK 3:7

The speech of fools

Fools speak unwisely

PRO 18:6–18:7 See also ECC 10:12; EPH 5:4

Fools are slanderous

PRO 10:18 See also 2PE 2:15

Fools are mockers

PRO 14:9 See also PRO 1:22, PRO 14:6, PRO 23:9, PRO 24:9

Fools love quarrelling and dissension

PRO 20:3 See also PRO 19:1; 1TI 1:4, 1TI 6:4; 2TI 2:23; TIT 3:9

The words of fools are empty

PRO 15:2 See also PRO 14:7, PRO 26:7; ECC 9:17, ECC 10:14

Fools rely on themselves

PRO 12:15 See also PRO 14:12, PRO 28:26

Fools rely on words, not deeds

JAS 2:20 See also ECC 5:4; LUK 11:39–11:40

title: 8761: fools, in teaching of Jesus Christ
content:
Jesus Christ speaks about those whose words and actions demonstrate opposition to, or disregard for, the wisdom of God revealed in his words and through the Scriptures, and in parables points to the serious consequences of folly.

The foolishness of the Pharisees

Their blindness

MAT 23:16–23:17 The Pharisees demonstrate foolishness by attaching undue significance to what is less important whilst neglecting what really matters. See also MAT 7:3 parallel LUK 6:41; MAT 15:14 parallel LUK 6:39; MAT 23:23–23:24

Their hypocrisy

LUK 11:39–11:40 The Pharisees were concerned with the externals of religion. Jesus Christ is concerned, also, with the inner life. See also MAT 12:35–12:36, MAT 23:25–23:28

The foolishness of the disciples

LUK 24:25 See also MAT 15:16–15:20 parallel MRK 7:20–7:23; MRK 8:17 parallel MAT 16:9; MRK 9:32, MRK 16:12–16:14

Fools in Jesus Christ's parables

The rich fool

LUK 12:16–12:21 The foolishness of trusting in wealth and not in God. See also JOB 27:16–27:19; DAN 4:30–4:31; MAT 6:19

The foolish builder

MAT 7:24–7:27 parallel LUK 6:49 See also PRO 1:28–1:33; ISA 65:2; JER 5:21–5:25, JER 13:10; EZK 3:7

The foolish virgins

MAT 25:1–25:13 The foolishness of being unprepared for the coming of God's kingdom. See also MRK 13:35–13:36; LUK 12:35–12:36

The seriousness of the term ``fool''

MAT 5:22 See also PRO 1:32; ECC 7:17

title: 8763: forgetting
content:
The process of accidentally or deliberately failing to remember people, events or ideas. Scripture rebukes those who forget the past work of God in history or in their lives or who neglect their present responsibilities towards God in order to please themselves.

Causes of forgetting

Forgetting can be deliberate

2PE 3:5

Forgetting can be caused by idolatry

JER 23:25–23:27 See also DEU 32:15–32:18; JDG 3:7; JER 18:15; HOS 2:13

Forgetting can be caused by pride

HOS 13:4–13:6 See also 2CH 26:16; PSA 10:4

Forgetting can be caused by drinking

PRO 31:4–31:5 See also GEN 9:20–9:21; MAT 24:45–24:51 parallel LUK 12:42–12:46

Forgetting can be caused by affliction

PSA 102:4 See also GEN 41:28–41:31; LAM 3:17–3:20

Forgetting people

GEN 40:23 See also JOB 19:13–19:15; PSA 31:11–31:12

Forgetting God

DEU 32:18 See also JDG 2:10–2:13; 1SA 12:9–12:10

Forgetting God's acts in the past

PSA 78:11–78:20 See also JDG 8:33–8:34; NEH 9:16–9:17; PSA 106:7–106:13

Consequences of forgetting God

Forgetting God brings suffering on the individual

PSA 50:22 See also 1SA 12:9; ISA 17:10–17:11

Forgetting God brings suffering on others

2SA 12:9 David's forgetting of God in his adultery with Bathsheba led to her husband Uriah suffering death through David's manipulation of events. See also PSA 106:13–106:15; JER 3:21

Forgetting God brings destruction on the nation

DEU 8:19–8:20 See also ISA 65:11–65:12; HOS 8:14

Warnings not to forget God

DEU 6:12 See also DEU 4:9, DEU 8:10–8:14; 2KI 17:35–17:38

People may sometimes feel that God has forgotten them

PSA 13:1 See also PSA 42:9–42:10, PSA 44:23–44:24; ISA 49:14; MAT 27:46 parallel MRK 15:34; PSA 22:1

God promises never to forget his people

ISA 44:21 See also ISA 49:15–49:16; HEB 6:10

Things God urges believers to forget

ISA 43:18 See also PHP 3:13–3:15

title: 8764: forgetting God
content:
Scripture warns people how easy it is to forget God in the varying circumstances of life and to fail to give him his due place, and points out the consequences of so doing.

Warnings not to forget God

Forgetting God's past acts

DEU 4:9 See also DEU 9:7–9:8; ISA 51:12–51:13

Forgetting God's covenant

DEU 4:23 See also 2KI 17:38

Forgetting God's ways

ISA 55:6–55:8 See also DEU 18:9–18:13; 1KI 2:1–2:4

Reasons why people forget God

Easy circumstances

DEU 6:10–6:12 See also DEU 8:10–8:14

Idolatry

JDG 8:33–8:34 See also EXO 32:1–32:8; DEU 12:29–12:31; 1KI 11:4–11:6

Pride and stubbornness

NEH 9:16 See also DEU 9:12–9:13; 2KI 17:14–17:17; JER 7:22–7:26

HOS 1:2 See also JER 3:6–3:10; HOS 4:10–4:13, HOS 5:4

DEU 16:1–16:3, DEU 16:9–16:12; ; 1CO 11:23–11:26

God's challenge to those who forget him

God's call to those who forget him

JER 3:19–3:22 See also REV 2:4–2:5, REV 3:20

God's grace even when his people do forget him

ISA 49:15–49:16 See also DEU 4:25–4:31; NEH 9:29–9:31

title: 8765: grudge
content:
A persistent feeling of ill will or resentment held by one person against another, often as the result of an injury or insult. Christians are not to bear grudges against others; instead they are to forgive those who have wronged them.

Examples of those who held grudges

Esau against Jacob

GEN 27:41

Joseph's brothers and Joseph

GEN 37:4 See also GEN 37:5, GEN 37:8, GEN 37:18–37:19, GEN 37:23–37:24, GEN 50:15

The Israelites against Moses and Aaron

NUM 11:1, NUM 14:1–14:4, NUM 14:27

Saul against David

1SA 18:7–18:9

Ahab against Elijah

1KI 18:16–18:17, 1KI 21:20, 1KI 22:8

Herodias against John the Baptist

MRK 6:18–6:19

The disciples against others

See also MAT 26:6–26:9 parallel MRK 14:3–14:5; JHN 12:3–12:6

The Sadducees against the apostles

ACT 5:17

The Jews against Stephen

ACT 7:54

GEN 4:4–4:8

GEN 37:18–37:20

MRK 6:22–6:24, MRK 6:27–6:28

In the OT

In Jesus Christ's teaching

MRK 7:21–7:23 parallel MAT 15:19–15:20

In the apostles' teaching

ROM 12:17–12:21; 1TH 5:15 See also GAL 5:15, GAL 5:19–5:21; PHP 2:13–2:15; COL 3:8; 2TI 2:24; JAS 3:14–3:16; 1PE 2:1

MAT 5:43–5:47 See also MAT 18:21–18:35; COL 3:13

title: 8766: heresies
content:
Teachings held by a factional religious party which deny some aspect of established doctrine. NT writers give no toleration to heresies in the church.

HEB 13:9 See also GAL 1:6–1:7; 2TI 4:3–4:4

The party of the Pharisees

ACT 26:5 See also ACT 15:5; PHP 3:5–3:6

The party of the Sadducees

ACT 23:8 See also MAT 22:23 parallels MRK 12:18, LUK 20:27

Christianity was perceived as a heresy within Judaism

ACT 24:14 See also ACT 24:5, ACT 28:22

The imposition of Jewish regulations on Gentile converts

ACT 15:1 See also GAL 6:12–6:13; 1TI 1:3–1:7; TIT 1:10

Heresy condemned

title: 8767: hypocrisy
content:
An outward pretence masking an inner reality. Scripture condemns hypocrisy, especially in matters of faith. Believers should express their commitment to God in their words and their deeds, as well as in their inner motivation.

The origin of hypocrisy

JER 17:9 See also HOS 10:2 Israel; MRK 7:21–7:22 parallel MAT 15:19

The expression of hypocrisy

Insincere motives

MAT 6:2 See also MAT 6:5, MAT 6:16, MAT 15:7–15:9, MAT 22:18, MAT 23:5–23:7

When deeds do not match words

ISA 29:13 See also MAT 15:7–15:8 parallel MRK 7:6; PRO 26:24–26:26; JER 9:8, JER 12:2; EZK 33:31; MAT 23:28; ROM 2:17–2:24; JAS 2:14–2:26

A tendency to judge others

MAT 7:5 parallel LUK 6:41 See also ROM 2:1

The alternative to hypocrisy

HEB 10:22 See also PSA 24:3–24:4, PSA 26:4, PSA 32:2; JAS 3:17, JAS 4:8; 1PE 2:1–2:3

JER 6:13 See also JER 8:8

The Pharisees

MRK 12:38–12:40 See also MAT 23:1–23:32; LUK 12:1–12:2, LUK 12:56

Peter and Barnabas

GAL 2:12–2:13 By acting in this way, Peter was denying his own conviction that Gentiles could be saved by faith without having to submit to the law.

2CO 1:12 See also 2CO 2:17; 1TH 2:3–2:10

title: 8768: idolatry
content: The worship or adoration of anyone or anything other than the LORD God. Idolatry includes the worship of other gods, such as those of the nations surrounding Israel, images or idols and the creation itself.

title: 8769: idolatry, in OT
content:
Scripture provides illustrations of idolatry from various periods in the history of the people of God. Idolatry is seen as a constant temptation for believers, especially in times of national or personal stress.

Idolatry among the Gentiles

JDG 11:24, JDG 16:23–16:24; ; 2KI 5:18; ; ISA 36:18–36:20, ISA 37:38, ISA 46:1; ; EZK 8:14; ; ACT 14:11–14:13; ; 1CO 8:5

Idolatry among God's people

In patriarchal times

JOS 24:2 See also GEN 31:30, GEN 31:34 these household gods may have been either masks or statuettes; GEN 35:2

In the Mosaic period

EXO 32:4

In the period of the judges

JDG 17:5 See also JDG 10:6

In the early monarchy

1KI 11:10 See also 1KI 12:28 The golden calves were perhaps pedestals on which the LORD was thought to sit.

In the middle monarchy

1KI 16:33 An Asherah pole was probably a crude carved wooden image of a Canaanite fertility goddess. See also 1KI 11:7–11:8, 1KI 16:32

In the late monarchy

2KI 21:2–21:6

After the fall of Jerusalem

EZK 8:10 See also EZK 8:3, EZK 8:14, EZK 8:16

Objects of false worship

DEU 4:19 See also DEU 17:3; JOB 31:26

Other objects of worship

DEU 4:28 See also DEU 16:22 sacred stones; 1KI 12:31 high places; ISA 1:29 oaks

The burning of children

2KI 23:10

The superstitious use of religious symbols

2KI 18:4 See also JDG 8:27 The ephod was a priestly garment sometimes subject to excessive veneration.

Sexual deviance

DEU 23:17 See also 1KI 14:24; HOS 4:14

title: 8770: idolatry, in NT
content:
The NT world included many religions which promoted the worship of idols. Idolatry was thus of continuing importance to NT writers, especially Paul.

Idolatry in the Gentile world

ACT 17:16 See also ACT 14:11–14:13, ACT 17:22–17:23, ACT 19:24; 1CO 8:5; GAL 4:8

Criticism of idolatry

Idolatry leads to other sinful behaviour

ROM 1:24 Verses 22 and 24–25 show the link between idolatry and immoral conduct.

Idolatry is an offence against the doctrine of creation

ROM 1:20 See also ACT 17:24–17:29

Idols are futile and degrading

ROM 1:22–1:23 See also 1CO 8:4, 1CO 10:19, 1CO 12:2

Idolatrous worship of human beings

ACT 12:22 See also LUK 20:24–20:25 Jesus Christ opposes the hypocrisy which objected to Roman coinage as idolatrous on the grounds that the emperor's head infringed the Ten Commandments; ACT 28:6

Demonic powers are involved with idolatry

1CO 10:20 See also REV 9:20, REV 13:4

Food sacrificed to idols

ACT 15:20 See also ROM 14:2–14:3, ROM 14:6; 1CO 8:4–8:13, 1CO 10:14–10:31

Encounters with idolatrous practice

ACT 19:28 See also ACT 14:11–14:18, ACT 17:18–17:31

Spiritual idolatry

1JN 5:21 “idols” here may well refer to a wide range of God-substitutes.

The temptations of Jesus Christ present three main kinds of spiritual idolatry

Possessions

MAT 4:6 parallel LUK 4:9 See also LUK 3:8, LUK 10:29, LUK 18:11–18:12, LUK 18:21; ROM 2:19

Power

MAT 4:8–4:9 parallel LUK 4:6–4:7 See also LUK 9:54–9:55, LUK 23:39; JHN 18:10–18:11, JHN 19:10; PHP 2:6; JAS 4:6, JAS 4:10

content:
Scripture presents idolatry as absurd and irrational, offensive to God and a source of spiritual and moral danger.

The absurdity of making idols

PSA 135:17–135:18 parallel PSA 115:5–115:8 See also ISA 2:8, ISA 44:15–44:17, ISA 46:6; JER 1:16; MIC 5:13

title: 8773: jealousy
content:
A strong feeling of possessiveness, often caused by the possibility that something which belongs, or ought to belong, to one is about to be taken away. The word can be used in a positive sense (e.g., the jealousy of God), meaning a passionate commitment to something which rightly belongs to one. It can also be used in a negative sense (e.g., human jealousy), to mean a self-destructive human emotion similar to envy.

God's jealousy for his people

God's jealousy demands an exclusive response from his people

EXO 20:4–20:6 See also EXO 34:14; DEU 32:16, DEU 32:21

God pictured as a jealous husband with an unfaithful wife

EZK 16:1–16:63

God is jealously protective of his people

JOL 2:18 See also ISA 26:11; ZEC 1:14–1:15, ZEC 8:2

God possessiveness expresses itself in judgment on his people's unfaithfulness

DEU 4:24 See also DEU 6:15, DEU 29:20; JOS 24:19; 1KI 14:22; EZK 23:25, EZK 36:6; NAM 1:2; ZEP 1:18, ZEP 3:8

Human jealousy arises from sin

MRK 7:21–7:23 parallel MAT 15:19–15:20

Human jealousy can be destructive

title: 8774: legalism
content:

title: 8778: materialism
content: The outlook on life which treats material possessions as being of supreme importance or which denies the spiritual aspects of life. Scripture notes the dangers of material wealth and possessions. The accumulation of wealth can easily become a god in itself and lead people astray from the worship of the true God. Yet it is not money itself, but the love of money, which is seen by Scripture as a fundamental cause of evil.

title: 8785: opposition
content: The act of resisting individuals and forces. Scripture stresses the reality of sin and evil in the world and calls upon believers to resist them. content: Scripture indicates that believers can expect to face hardship, ridicule and oppression, from individuals and state authorities, on account of their faith.
