Persecution is part of the tribulation of the church

MAT 24:7–24:10 See also 2TH 2:3–2:4; REV 6:11

Persecution is sometimes part of God's judgment on his people

LAM 4:16–4:19 See also JER 6:22–6:26, JER 32:26–32:29, JER 39:5–39:10

title: 8796: persecution, forms of
content:
Scripture identifies a number of reasons why individuals and governmments may attempt to persecute believers and also the methods by which they may carry this out.

The motives for persecution

Envy

ACT 5:17–5:18 See also GEN 26:14–26:15, GEN 37:4, GEN 37:8; 1SA 18:8–18:9; PSA 106:16; DAN 6:1–6:5; MAT 27:18; ACT 13:45; JAS 3:16

Fear

LUK 22:2 See also EXO 1:10; 1SA 18:15, 1SA 18:29; MAT 2:3; ACT 19:23–19:27

Hatred

1JN 3:12 See also GEN 4:3–4:8; 1KI 22:8 parallel 2CH 18:7; JHN 7:7

The means of persecution

Deception

PSA 38:12 See also 1KI 21:10; EZR 4:12–4:13; PSA 35:11; JER 20:10; AMO 7:10; MAT 5:11; JHN 7:12; ACT 6:11, ACT 21:21, ACT 21:28, ACT 24:5

Threats

PSA 10:7 See also EZR 4:4; DAN 3:15; JHN 9:22; ACT 4:17

Ridicule

NEH 4:1–4:3 See also HOS 9:7; 1CO 4:13; HEB 13:13; REV 2:9

Ostracism

MAT 10:22 See also JHN 9:29, JHN 9:34, JHN 12:42, JHN 16:2

Violence

ROM 8:35 See also JER 38:6; MAT 10:17 parallel MRK 13:9; JHN 21:18–21:19; ACT 5:40, ACT 16:37; 2CO 11:25; GAL 6:17; HEB 11:36–11:39

How God deals with persecutors

1TI 1:13 See also DAN 4:34–4:35; ACT 12:1, ACT 12:21–12:23; GAL 1:23

title: 8797: persecution, attitudes to
content:
Scripture outlines the attitudes which believers should adopt in the face of persecution, laying particular emphasis upon the faithfulness of God, the example of Jesus Christ and the need for patience and hope by believers.

The call to endure in the face of persecution

Passively

PSA 119:87 See also MAT 10:22, MAT 10:28; 1CO 4:12; 2TH 1:4; JAS 5:8

Actively

HEB 12:1 See also EPH 6:10–6:20; 2TI 2:3; 1PE 5:9; REV 2:3

Attitudes believers are to adopt in facing persecution

Living holy and forgiving lives

1PE 2:12 See also MAT 5:44; ROM 12:19–12:20; 1PE 2:15, 1PE 2:23, 1PE 3:16

Rejoicing in suffering

ROM 5:3–5:5 See also PSA 30:5; MAT 5:11–5:12 parallel LUK 6:22–6:23; ACT 5:41, ACT 16:22–16:25; ROM 12:15; COL 1:24; 1PE 1:6, 1PE 1:8, 1PE 4:12, 1PE 4:16

Relying on the promise of God's grace to endure

LAM 3:22–3:23 See also PSA 18:17–18:19; NAM 1:7–1:8; ROM 8:18, ROM 8:35–8:39; 2TI 3:10–3:11; HEB 13:6; REV 3:10

Trusting in the promise of God's presence

HEB 13:5 See also PSA 23:4; ISA 43:2, ISA 43:5; MAT 28:20; 2CO 4:9

Praying always

EPH 6:18 See also PSA 35:24, PSA 38:15–38:16, PSA 129:5, PSA 143:9; MIC 7:7–7:8; LUK 6:28, LUK 18:7–18:8; 1PE 4:7

The certain prospect of victory over persecution

The triumph of Jesus Christ

1CO 15:25 See also OBA 1:21; PHP 3:20–3:21; 2TH 1:6–1:8; REV 11:15

The vindication of the saints

JUD 1:24 See also EZR 6:8; EST 6:11–6:13; PSA 126:1; DAN 6:26; HAG 2:22–2:23; 2TI 1:12; REV 2:10, REV 7:13–7:17, REV 12:11

Believers are to take heart from the example of Jesus Christ in facing persecution

The persecution of Jesus Christ was predicted in the OT

PSA 22:1–22:18; ; ISA 50:6, ISA 53:7–53:12

The fulfilment of these predictions

MAT 27:26–27:31 parallel MRK 15:15–15:20

The relevance of Jesus Christ's innocent suffering to believers

1PE 2:20–2:23 See also 1PE 3:14–3:17 suffering for the sake of righteousness; 1PE 4:13–4:14 rejoicing at sharing in Christ's sufferings

title: 8799: polytheism
content:
Belief in, and worship of, more than one god. It is forbidden in Scripture because God has revealed himself as the one true God. Israel in the OT and the church in the NT lived amongst polytheistic peoples. The Israelites shared in this worship and so came under God's judgment.

The uniqueness of God

There is only one true God

ISA 45:5–45:6 See also DEU 6:4, DEU 32:39; ISA 43:10, ISA 44:8

The contrast of the true God with idols

1TH 1:9 See also 1CH 16:26 parallel PSA 96:5; ISA 40:18–40:19, ISA 40:25–40:26; ACT 17:29; 1CO 8:4–8:6; GAL 4:8

Polytheism is expressly forbidden

Warnings against worshipping idols

EXO 20:23 See also EXO 20:3–20:5 parallel DEU 5:7–5:9; EXO 23:13; LEV 17:7

Polytheism compromises relationship with God

2KI 17:35–17:38 See also DEU 31:16; JER 11:10; 1CO 10:18–10:22

The challenge to Israel to worship God only

JOS 24:15 See also GEN 35:2–35:4; DEU 12:2–12:4; 1KI 18:21

Polytheism brings God's judgment

EXO 22:20; ; DEU 31:17–31:18; ; JOS 23:16; ; JER 11:11–11:13

Polytheism among Israel's neighbours

JDG 10:6 See also JDG 16:23; 1KI 11:33; 2KI 1:2, 2KI 17:29–17:33; ISA 46:1; JER 50:2; EZK 8:14

Polytheism among the Israelites

They were called to destroy foreign gods

NUM 33:51–33:52 See also EXO 23:24, EXO 34:12–34:13; DEU 12:2–12:3

They were seduced by foreign gods

2KI 17:15–17:18; JER 2:11 See also EXO 34:15–34:16; NUM 25:2; DEU 12:30, DEU 32:16–32:17; JDG 2:11–2:13; PSA 106:34–106:36; HOS 2:13, HOS 11:2

Polytheism among Israel's kings

1KI 11:5–11:7 Solomon; ; 1KI 12:28–12:29 Jeroboam, king of Israel; ; 1KI 16:30–16:33 Ahab, king of Israel; ; 2KI 16:3–16:4 Ahaz, king of Judah; ; 2KI 21:3–21:5 Manasseh, king of Judah

Examples of reforming kings

1KI 15:12–15:13 Asa, king of Judah; ; 2KI 18:4 Hezekiah, king of Judah; ; 2KI 23:12–23:15 Josiah, king of Judah

The character of polytheism in the OT

The physical representation of deities

LEV 26:1; ; 1KI 14:23; ; ISA 48:5

Cult prostitution

DEU 23:17; ; 1KI 14:24

Human sacrifice

LEV 18:21 to Molech; ; DEU 12:31; ; 2KI 3:26–3:27 to Chemosh; ; JER 19:5 to Baal; ; EZK 16:20–16:21

Self-mutilation

1KI 18:28–18:29

Polytheism in the NT

It was widespread

ACT 17:23 The Athenians were fearful of offending a god by failing to give him attention. Any omissions were covered in the designation “UNKNOWN GOD”. See also ACT 14:11–14:13, ACT 19:35; 1CO 8:5–8:6

The worship of man-made idols

1CO 12:2 See also ACT 17:16, ACT 19:26; ROM 1:20–1:23; 1CO 10:19–10:20 Idols in themselves are nothing, but they represent a demonic presence which lies behind polytheistic worship.

title: 8800: prejudice
content:
Seen mainly in Scripture as a bias against places, peoples and ideas. It is sometimes so firmly rooted as to resist all contrary evidence.

Prejudice against places

JHN 1:46 See also JHN 7:41, JHN 7:52

Prejudice against people

Prejudice due to an attitude of superiority

JHN 7:49 See also 1SA 10:27, 1SA 25:10–25:11; JOB 30:1–30:10; ISA 65:5; LUK 18:11

Prejudice based on fear or jealousy

EXO 1:9–1:10, EXO 1:12–1:13; ; 1SA 18:8–18:9, 1SA 18:29

Prejudice against Jesus Christ

JHN 12:37 See also MAT 9:34; MRK 6:2–6:3; JHN 9:29, JHN 10:20

Prejudice may be based on false assumptions about people's behaviour

Hostility incorrectly assumed

GEN 12:11–12:12 See also GEN 20:1–20:2, GEN 26:1–26:11

Motives misunderstood

NUM 32:5–32:9 The leaders of Reuben and Gad chose to inhabit the fertile land in Transjordan but they were also prepared to cross the Jordan to help their brothers conquer the land. See also NUM 32:14, NUM 32:17; JOS 22:10–22:24; 2SA 10:3

Prejudice in terms of partiality

Favouritism

GEN 25:28, GEN 37:3, GEN 44:20, GEN 44:27–44:29

People are often prejudiced in favour of their own kind

MAT 5:46–5:47 parallel LUK 6:32–6:34 See also LUK 7:29, LUK 17:16; ACT 10:45; LUK 11:18

Prejudice on grounds of outward appearance or behaviour

JAS 2:3–2:4 See also 1SA 16:7; 2SA 14:25; ECC 9:16; JHN 8:15; ROM 14:1, ROM 14:3, ROM 14:10, ROM 14:13; 1CO 4:5; GAL 2:6

Prejudice due to race

EST 3:5–3:6 See also EZR 4:15–4:16; NEH 4:1–4:4; EST 3:8–3:14, EST 7:4; DAN 3:8–3:12, DAN 6:3–6:9, DAN 6:13

Partiality forbidden

EXO 23:3 See also LEV 19:15; JAS 2:9

God is not prejudiced

God is impartial

ACT 10:34 See also ROM 2:11; EPH 6:9; COL 3:25

Job falsely accuses God of partiality

JOB 9:16, JOB 9:20, JOB 9:30–9:31, JOB 10:15–10:17

Prejudice which no contrary evidence would change

LUK 16:31 See also 1SA 22:13–22:15; MAT 11:21–11:23, MAT 21:32; ACT 7:52, ACT 13:41

The Sadducees' prejudice against the resurrection

MAT 22:23 parallels MRK 12:18, LUK 20:27 See also ACT 4:1–4:3, ACT 23:8

title: 8801: presumption
content:
A form of self-confidence, which makes overconfident assumptions concerning one's importance and rights. It is criticised as a form of arrogance that is unacceptable among believers, whose lives should be characterised by humility.

Presumption is unacceptable

PSA 5:5; ISA 13:11 See also NUM 15:30; DEU 6:16, DEU 18:20; ISA 45:9; ROM 2:4, ROM 9:20; 1CO 10:9; JAS 4:13; 2PE 2:10

Examples of presumption

GEN 11:1–11:4 those preparing to build the tower of Babel in defiance of God; ; NUM 14:40–14:45 the Israelites, ignoring Moses' orders; ; LUK 12:16–12:21 the rich fool

Humility is commended in place of presumption

MIC 6:8 See also LUK 14:10, LUK 22:26; ROM 12:3; JAS 4:10; 1PE 5:5

title: 8802: pride
content: Arrogance or delusions of greatness on account of one's achievements, status or possessions. Scripture frequently speaks of God humbling the proud.

title: 8803: pride, evil of
content:
Pride is viewed as a great evil because it involves pretending to a greatness and glory that belong rightly to God alone.

The sinfulness of pride

It is condemned as evil

1SA 15:23; PRO 21:4; JAS 4:16 See also MRK 7:22–7:23; ROM 1:29–1:30; 2CO 12:20; 2TI 3:1–3:2; 1JN 2:16

It is a characteristic of Satan

EZK 28:2; 1TI 3:6 See also 2TH 2:4 the antichrist

Warnings against pride

In the book of Proverbs

PRO 16:5, PRO 16:18 See also PRO 3:7, PRO 3:34, PRO 6:16–6:17, PRO 11:2, PRO 25:6–25:7, PRO 25:27, PRO 26:12, PRO 27:1, PRO 29:23

Elsewhere in Scripture

PSA 119:21 See also LEV 26:191SA 2:3; PSA 12:2–12:3; JER 9:23–9:24 PSA 5:5, PSA 40:4, PSA 138:6; ISA 5:21; JER 13:15–13:17; MAT 23:12 parallel LUK 14:11 Jesus Christ's teaching on pride; ROM 12:16; 1CO 10:121PE 5:5; JAS 4:6; PRO 3:34

The gospel excludes pride

ROM 3:27 See also LUK 18:9–18:14; ROM 4:2–4:3, ROM 11:17–11:20; 1CO 1:26–1:31; EPH 2:8–2:9

Godliness involves rejecting pride

PRO 8:13 See also PSA 101:5, PSA 131:1; ROM 12:3; 1CO 13:4; GAL 6:14

resource.label: 6157: fall, of Satan and his angels

title: 8804: pride, examples of
content:
Scripture illustrates the many different ways in which pride manifests itself.

Pride in status

EXO 5:2 Pharaoh; ; 2KI 5:11 Naaman; 2KI 20:13; ; 2CH 32:25; EST 5:11–5:12 Haman; ISA 16:6; ; JER 48:29; ISA 47:8 Babylon; ; EZK 16:49–16:50 Sodom; ; EZK 28:2 the king of Tyre; EZK 31:3, EZK 31:10; DAN 5:23 Belshazzar; ; OBA 1:3 Edom; ; ZEP 2:15 Nineveh; MAT 23:6–23:7 parallels MRK 12:38–12:39, LUK 20:46; ; LUK 11:43; ACT 8:9 Simon the sorcerer; ; REV 18:7 Babylon the Great

Pride in strength

1SA 17:42 Goliath; ; 2KI 14:9–14:10 Amaziah, king of Judah; ; 2KI 18:33–18:35 the Assyrian commander; ISA 9:9–9:10; ; HOS 10:13; ISA 10:13 the king of Assyria; DAN 3:15, DAN 4:30; MAT 26:33–26:35 parallels MRK 14:29–14:31, LUK 22:33; ; JHN 13:37

Pride in wisdom

ISA 10:13 the king of Assyria; ; ACT 17:21; ; ROM 1:22; ; 1CO 1:20, 1CO 3:18

Proud ambition

ISA 14:13–14:14 the king of Babylon; ; 2TH 2:3–2:4 the antichrist

Spiritual pride

2KI 10:16; ; JOB 32:1, JOB 33:9; ; ISA 65:5; ; MAT 6:2, MAT 6:3, MAT 6:16; MAT 23:5, MAT 23:30; ; MRK 12:40 parallel LUK 20:47; ; LUK 16:14–16:15, LUK 18:9, LUK 18:11–18:12; ; JHN 9:40–9:41; LUK 10:29 an expert in the law; JHN 8:33, JHN 9:34; ; ROM 2:17–2:20; 1CO 4:7, 1CO 4:18; ; REV 3:17 the church in Laodicea

title: 8805: pride, results of
content:
The real nature of pride can be seen in the fact that it leads to many other evils and ends in destruction.

Pride leads to other forms of evil

Self-deception

GAL 6:3 See also DEU 8:17–8:18; ISA 16:6, ISA 47:10; JER 49:16 parallel OBA 1:3; 1CO 8:2; 1TI 6:3–6:4

Spiritual blindness

JER 43:2 See also DEU 8:14; NEH 9:16, NEH 9:29

A hard heart

PSA 36:2 See also PSA 10:3, PSA 52:1; DAN 5:20

A malicious spirit

PSA 119:85 See also PSA 73:8, PSA 140:5

Contempt for others

PSA 123:4 See also PSA 119:51; PRO 21:24

Quarrelling

PRO 13:10

Violence

PSA 73:6 See also EST 3:5–3:6; PSA 86:14

Injustice

PSA 119:78 See also PSA 56:2

Oppression

PSA 10:2 See also PSA 119:122; HAB 2:4–2:5

Contempt for God

PSA 10:4 See also 2KI 19:22

Pride may be accompanied by temporary prosperity

PSA 73:3 See also PSA 10:5

Pride ends in disaster

PRO 16:5, PRO 16:18 See also 2SA 22:28 parallel PSA 18:27; JOB 40:11–40:12; PSA 31:23, PSA 101:5; PRO 11:2, PRO 15:25, PRO 26:12, PRO 29:23; ISA 2:11–2:12, ISA 2:17, ISA 13:11, ISA 26:5; ZEP 3:11; MAL 4:1; LUK 1:51–1:52; 1TI 3:6

Examples of the proud being humbled

Pharaoh: EXO 14:28; ; NEH 9:10; 2CH 26:16 Uzziah; 2CH 32:21; ; ISA 10:12, ISA 10:16; 2CH 32:25 Hezekiah; ; EST 7:10 Haman; ; ISA 3:16–3:17 the women of Zion; ISA 13:19, ISA 14:11–14:15; ISA 23:9, ISA 25:10–25:12 Moab; ; ISA 28:1–28:3 Samaria; ISA 47:10–47:11; ; JER 50:31–50:32; JER 13:9; ; EZK 7:24; EZK 16:49–16:50 Sodom; EZK 28:5–28:9, EZK 28:17; EZK 30:6, EZK 32:12; DAN 4:30–4:33 Nebuchadnezzar; ; DAN 5:30 Belshazzar; ; AMO 6:8; ; ZEP 2:15 Nineveh; ; ZEC 9:6, ZEC 10:11 Assyria; ; MAT 11:23 Capernaum; ; ACT 12:21–12:23 Herod; ; REV 18:7–18:8 Babylon the Great

title: 8807: profanity
content:
Behaviour which dishonours God's name or brings it into disrepute. It is often the result of idolatry, injustice or irreverence. Scripture strongly admonishes God's people to avoid it.

General warnings against profanity

LEV 22:31–22:33 See also LEV 21:5–21:6

God's name profaned through idolatry

Through child sacrifice

LEV 18:21 See also LEV 20:3; DEU 12:29–12:31, DEU 18:9–18:13; 2KI 16:1–16:4 parallel 2CH 28:1–28:4; 2KI 17:16–17:17, 2KI 21:1–21:6 parallel 2CH 33:1–33:6; PSA 106:36–106:39; ISA 57:3–57:5; JER 32:32–32:35; EZK 16:20–16:22

Through the worship of idols

EZK 20:39 See also JER 44:25–44:28; EZK 20:31, EZK 43:6–43:9

God's name profaned through injustice and evil

MAL 2:10 See also JER 34:12–34:16; AMO 2:6–2:8, AMO 5:7–5:15; MIC 6:6–6:8

God's name profaned through false swearing

LEV 19:12 See also JER 5:1–5:2; MAT 5:33–5:37; JAS 5:12

God's name profaned through blasphemy

ISA 52:5–52:6 See also EXO 20:7 parallel DEU 5:11; LEV 24:10–24:16; ISA 37:23; 2PE 2:12

God's name profaned through irreverence

LEV 22:2 See also EZK 22:26; ZEP 3:1–3:4; MAL 1:6–1:14

God's name profaned in the sight of foreign nations

EZK 39:7 See also EZK 20:13–20:44, EZK 36:16–36:23; ROM 2:17–2:24; ISA 52:5

Penalties for profanity

LEV 20:1–20:5 See also JER 44:25–44:30; EZK 13:17–13:23, EZK 21:24–21:27, EZK 39:1–39:8; AMO 4:2–4:13, AMO 8:4–8:14; MAL 2:7–2:9

title: 8808: riches
content: Material possessions and wealth. Scripture stresses that riches originate from God: used wisely, they can be a blessing; used foolishly, they can lead people away from God.

title: 8809: riches, nature of
content:
God has created an abundance of good things. Those who have material wealth should understand its true nature and acknowledge God.

God and riches

All riches belong to God the Creator

PSA 24:1–24:2 See also JOB 41:11; PSA 50:12; HAG 2:8

God gives of his riches

1SA 2:7 See also ECC 5:19; 1CH 29:12; 2CH 1:12

God gives the ability to produce wealth

DEU 8:17–8:18 See also GEN 26:12–26:13; DEU 26:9–26:10

Riches may be a sign of God's blessing

PRO 10:22 See also 2CH 25:9; JOB 1:9–1:10; PSA 112:1–112:3, PSA 128:1–128:2; PRO 8:17–8:18

Riches should be thankfully received

1TI 4:4–4:5 See also MAT 14:19; ROM 1:21; COL 3:17

The character of earthly riches

Riches provide great opportunity for doing good

EXO 35:29; ; 1CH 29:6–29:7; ; LUK 12:33, LUK 16:9, LUK 19:8; ; ACT 4:34–4:35

Riches do not satisfy

ECC 5:10 See also PRO 13:11, PRO 27:20, PRO 27:24; ECC 4:8, ECC 6:7; LUK 12:18

Riches are insecure and uncertain

1TI 6:17 See also JOB 1:13–1:19; PRO 23:5, PRO 27:24; JER 48:36; MAT 6:19; 1PE 1:18; REV 18:14–18:20

Riches are for this life only

1JN 2:17 See also LUK 12:13–12:21; 1TI 6:6–6:8

title: 8810: riches, dangers of
content:
Material wealth can be a source of both physical and spiritual danger, against which believers are clearly warned to be on their guard.

Riches are spiritually dangerous

Love of riches a root of many evils

1TI 6:10 See also JOS 7:11, JOS 7:20–7:21; 1TI 3:3

They may lead to divided loyalty

MAT 6:24 parallel LUK 16:13 See also MAT 4:9–4:10; JAS 4:4

They may hinder people's response to the gospel

MAT 13:22 parallels MRK 4:19, LUK 8:14; ; MAT 19:21–19:22 parallels MRK 10:21–10:22, LUK 18:22–18:23

They may create false security

1TI 6:17 See also JOB 31:24–31:28; PSA 52:6–52:7; PRO 11:28; JER 49:4

They may make people proud

EZK 28:5 See also PSA 62:10; PRO 18:23, PRO 28:11; HOS 12:8

They may cause unbelief and anxiety

ECC 5:12 See also JOB 20:17–20:20; PRO 15:6

They may lead people to forget God

PRO 30:8–30:9 See also DEU 8:10–8:14, DEU 32:15; NEH 9:25–9:26; HOS 13:6

Riches are physically dangerous

Working for them may cause excessive tiredness

PRO 23:4 See also JHN 6:26–6:27

Enjoying them may lead to self-indulgence

JAS 5:5 See also HAG 1:3–1:5; MAT 23:25; LUK 16:19–16:21; 1TI 6:8–6:9

Misusing them may foster oppression and injustice

LEV 19:13 See also DEU 24:12–24:15; PRO 22:16; ISA 1:23; JER 22:13; MIC 6:12; MAL 3:5; JAS 2:6, JAS 5:4

title: 8811: riches, believers' attitudes towards
content:
God entrusts some of his people with material wealth. If this is to be a blessing, it must be used in God-honouring ways.

Believers may be blessed with riches

Riches can be a blessing from God

1CH 29:16 See also 1CH 29:14–29:15; JOB 1:9–1:102KI 4:1; MAT 8:20; LUK 6:20, LUK 16:20–16:22; ROM 15:26

The attitude of believers towards riches

They acknowledge that their riches come from God

1CH 29:12 See also ECC 5:19–5:20

They devote their riches to God's service

PRO 3:9–3:10 See also 1CH 29:1–29:9; ACT 4:32–4:37

They support gospel work and workers

LUK 8:1–8:3; ; ACT 16:15

They give to the poor

1JN 3:17 See also LUK 19:8; ACT 9:36–9:39; GAL 2:10

They are generous

1TI 6:18 See also DEU 15:10–15:11; 2CO 9:10–9:11

They remain humble

JAS 1:10–1:11

They do not trust in riches

1TI 6:17 See also JOB 31:24–31:28; PRO 11:28; JER 49:4

They do not set their heart on riches

PSA 62:10 See also LUK 12:29–12:30

Believers value heavenly riches most

MAT 6:20–6:21 See also LUK 12:33–12:34; 1TI 6:18–6:19

Examples of rich believers

Abraham

GEN 12:1–12:3, GEN 13:1–13:2

Solomon

2CH 1:11–1:12, 2CH 9:22

Hezekiah

2CH 32:27–32:29

Job

JOB 1:1–1:3

Joseph of Arimathea

ISA 53:9; ; MAT 27:57–27:60 parallels MRK 15:42–15:46, LUK 23:50–23:54, JHN 19:38–19:42

title: 8812: riches, ungodly use of
content:
Ungodly people often make the possession of wealth a priority. They do not understand the true nature of wealth, and they do not realise that they will have to face God in judgment.

The ungodly grow rich

PSA 73:12 See also LUK 19:21; JAS 2:6–2:7

The ungodly misuse riches

They often obtain their riches unjustly

PRO 10:2 See also 1KI 20:5; PRO 13:11, PRO 21:6, PRO 22:16; JER 17:11; MIC 2:1–2:5, MIC 6:10–6:12; HAB 2:6–2:11

They accumulate and hoard their riches

PRO 11:26 See also JOB 27:16–27:17; PRO 3:27; ECC 2:26, ECC 5:10–5:14; JAS 5:1–5:3

They trust in their riches

PSA 49:5–49:6 See also JOB 31:24; PSA 52:7; PRO 11:28; JER 9:23–9:24, JER 48:7

The ungodly suffer difficulties because of their riches

PRO 15:6 See also PRO 10:16, PRO 13:7–13:8, PRO 15:16–15:17

The ungodly, like all people, must leave their riches to others

PSA 49:10 See also PSA 39:6; ECC 2:18–2:21; LUK 12:20

Jesus Christ warned the rich of their danger

LUK 6:24 See also LUK 12:15, LUK 16:25

Examples of the ungodly rich

Nabal

1SA 25:2–25:3

Rich young ruler

MRK 10:17–10:23 parallels MAT 19:16–19:24, LUK 18:18–18:25

title: 8813: riches, spiritual
content:
Out of his infinite abundance God gives his people spiritual treasure. This, much more valuable than material wealth, is to be held in the highest esteem and sought after eagerly.

The riches of God

His wisdom and knowledge

ROM 11:33–11:36

His mercy, love and grace

EPH 2:4, EPH 3:8 See also ROM 2:4; EPH 2:7

His riches in Jesus Christ

COL 2:2–2:3 See also PHP 4:19; COL 1:27

God bestows spiritual riches on believers

His precious word

JOB 23:12; ; PSA 19:9–19:10, PSA 119:72, PSA 119:111, PSA 119:127

A wealth of spiritual qualities

ISA 33:5–33:6 See also PRO 2:1–2:5, PRO 15:6; 2CO 9:10–9:11; EPH 1:7–1:8; COL 2:2–2:3; JAS 2:5

A glorious gospel

2CO 4:7

A costly kingdom

See also MAT 13:44–13:46

A rich reward

RUT 2:12 See also 1SA 26:23; PSA 18:20; PRO 25:21–25:22; COL 3:24; HEB 10:35

A heavenly inheritance

ACT 20:32 See also EPH 1:13–1:14, EPH 1:18; COL 1:12, COL 3:24; 1PE 1:4

Christians and spiritual riches

Christians need to appreciate their spiritual riches

EPH 1:7–1:8 See also EPH 1:18; REV 2:9

Christians need to store up treasure in heaven

LUK 12:33 See also MAT 6:20; LUK 12:20–12:21; 1TI 6:19; HEB 11:26; REV 3:18

title: 8815: ridicule
content: Laughing others to scorn, publicly humiliating or making fun of them in a demeaning manner.

title: 8816: ridicule, nature of
content:
Scripture declares that ridicule of the weak, the poor and the godly is unacceptable. Those who ridicule them invite judgment upon themselves.

Warnings against ridicule

Ridicule is foolish

PRO 11:12 See also PRO 1:20–1:22, PRO 14:6, PRO 14:9

Ridicule creates trouble

PRO 9:12 See also PRO 19:29, PRO 22:10, PRO 29:8, PRO 30:17; MAT 5:22 “Raca” probably means “empty-head”, a term of derision.

Ridicule is a sign of the last days

2PE 3:3–3:4 See also JUD 1:18

Examples of ridicule

JDG 9:28–9:29, JDG 9:38; ; 1SA 17:41–17:44; ; 1KI 22:24; ; 2KI 2:23–2:24, 2KI 18:23–18:25; ; NEH 2:19, NEH 4:1–4:3

Ridicule associated with divine punishment

ISA 14:3–14:4 See also ISA 37:22–37:23; JER 49:17, JER 50:13; EZK 36:1–36:7; HAB 2:6; ZEP 2:15MIC 2:3–2:4 See also DEU 28:37; 1KI 9:6–9:9 parallel 2CH 7:19–7:22; JER 19:8, JER 24:9; EZK 5:14–5:15, EZK 23:32, EZK 22:3–22:5; HOS 7:16; MIC 6:16

Prophets ridicule idolatry

1KI 18:27 See also ISA 41:7, ISA 41:21–41:24, ISA 44:12–44:17, ISA 46:1–46:2; JER 10:3–10:5

title: 8817: ridicule, objects of
content:
Ridicule of God and of believers is to be expected, but it will bring divine retribution upon its perpetrators.

God ridiculed

PSA 74:10–74:18 See also 2KI 19:4 parallel ISA 37:4

Jesus Christ mocked

LUK 22:63–22:65 parallels MAT 26:67–26:68, MRK 14:65 See also LUK 23:11; MAT 27:27–27:31 parallel MRK 15:16–15:20; JHN 19:1–19:3; MAT 27:39–27:44 parallels MRK 15:29–15:32, LUK 23:35–23:37

God's messengers scorned

2CH 36:15–36:16 See also 2CH 30:6–30:10; ACT 2:1–2:13, ACT 17:17–17:18, ACT 17:32; HEB 11:36

God's people may suffer ridicule for their faith

PSA 22:6–22:8 JOB 12:4, JOB 16:10, JOB 19:18, JOB 30:1, JOB 30:9; PSA 35:15–35:25, PSA 42:10, PSA 69:10–69:12, PSA 79:4, PSA 89:50–89:51, PSA 123:3–123:4; ; JER 20:7; ; LAM 2:15–2:16, LAM 3:14, LAM 3:63

Divine judgment because of ridicule

ZEP 2:8–2:11 See also PRO 3:34; ISA 28:22

God ridicules his enemies

PSA 2:4–2:5 See also PSA 59:8

title: 8819: scoffing
content:
Treating individuals, people, ideas or values with contempt or ridicule. Scripture indicates that God's word and his people can expect to be treated with contempt by the world.

Objects of scoffing

Nations punished by God

JER 19:8 See also 1KI 9:6–9:9; JER 49:17, JER 50:13; LAM 2:15–2:17; ZEP 2:13–2:15

God's messengers

2CH 36:15–36:16

Reasons for scoffing

Unbelief

2PE 3:3–3:4 See also ACT 13:41; HAB 1:5; JUD 1:17–1:19

Arrogance

HAB 1:10 See also PSA 73:3–73:8; ISA 28:14–28:15

Lack of wisdom

PRO 29:9

God scoffs at the nations

PSA 59:5–59:8 See also PSA 2:1–2:6

title: 8820: self-confidence
content:
A positive assessment of one's own abilities and resources. Scripture censures excessive self-confidence, in that such an attitude lacks humility and fails to recognise the role of God's grace in the Christian life.

Excessive self-confidence

In one's own abilities

ISA 28:15; MAT 26:33–26:35 parallels MRK 14:29–14:31, LUK 23:33–23:34, JHN 13:37–13:38 See also LUK 22:33–22:34; JDG 16:20; 1KI 20:11; 2KI 19:23–19:24; JOB 8:13–8:14; PSA 49:5–49:6; JER 17:5; HOS 12:8

Excessive self-confidence leads to pride

ISA 9:9–9:10; OBA 1:3 See also GEN 11:4, GEN 37:5; EXO 15:9; 2CH 26:16; PRO 16:18; ISA 16:6; EZK 28:2; ACT 8:9; ROM 11:17–11:18; 1CO 5:2; 1JN 2:16

Challenges to excessive self-confidence

NEH 6:16; 1CO 4:7 See also PSA 49:12–49:13, PSA 52:7; PRO 3:5–3:7, PRO 11:28, PRO 28:26; ISA 5:21, ISA 14:13–14:15; JER 49:7, JER 49:4–49:5; JAS 4:13–4:16

Excessive self-confidence is a barrier to justification

LUK 18:9–18:14

Accurate self-confidence

Of one's natural advantages

PHP 3:4–3:6 See also ACT 22:3, ACT 22:28

Of one's experience of God

2CO 12:2 See also ACT 22:4–22:21; 2CO 12:1, 2CO 13:5–13:6; GAL 1:13–1:17, GAL 6:4

Of one's calling to serve

2CO 10:8 See also 2CO 10:13–10:17; GAL 2:7

Of one's service

ACT 20:19; ROM 12:3 See also ACT 20:18, ACT 20:20–20:21; 1CO 9:15–9:18; 2CO 1:12; PHP 2:16; 1TH 2:1–2:12

Of one's own weakness

2CO 11:29–11:30 See also 2CO 11:21–11:28, 2CO 12:9

Accurate self-estimates lead to justification

LUK 18:9–18:14

Justified self-confidence may appear as pride

2CO 11:17–11:18

Jesus Christ's accurate assessment of himself

MAT 16:15–16:17 parallels MRK 8:29, LUK 9:20–9:21 See also MAT 26:62–26:64; JHN 13:13

The proper source of all confidence

JER 9:23–9:24 See also PSA 34:2, PSA 44:6–44:7; ISA 10:15; 1CO 1:27–1:31

title: 8821: self-indulgence
content:
Throwing off restraint and discipline and yielding to the desire to gratify selfish appetites and cravings. Scripture warns against such a characteristic and urges, instead, self-control, generosity and consideration for others.

The desire to satisfy selfish cravings

EPH 2:3 See also ROM 7:8, ROM 16:18; TIT 3:3; JAS 1:14; 2PE 2:18–2:19; 1JN 2:16

Examples of self-indulgent desires

Selfish ambition

JAS 3:14–3:16 See also PRO 18:1; GAL 5:20; PHP 1:17

The desire for one's own way

ISA 56:11–56:12 See also DEU 29:19; EST 1:10–1:12; JAS 4:1–4:3

The desire for sexual gratification

GAL 5:19 See also GEN 19:5NUM 25:1; 1CO 10:8 2SA 11:2–11:4 David's adultery with Bathsheba; 2SA 13:11–13:14 Amnon's rape of Tamar; PRO 7:16–7:18 the lure of the adulteress; 2CO 12:21 sexual sin in the church at Corinth; 2PE 2:14 sexual desires of false teachers

The desire for wealth

JAS 5:3–5:5 See also JOS 7:21 Achan; 1SA 8:3 Samuel's sons; JER 22:17 Jehoiakim, king of Judah; HAG 1:4 the people of Judah; TIT 1:11 false teachers in Crete

Indulgence in food and drink

ISA 22:13 See also PRO 23:20; ECC 6:7

Abandoning restraint

EPH 4:19 See also ROM 1:26–1:31; 2TI 3:1–3:4; JUD 1:7

The consequences of self-indulgence

Self-indulgence proves futile

ECC 2:1–2:11 See also LUK 12:18–12:21

Self-indulgence leads to ruin

PRO 21:17 See also PRO 6:26, PRO 23:21, PRO 23:29–23:32; LUK 15:13–15:16; 1TI 5:6

Self-indulgence brings God's judgment

ROM 2:8 See also PRO 5:20–5:21; PHP 3:19; DAN 4:29–4:32 God's judgment on Nebuchadnezzar's selfish pride; AMO 4:1–4:2 God's judgment on Israel's pampered upper-class women; AMO 6:4–6:7 God's judgment on Israel's self-indulgent nobility; LUK 12:19–12:20

Dealing with self-indulgence

Receiving new life through Jesus Christ

MAT 23:25 Dealing with self-indulgence requires an inner transformation. See also ROM 12:2; COL 2:21–2:23ROM 13:14 See also GAL 5:24; TIT 2:11–2:12ROM 8:5; GAL 5:16

Seeking God's will

PSA 119:36; ; 1PE 1:14, 1PE 4:2

Self-control

1TH 4:3–4:5 See also PRO 23:4; 1CO 9:25–9:27; 1PE 4:7; 2PE 1:6

Ruthless self-denial

COL 3:5 See also DAN 1:8; MAT 5:28–5:29; 1PE 2:11

Consideration for others

GAL 5:13 See also 1CO 10:23–10:24; PHP 2:3–2:4

Generosity

DEU 15:7–15:8; ; LUK 19:8

title: 8822: self-justification
content:
A self-centred attitude by which people defend their actions and beliefs without reference to God. Scripture insists that the confidence and ultimate justification of believers lie with God, and condemns those who look elsewhere for these.

The impossibility of self-justification

Self-justification is impossible before a holy God

JOB 25:4 See also 1SA 6:20; MAL 3:2; REV 6:17

Justification is achieved by God, not by people

ROM 5:1–5:2 See also ROM 3:27–3:30; GAL 2:20–2:21

How self-justification occurs

Self-justification occurs through ignoring God and his ways

NEH 9:16 See also LUK 16:14–16:15

Self-justification occurs through pride

LUK 18:9–18:14 See also MAT 23:1–23:7 parallels MRK 12:38–12:39, LUK 20:45–20:46; ROM 2:17–2:27

Self-justification occurs through legalism

LUK 10:25–10:29 See also GAL 3:1–3:5, GAL 5:4

Self-justification causes separation from God and Jesus Christ

GAL 5:4 See also MAT 18:21–18:35; LUK 18:9–18:14

Examples of self-justification

GEN 3:8–3:12 Adam; ; EXO 32:19–32:24 Aaron; ; 1SA 13:7–13:14 Saul; ; MAT 19:16–19:22 parallels MRK 10:17–10:22, LUK 18:18–18:23 the rich young man; ; PHP 3:4–3:9 Paul as a Pharisee

God's attitude to self-justification

God's condemnation of self-justification

ROM 2:1–2:11

God's punishment of self-justification

PRO 29:1 See also GEN 3:8–3:19; JER 6:19–6:23

The true basis of justification

People are justified by God's grace alone

EPH 2:8–2:9 See also ROM 3:21–3:24; TIT 2:11, TIT 3:4–3:7

God accepts those who trust in his mercy without trying to justify themselves

PSA 130:3–130:4 See also PSA 143:2; LUK 18:9–18:14

title: 8823: self-righteousness
content: A moral self-confidence and superiority arising from satisfaction in one's own achievements. True righteousness can only be found in a relationship with Jesus Christ.

title: 8824: self-righteousness, nature of
content:
Self-righteousness fosters the sinful human illusions of sinlessness, sufficiency and freedom.

The claim to self-righteousness

ROM 10:3 See also LUK 10:29, LUK 18:9; PHP 3:4–3:6

The illusion of self-righteousness

That people are sinless

1JN 1:8 See also PRO 20:9; HOS 12:8

That people are guiltless

PRO 16:2 See also JER 2:34–2:35

That people are deserving

DEU 9:4 See also EZK 28:2

The results of self-righteousness

Self-deception

1JN 1:5–1:6 See also PRO 30:12; JER 17:9; MAT 23:23–23:24, MAT 23:27–23:28; LUK 16:15; HEB 3:13

A sense of superiority

LUK 18:9–18:11 See also PHP 2:3; COL 2:16–2:18

Separation from God

1JN 1:10 See also ZEP 3:11; 2CO 10:18; GAL 5:4

Examples of self-righteousness

NUM 16:3 some Israelites opposed to Moses; ; 1SA 15:13–15:21 Saul; ; PSA 10:5 the wicked; LUK 16:14, LUK 18:9–18:14; ; JHN 9:39–9:41; REV 3:17–3:18 the church at Laodicea

title: 8825: self-righteousness, and the gospel
content:
Self-righteousness is an obstacle to the gospel, which insists that true righteousness can only be found in Jesus Christ.

The real issue of righteousness

JOB 9:2 See also 1SA 6:20; JOB 4:17, JOB 15:14, JOB 32:2 Although Elihu had misjudged Job, his main point, that only God was righteous, was correct; JOB 40:8; PSA 130:3

True righteousness is not the result of human effort

ROM 3:20 Even though God's law tells people what God requires, human beings cannot keep it because of the weakness of their sinful human natures. See also ROM 9:31; GAL 2:16, GAL 3:11; EPH 2:8–2:9; TIT 3:5; 1JN 2:16

Self-righteousness is a contradiction in terms

2CH 6:36; ISA 64:6 See also EZR 9:15; PSA 14:3; ECC 7:20; DAN 9:7; ROM 3:10, ROM 3:23

God calls people from their pretended self-righteousness

ISA 2:22 See also PSA 75:2–75:4; JER 17:5; MAT 5:20

True righteouness

It comes from God

ROM 10:3 See also PSA 98:2; ISA 46:13, ISA 51:5; JER 9:23–9:24; ROM 1:17

It is grounded in Jesus Christ

ACT 13:39 See also 1CO 1:30; 2CO 5:21

It comes about by faith

ROM 5:1 See also GAL 5:5; EPH 2:8

It is received in humility

LUK 18:13–18:14 See also ROM 3:27, ROM 4:2; 1CO 1:31, 1CO 4:7; 2CO 11:30, 2CO 12:9; GAL 6:13–6:14; EPH 2:9; PHP 3:7–3:9

title: 8827: selfishness
content:
A self-centred concern for oneself, without due regard to the needs of others. Scripture treats selfishness as an aspect of sin and urges believers to care for others as well as themselves.

Selfishness is a characteristic of the sinner

ROM 8:5; 2CO 5:15 See also PRO 18:1; ROM 2:8; EPH 2:3

Selfishness is a characteristic of sinful society

2TI 3:1–3:2 See also JDG 17:6, JDG 21:25

Expressions of selfishness

Greed

MAT 23:25 See also MRK 12:7; LUK 12:13–12:21; ACT 5:3

Ambition

PHP 2:3 See also JER 45:5; GAL 5:19–5:20; PHP 1:17; JAS 3:14–3:16

Boastfulness

DAN 4:30

Examples of selfishness

See also GEN 11:4 the builders of the tower of Babel; GEN 13:10–13:11 Lot in his choice of territory; EZK 28:2–28:5 the king of Tyre; EZK 34:8 Israel's leaders; MRK 10:35 James and John

Self-absorption as the result of pain or depression

JOB 14:22; 1KI 19:10

Antidotes to selfishness

God's word

PSA 119:36

The example of Jesus Christ

ROM 15:3 See also PHP 2:4–2:8

Dying to the old nature

ROM 6:6 See also EPH 4:22; COL 3:9

Serving one another

1PE 4:10 See also 1CO 10:24

Loving one another

JHN 13:34 See also MAT 22:39; ROM 13:8–13:10

title: 8828: spite
content:
The malicious desire to retaliate in words or action. It may be in response to good or evil. Believers are to rid themselves of any such vindictive spirit.

Examples of people acting out of spite

In response to good

1KI 19:1–19:2 Jezebel; ; 2CH 16:10 Asa, king of Judah; ; EST 3:6 Haman; ; MAT 14:3–14:12 parallel MRK 6:17–6:29 Herodias; ; JHN 12:10 the chief priests; ACT 7:54, ACT 7:57–7:58

In response to evil

PSA 140:3 See also GEN 27:41 EsauGEN 37:4, GEN 37:8, GEN 37:11, GEN 37:18–37:27 EZK 25:15 the Philistines; ACT 23:12–23:15 some Jews

Spite has no place in the lives of believers

Believers are to rid themselves of all spitefulness

EPH 4:31 See also 1CO 5:8; COL 3:8; 1PE 2:1

As a result believers are enabled not to retaliate against others

LEV 19:18 See also PRO 20:22, PRO 24:29; MAT 5:38–5:40; ROM 12:17, ROM 12:19–12:21; 1TH 5:15; 1PE 2:21–2:23, 1PE 3:9

title: 8829: superstition
content:
Misplaced credulity concerning the supernatural, which leads to irrational fear, misdirected reverence, false religion and magic, and which brings God's judgment. Scripture warns against and condemns such things.

Superstition causing irrational fear

JER 10:2 See also JOB 15:20–15:24, JOB 18:11

Fear of Jesus Christ or his disciples

MAT 14:26–14:27 parallel MRK 6:49–6:50 See also MAT 14:2 parallel MRK 6:14; ACT 5:13

Fear of other gods

1KI 20:23 See also 1KI 18:28, 1KI 20:28; ACT 17:23

Misunderstanding God's work

ACT 8:18–8:19 See also LUK 24:36–24:37; ACT 12:15, ACT 19:13 invoking the name of Jesus Christ for exorcism as though it were a magic formula; ACT 28:3–28:4

Superstition leading to misdirected reverence

ACT 14:11–14:13 See also ACT 28:5–28:6; REV 22:8–22:9

False religion

JDG 10:6–10:7 See also 1SA 7:3–7:4; 1KI 13:33, 1KI 14:15–14:16, 1KI 14:22–14:24; 2CH 28:2–28:4 parallel 2KI 16:3–16:4; JER 9:14, JER 44:17–44:18; HOS 11:2

Unhelpful speculations

1TI 1:3–1:4 See also ISA 65:2–65:3, ISA 66:17–66:18; EZK 13:2, EZK 13:17; 1TI 6:3–6:4

The true demonic source of superstition

1TI 4:1 See also REV 9:20–9:21

title: 8830: suspicion
content:
The belief that people or things are not as they appear. It may be based on evidence, but it can also be ill-founded, occasioned by jealousy or malicious gossip.

Suspicion of sexual impurity

DEU 22:13–22:19 See also NUM 5:11–5:31

Suspicion of drunkenness

1SA 1:9–1:18 See also ACT 2:13–2:15

Suspicion of espionage

2SA 10:1–10:5

Suspicion of treachery

1SA 18:6–18:9 See also EXO 1:9–1:10; 1SA 20:24–20:31, 1SA 21:10–21:12, 1SA 29:1–29:11

Lack of suspicion

2SA 15:7–15:12 See also 1SA 27:1–27:12; 2SA 13:1–13:11, 2SA 13:23–13:29

Evil suspicions

1TI 6:3–6:5

title: 8831: syncretism
content:
The incorporation into religious faith and practice of elements from other religions, resulting in a loss of integrity and assimilation to the surrounding culture.

Syncretism in Israel

God's claim to exclusive worship, the basis of the rejection of syncretism

EXO 20:3 parallel DEU 5:7 See also DEU 6:13–6:15; JOS 24:14–24:15; 1KI 18:21

Syncretism forbidden to Israel

EXO 34:15–34:16 See also DEU 7:1–7:6; JOS 23:16; 1SA 7:3

Israelite practice of syncretism

JER 19:4–19:5 See also 2KI 17:34–17:41, 2KI 21:1–21:7 parallel 2CH 33:1–33:7; EZK 8:9–8:16

The consequence of syncretism

JER 2:5 See also DEU 18:9–18:13; 2KI 17:15–17:17; ISA 2:6

Punishment for syncretism

ZEP 1:4–1:5 See also DEU 17:2–17:7; JER 19:10–19:13; HOS 2:2–2:13

Syncretism in NT times

Mediterranean society was syncretistic

ACT 14:11–14:13, ACT 17:16–17:23, ACT 19:13–19:16

NT opposition to syncretism

HEB 13:9 See also 1CO 10:21; GAL 4:9–4:10; COL 2:18

Monotheism is incompatible with syncretism

ISA 44:6 See also DEU 6:4–6:5; ISA 43:10–43:12; 1CO 8:4–8:6

title: 8832: testing
content:
God allows his people to pass through certain experiences, so that he may see, and prove to them, that their faith in him is genuine. Believers sometimes doubt God and test him, to see if he is true to his word, but this is forbidden in Scripture.

God tests his people

JAS 1:2–1:3; 1PE 1:7 See also JOB 7:17–7:18, JOB 23:10; PSA 11:5; ISA 1:25; ZEC 13:9; MAL 3:3; JAS 1:12

Examples of God testing his people collectively

EXO 16:4; DEU 8:2–8:3 See also EXO 20:20 at the giving of the law; DEU 8:16 over the gathering of manna; DEU 13:3–13:4 by their attitude to a false prophet; JDG 2:20–3:4 by leaving nations in the promised land

Examples of God testing his people individually

GEN 22:1–22:2 See also JDG 7:4–7:7 Gideon; 2CH 32:31 Hezekiah; 2CO 12:7–12:9 Paul

Jesus Christ tested the faith of people when he was on earth

JHN 6:5–6:6 See also MAT 15:22–15:28 parallel MRK 7:25–7:30 a Canaanite woman; MRK 8:17–8:21 his disciples

Believers have a responsibility to test the quality of their lives

ROM 12:2 See also PSA 17:3PSA 26:2, PSA 139:23 LAM 3:40; 2CO 13:5; GAL 6:4; 1TH 5:21

God will make a final test of believers' lives and service

1CO 3:12–3:15

People may test God as an expression of faith and obedience

MAL 3:10 See also JDG 6:39

People must not test God as an expression of doubt and disobedience

EXO 17:2 See also EXO 17:7; NUM 14:22–14:23; DEU 6:16, DEU 33:8; PSA 78:18, PSA 78:41, PSA 78:56, PSA 95:8; MAT 4:7 parallel LUK 4:12; DEU 6:16; MAT 19:3 parallel MRK 10:2; ACT 5:9, ACT 15:10; HEB 3:8–3:9

The command to test the spirits

1JN 4:1

title: 8833: threats
content:
Intimidating announcements of action to be taken unless conditions are met. God uses threats against tyrannical and disobedient earthly rulers as a means of restoring them to obedience and humility in his sight. God's people are not to threaten others and though the wicked will sometimes seek to intimidate them, they are to rely on God's protection.

God threatened Pharaoh

See also EXO 8:1–8:4, EXO 8:21, EXO 9:2–9:3, EXO 9:13–9:14, EXO 10:3–10:6

God threatened his own people

In general

JOS 23:15–23:16 See also LEV 26:14–26:20; DEU 11:26–11:28, DEU 28:15–28:20; 1SA 12:15, 1SA 12:25; 1KI 9:6–9:7

Regarding the Babylonian captivity

EZK 6:9–6:10 See also JER 6:8, JER 22:5–22:7, JER 44:28–44:29

Threats made by God may be averted

Through a faithful intercessor

EXO 32:11–32:14 See also NEH 1:8–1:9

Through turning from evil

JON 3:10

The result of threats inflicted by God may be alleviated

Through returning to the LORD

DEU 30:1–30:3

Through submission to God's will

See also JER 27:6–27:13

God's people may be threatened by others

ACT 9:1 See also 2KI 18:17–18:35 parallel ISA 36:1–36:20; NEH 4:7–4:8; PSA 55:9–55:11, PSA 73:8

God's people, when threatened, are to rely on him

PSA 64:1–64:10 See also 2KI 19:6–19:7 parallel ISA 37:6–37:7; NEH 6:11–6:14; ISA 30:17–30:18; ACT 4:17–4:21, ACT 4:29–4:30

God's people are not to threaten others

EPH 6:9 See also 1PE 2:20–2:23

The rich are more likely to be threatened than the poor

PRO 13:8

title: 8834: unbelief
content: The lack of faith and trust in God that challenges his truthfulness and finds expression in disobedience and rebellion.

title: 8835: unbelief, nature and effects of
content:
Unbelief, or the failure to trust God, holds back his blessing and leads to condemnation and spiritual death.

The nature of unbelief

Not trusting God

PSA 78:22

Rebelling against God

HEB 3:12 See also PSA 78:40; HEB 3:16

Disobeying God

HEB 11:31 NIV footnote. See also EPH 2:2; HEB 3:18–3:19, HEB 4:11

Questioning God's truthfulness

1JN 5:10 See also PSA 106:24; 1JN 1:10

Unbelief as the result of the devil's work

Taking away God's word

LUK 8:12 parallels MAT 13:19, MRK 4:15

Causing spiritual blindness

2CO 4:4 See also ROM 1:21; 2CO 4:3; EPH 4:18

Unbelief as the result of not belonging to God

JHN 10:26 See also JHN 5:38, JHN 8:44–8:45, JHN 12:37–12:40; 1CO 2:14

Unbelief hinders Jesus Christ's miracles

MAT 13:58 parallel MRK 6:5–6:6

The consequences of persistent unbelief

Failure to receive God's reward

HEB 3:19 The “rest” that God's people enjoyed on entering the promised land is here taken to symbolise the final reward prepared by God for his people. See also HEB 4:1–4:2, HEB 4:6; JUD 1:5

Exclusion from the people of God

ROM 11:20 See also HEB 6:4–6:6

Death in sin

JHN 8:24 See also PSA 106:43; MRK 4:12; ACT 10:43

God's wrath

title: 8836: unbelief, as response to God
content:
The stubborn and sinful refusal to accept God's word and his messengers. Since the coming of Jesus Christ it is frequently expressed in the rejection of his person and teaching.

title: 8839: unfaithfulness
content: The failure to fulfil the obligations of a relationship, resulting in disloyalty to God and to others.

title: 8840: unfaithfulness, to God
content:
In the OT the terms of the covenant with God were constantly broken by Israel by acts of idolatry and disobedience. The consequence was God's judgment, which eventually included exile.

Warnings within the covenant

NEH 1:8; ; LEV 26:1, LEV 26:14–26:17, LEV 26:31–26:33; ; DEU 4:25–4:27, DEU 8:19–8:20; ; PRO 2:22; ; EZK 14:13, EZK 15:8

Unfaithfulness seen in idolatry

Idolatry as marital unfaithfulness

JER 3:20 The covenant between God and Israel at Sinai viewed in terms of a marriage contract; JER 3:6–3:9 See also JER 3:12–3:14, JER 9:2, JER 31:32; HOS 1:2

Idolatry as prostitution

1CH 5:25; ; HOS 4:10–4:12, HOS 9:1

Idolatry as abandoning God

JER 1:16 See also JDG 10:13; JER 5:19, JER 15:6

Trust in money and possessions

JOB 31:24–31:28 See also JER 49:4

Doing wrong to others

NUM 5:5–5:6 See also LEV 6:2; PRO 11:3, PRO 13:2; ISA 1:21–1:23; HOS 6:6–6:7

Marrying foreign wives

EZR 10:2 See also EZR 9:1–9:4; NEH 13:27

Withholding tithes and offerings

JOS 7:1, JOS 22:20; ; MAL 3:8

1SA 14:33; ; MAL 1:7–1:8

JER 5:11 See also ACT 7:37–7:41; JDG 2:16–2:17; NEH 9:26; HAG 1:7–1:9

Unfaithfulness among Israel's leadership

The unfaithfulness of the priesthood

EZR 9:1–9:2 See also 2CH 36:14; EZK 22:26; MAL 2:7–2:8

Unfaithful kings

Solomon's unfaithfulness leads to unfaithfulness among his subjects: 1KI 11:4–11:5, 1KI 11:33; 2CH 12:1–12:2 Rehoboam; ; 2CH 26:16–26:18 Uzziah's bad example; 2CH 28:19–28:23, 2CH 29:19; 2KI 21:9 parallel 2CH 33:9; ; 2KI 21:16; ; 2CH 33:19

Unfaithfulness leads to judgment

DEU 32:20; ; PSA 73:27, PSA 78:56–78:59; ; PRO 21:18

JOS 7:1, JOS 7:25; ; 1CH 10:13

content:
A breach of the trust that is expected within specific relationships, and also a failure of mutual responsibility within a community life; the breaking of the last six of the Ten Commandments.

MAL 2:14–2:15

title: 8843: unforgivable sin
content:
The wilful, outwardly expressed and impenitent slander against the Holy Spirit, when Jesus Christ's mighty works, clearly performed by the power of the Holy Spirit, are attributed to Satan, thus subjecting Christ to public disgrace.

The unforgivable sin is slandering the Holy Spirit

MAT 12:31–12:32 parallel MRK 3:28–3:29 See also LUK 12:10; HEB 10:26–10:29

The unforgivable sin is attributing Jesus Christ's miracles to Satan

MRK 3:30 See also MAT 12:24 parallels MRK 3:22, LUK 11:15

title: 8844: unforgiveness
content:
God remains unforgiving to those described as unrepentant, who blaspheme against the Holy Spirit and who are themselves unforgiving. Being unforgiving and demonstrating true love are mutually exclusive.

Towards the unrepentant

DEU 29:18–29:21 See also EXO 23:21, EXO 34:7; NUM 14:18; JOS 24:19; 2KI 24:4; ISA 30:12–30:14; JER 5:7; LAM 3:42; HOS 1:6; LUK 18:10–18:14; HEB 10:28–10:31

MAT 12:31–12:32 parallels MRK 3:28–3:29, LUK 12:10 Blasphemy against the Spirit probably involves attributing the authenticating miracles of Jesus Christ to the work of Satan rather than to the power of the Holy Spirit. See also 1JN 5:16

title: 8846: ungodliness
content:
The state of believing in God, while adopting a lifestyle which seems to deny this. Believers are warned to guard against ungodliness.

A defiant spirit towards God

MAT 7:6 Jesus Christ is teaching his disciples not to share the riches of spiritual truth with persons who are persistently unappreciative, vicious and defiant. See also JOB 36:8–36:13; PSA 73:8–73:11

Mocking God and/or his people

2PE 3:3–3:4 See also PSA 35:15–35:16; ACT 13:40–13:41; HAB 1:5

Evil behaviour

ISA 32:6–32:7 See also PRO 11:9; JON 1:1–1:2; 1TI 1:9–1:11

2CH 36:15–36:16 the southern kingdom of Judah; ; PSA 52:1–52:3 Doeg the Edomite; ; ISA 9:13–9:17 the northern kingdom of Israel; JER 23:11–23:12, JER 23:15–23:17; 1CO 6:9–6:11; ; EPH 2:1–2:3; 2TI 3:1–3:5 people in general during the last days (the time between the first and second comings of Jesus Christ); ; HEB 12:16 Esau

In this life

title: 8848: worldliness
content:
The sinful tendency to conform to the world, to be contrasted with the biblical command to maintain contact with the world while avoiding becoming like the world. Believers are called to live in the world, while not being of the world. This attitude is supremely exemplified in the ministry of Jesus Christ.

The paradox of God's love for a sinful world

JHN 3:16; ; 1JN 2:15–2:16

God's people are called to be separate from the world, yet a source of blessing to it

The example of Abraham

GEN 12:1–12:3 The life of Abraham illustrates the important biblical balance, called to separation from his native environment to be a blessing to the nations. See also GEN 15:7, GEN 18:18; GAL 3:8

The example of others

GEN 41:56–41:57 Joseph; ; DAN 2:48–2:49 Daniel and his friends

Conformity to the pagan standards of the OT world disparaged

LEV 18:28 with respect to sexual perversion; 1SA 8:5; ; 1KI 21:7; 1KI 11:7–11:8 with respect to idolatry; ; ISA 13:19 with respect to pride; ISA 31:1; ; ZEC 4:6

God's concern for the nations of the world

ISA 49:6 See also JON 4:11; REV 22:2

1CO 5:9–5:10 See also JHN 17:11

title: 8849: worry
content:
A sense of uneasiness and anxiety about the future. Scripture indicates that such anxiety is ultimately grounded in a lack of trust in God and his purposes.

Being world-centred

MAT 6:25 parallel LUK 12:22 See also MAT 6:34, MAT 13:22 parallels MRK 4:19, LUK 8:14; LUK 12:29, LUK 21:34; 1CO 7:33

Lacking confidence in God

JHN 14:1 See also MAT 6:26–6:32 parallel LUK 12:27–12:30; MAT 8:25 parallels MRK 4:38, LUK 8:24; MAT 14:31, MAT 16:8

Abandoning God

DEU 28:64–28:65 See also LAM 1:3; EZK 4:16–4:17, EZK 12:19

PSA 37:8 See also PRO 12:25; MAT 13:22 parallel LUK 8:14; LUK 10:40–10:42

Worry is futile

MAT 6:27 parallel LUK 12:25 See also ECC 2:22–2:23
